kineticist.name: Eternal Torch
kineticist.text: You open a connection to your kinetic gate, large enough for a torch flame to flow. You create a magical, torch-like flame within 120 feet in any color you choose. It's as bright and hot as a torch. You can have it orbit a target willing creature or emit from a target object that's unattended or attended by a willing creature. If you create a flame on a weapon, you still need to use it as an improvised weapon to atta

magus.name: Familiar
magus.text: Magus, Sorcerer An animal serves you and assists your spellcasting. Wizard You make a pact with a creature that serves you and assists your spellcasting. Thaumaturge Whether by following occult rituals, piecing together scraps of arcane theory, or some other method, you've called forth a creature that now serves as your constant companion in your studies of the supernatural. You gain a familiar.

magus.name: Raise a Tome
magus.text: You can flip open a book to simultaneously study and deflect attacks. When you Raise a Shield, you can raise a book you're wielding instead of a shield. While you have a book raised, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and a +1 circumstance bonus to Recall Knowledge checks to identify creatures using a skill related to the subject of the book (Arcana if you're using your spellbook). If consulting the book normally

magus.name: Magus's Analysis
magus.text: You make an assessment informed by your knowledge of how a creature fights. Attempt a check to Recall Knowledge about a creature, then recharge your Spellstrike. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check if you previously hit the creature with a Strike this turn. The subject of your check is temporarily immune to Magus's Analysis for 1 day.

magus.name: Arcane Fists
magus.text: Your physical training encompasses unarmed combat forms. The damage die for your fist changes to 1d6 instead of 1d4. You don't take the normal –2 circumstance penalty when making a lethal attack with your fist or any other unarmed attacks. Your unarmed attacks gain the arcane trait, making them magical. At 5th level, you also gain the critical specialization effects of unarmed attacks in the brawling group and weapon

monk.name: Wolf Stance
monk.text: Requirements You are unarmored You enter the stance of a wolf, low to the ground with your hands held like fangs. You can make wolf jaw unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 piercing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the agile, backstabber, finesse, nonlethal, and unarmed traits. If you're flanking a target while in Wolf Stance, your wolf jaw unarmed attacks also gain the trip trait.

monk.name: Dragon Stance
monk.text: Requirements You are unarmored You enter the stance of a dragon and make powerful leg strikes like a lashing dragon's tail. You can make dragon tail attacks that deal 1d10 bludgeoning damage. They are in the brawling group and have the backswing, nonlethal, and unarmed traits. While in Dragon Stance, you can ignore the first square of difficult terrain while Striding.

monk.name: Monastic Weaponry
monk.text: You have trained with the weaponry of your monastery or school. You gain access to uncommon weapons with the monk trait and become trained in simple and martial monk weapons. When your proficiency for unarmed attacks increases to expert or master, your proficiency rank for these weapons increases to expert or master as well. If you have familiarity with an agile or finesse weapon (such as from the Catfolk Weapon Fami

monk.name: Monastic Archer Stance
monk.text: Requirements You are unarmored and wielding a longbow, shortbow, or a bow with the monk trait. You enter a specialized stance for a unique martial art centered around the use of a bow. While in this stance, the only Strikes you can make are those using longbows, shortbows, or bows with the monk trait. You can use Flurry of Blows with these bows. You can use your other monk feats or monk abilities that normally requir

monk.name: Qi Spells
monk.text: You have cultivated your qi to produce magical effects. You gain Inner Upheaval, Qi Rush, or another 1st-rank monk qi spell you have access to. Special You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different spell each time.

monk.name: Stumbling Stance
monk.text: You enter a seemingly unfocused stance that mimics the movements of the inebriated-bobbing, weaving, leaving false openings, and distracting your enemies from your true movements. While in this stance, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Deception checks to Feint. The only Strikes you can make are stumbling swing unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 bludgeoning damage; are in the brawling group; and have the agile, backst

monk.name: Twisting Petal Stance
monk.text: Requirements You're unarmored. Your body moves like a petal twisting on the wind, confounding your opponents while using their energy against them. You can make gale blossom strikes that deal 1d6 slashing damage. These strikes are in the brawling group and have the agile, finesse, nonlethal, shove, and unarmed traits. While in Twisting Petal Stance, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks to Shove and a

monk.name: Mountain Stance
monk.text: Requirements You are unarmored and touching the ground You enter the stance of an implacable mountain—a technique created by dwarven monks—allowing you to strike with the weight of an avalanche and block blows with your garments. The only Strikes you can make are falling stone unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8[bludgeoning] damage; are in the brawling group; and have the forceful, nonlethal, and unarmed traits. While in

monk.name: Tiger Stance
monk.text: Requirements You are unarmored You enter the stance of a tiger and can make tiger claw attacks. These deal 1d8 slashing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the agile, finesse, nonlethal, and unarmed traits. On a critical success with your tiger claws, if you deal damage, the target takes 1d4 persistent bleed damage. As long as your Speed is at least 20 feet while in Tiger Stance, you can Step 10 feet.

monk.name: Reflective Ripple Stance
monk.text: Requirements You're unarmored. You enter a stance of fluid grace as small amounts of water flow with your movements and attacks. You can make flowing wave attacks that deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage. They are in the brawling group and have the agile, disarm, finesse, nonlethal, trip, unarmed, and water traits. While in Reflective Ripple Stance, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks to Disarm, Swim, or Tri

monk.name: Rushing Goat Stance
monk.text: Requirements You're unarmored. You enter the stance of an unruly goat, lowering your body and preparing to butt heads with your foes. The only Strikes you can make are ramming horn attacks. These strikes deal 1d8 bludgeoning damage, are in the brawling group, and have the forceful, nonlethal, shove, and unarmed traits. When you make a ramming horn attack and your previous action was to Climb, Stride, or Leap, you gai

monk.name: Crane Stance
monk.text: Requirements You are unarmored Your arms flutter like a crane's wings. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC, but the only Strikes you can make are crane wing attacks. These deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage; are in the brawling group; and have the agile, finesse, nonlethal, and unarmed traits. While in Crane Stance, reduce the DC for High Jump and Long Jump by 5, and when you Leap, you can move an additional 5 feet horiz

necromancer.name: Death Speaker
necromancer.text: Your voice and magic speak to the core existence within undead creatures, circumventing the need for the creature to comprehend. Your spells and abilities ignore the mindless trait and any immunity to emotion, fear, or mental effects when targeting or affecting undead creatures. Additionally, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus when you attempt to [[/act make-an-impression]] on and make a [[/act request]] of an undead c

necromancer.name: Undead Familiar
necromancer.text: You gain the ability to raise an undead familiar who will serve you as your loyal and sometimes expendable partner as you explore your necromantic magic. You gain a familiar. It has the undead trait instead of the animal trait and is immune to bleed, death effects, disease, mental, and poison. necromancer.name: Widespread Fascination
necromancer.text: You are not content to restrict yourself to one field. Instead, you've studied a wider range of necromantic magic to better expand your horizons and explore your unscrupulous fascinations. You learn the grave spell for a Grim Fascination other than yours. You must have access to that fascination. Access can be gained from independent study or sought-out tutelage. Special You can select this feat more than once, choos

necromancer.name: Reach of the Dead
necromancer.text: You channel your necrotic magic through a thrall, expending it in the process. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that has range, you cast that spell from one of your thralls within 60 feet. That thrall becomes the point of origin for your spell; calculate range and cover from its space instead of yours. The thrall is then destroyed.

necromancer.name: The Hallowed Dead
necromancer.text: While many necromancers seek unholy and perverse power, you have dedicated yourself to the practice of necromancy to stop the creation of permanent undead and the corruption of souls. You and your thralls gain the holy trait. Strikes your thralls make gain the holy trait and deal 1 additional spirit damage. This additional spirit damage increases to 2 at 10th level. You also gain the following anathema: "purposefully

oracle.name: Widen Spell
oracle.text: You manipulate the energy of your spell, causing it to spread out and affect a wider area. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that has an area of a burst, cone, or line and does not have a duration, increase the area of that spell. oracle.name: Whispers of Weakness
oracle.text: Voices whisper to you how to best lay a creature low. You target one creature within 60 feet; if it has any weaknesses, you learn them, as well as which of its saving throw modifiers is lowest. You also come to understand its movements, gaining a +2 status bonus to your next attack roll (or skill check made as part of an attack action) against that foe before the end of your turn. oracle.name: Oracular Warning
oracle.text: Trigger You are about to roll initiative. You have a premonition about impending danger that you use to warn your allies. oracle.text: You tap into the collected lore of the divine, accessing a variety of potentially useful information. Attempt a religion check to understand the information you gain. psychic.name: Mental Buffer
psychic.text: Your mind deflects some amount of harm from attacks that induce pain or manipulate your mind directly. You gain resistance to mental damage equal to half your level (minimum 1). This resistance increases to equal to your level while your Psyche is Unleashed.

psychic.name: Ancestral Mind
psychic.text: By unraveling memories and connections passed down from your progenitors and buried within your unconscious mind, you learn to convert your inherent magic into psychic power. When a foe Casts a Spell that has the mental trait and you can see its manifestations, you can use your own mental magic to disrupt it. psychic.name: Psychic Rapport
psychic.text: Your telepathic sensitivity intensifies when you're affected by mental magic, making it easier for you to link to other creatures. After you Cast a Spell with the mental trait, until the start of your next turn, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, and Intimidation checks, and to Perception checks to Sense Motive. Effect: Psychic Rapport

ranger.name: Monster Hunter
ranger.text: You quickly assess your prey and apply what you know. As part of the action used to Hunt your Prey, you can attempt a check to Recall Knowledge about your prey. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll against that prey, and any ally you

ranger.text: You gain the service of a young animal companion that travels with you and obeys simple commands. When you Hunt Prey, your animal companion gains the action's benefits and your hunter's edge benefit if you have one.

ranger.name: Twin Takedown
ranger.text: Requirements You are wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand. You swiftly attack your hunted prey with each of your weapons, potentially combining their damage into a single devastating attack. ranger.name: Crossbow Ace
ranger.text: Requirements You are wielding a crossbow with reload 1 or higher. As normal, you must meet the requirements to Take Cover; you must be Prone, benefiting from cover, or near a feature that allows you to Take Cover.

ranger.name: Hunted Shot
ranger.text: Requirements You are wielding a ranged weapon with reload 0. You take two quick shots against the one you hunt. Make two Strikes against your hunted prey with the required weapon. If both hit the same creature, combine their damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. Apply your multiple attack penalty to each Strike normally.

ranger.name: Initiate Warden
ranger.text: You've trained with one of the ranger sects known as wardens, who practice a specialized type of primal magic. You gain your choice of one warden spell from these initial warden spells (or another you have access to). Gravity Weapon Heal Companion Magic Hide Special You can take this feat multiple times, choosing a different initial warden spell each time.

Even if you aren't Searching, you get a check to find traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap. rogue.name: Nimble Dodge
rogue.text: Trigger A creature targets you with an attack and you can see the attacker. Requirements You are not encumbered. You deftly dodge out of the way, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

rogue.text: You can put a single item you're holding of light or negligible Bulk onto a person without them noticing by succeeding at a thievery|defense:perception check against their Perception DC. rogue.name: Twin Feint
rogue.text: Requirements You are wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand. You use an attack with one weapon to distract your foe from a second attack coming at a different angle. Make one Strike with each of your two melee weapons, both against the same target. The target is automatically Off-Guard against the second attack. Apply your multiple attack penalty to the Strikes normally.

rogue.name: Overextending Feint

Critical Success The target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all attack rolls against you before the end of its next turn. rogue.name: Tumble Behind (Rogue)
rogue.text: You tumble under and behind your foe, your rapid movement letting you catch them off guard. When you successfully [[/act tumble-through]], the foe whose space you passed through is Off-Guard against the next attack you make before the end of your turn.

runesmith.name: Glyph Familiar
runesmith.text: You have taken a living rune as a familiar to aid you in your adventures. You gain a familiar. You choose one familiar or master ability per day instead of two, but your familiar also always has three additional familiar abilities: construct, flier, and tough.

runesmith.name: Seek the Hidden Glyphs
runesmith.text: You are well-versed in the use of magical runes in traps and hazards. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find magical traps. runesmith.name: Backup Runic Enhancement
runesmith.text: While you are not a spellcaster, you have a working knowledge of the most fundamental runic magic. You can cast the Sigil cantrip as an innate spell at will. You quickly sketch a rune in the air to gain a modicum of protection against the triggering magic. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your saving throw and AC against the spell.

You draw a rune onto the surface of your weapon in reverse, the mark branding or bruising itself into your target at the moment of impact. Make a melee strike with the weapon. On a success, you Trace a Rune onto the target of the Strike.

runesmith.name: Smithing Weapons
runesmith.text: Though you are an artisan, you are well versed in using the tools of your trade to fend off enemies. While wielding a weapon in the hammer, knife, or pick weapon group, you can use that weapon to etch runes without an Artisan's Toolkit. Additionally, a Strike with a hammer, knife, or pick deals 1 additional fire damage to an enemy bearing one of your runes as sparks fly on impact like a hammer to an anvil.

summoner.text: You can allow your eidolon to travel far from your side. You learn the Unfetter Eidolon link spell.

summoner.text: Your eidolon's heart beats with energy. Choose acid, cold, electricity, or fire. One of their unarmed attacks changes its damage type to the chosen type, and they gain resistance to that type equal to half your level (minimum 1).

summoner.name: Extend Boost
summoner.text: You can increase the duration of your eidolon's boosts. You learn the Extend Boost link spell.

summoner.name: Meld into Eidolon

options.name: Anger Phantom Eidolon
options.text: Your eidolon is a lost soul, bound to the mortal world by undying anger or a bitter grudge. Most phantom eidolons are humanoids with a spectral or ectoplasmic appearance, though some take far stranger forms. Your link with your eidolon prevents them from succumbing to corruption and undeath. Together, you will need to decide whether to work with your eidolon to control their anger or channel their wrath into power. T

options.name: Fey Eidolon
options.text: Your eidolon is a fey, a capricious being of the mysterious First World. Many fey appear similar to mortal humanoids, with unusual features such as pointed ears, wings, or bodies composed of natural elements, but the full variety of fey is endless, and many others appear completely inhuman. Fey from the First World never truly die, instead eventually forming into a new creature after being destroyed. Fey eidolons usu

options.name: Elemental Eidolon
options.text: Your eidolon is a primal chunk of elemental matter infused with sapience, power, and identity, but unable to manifest a true form of their own without the life force you provide via your connection. Most elementals in their natural environment already have different sorts of forms, from vaguely humanoid, to animalistic, to simple masses of their component element. As your life force provides your eidolon the instinct

options.name: Dragon Eidolon
options.text: Because dragons have a strong connection to magic, their minds can often leave an echo floating in the Astral Plane. Such an entity is extremely powerful but unable to interact with the outside world on their own. Dragon eidolons manifest in the powerful, scaled forms they had in life; most take the form of great dragons (albeit smaller), but some manifest as drakes or other draconic beings. You have forged a connect

options.name: Angel Eidolon
options.text: Your eidolon is a celestial messenger, a member of the angelic host with a unique link to you, allowing them to carry a special message to the mortal world at your side. Most angel eidolons are roughly humanoid in form, with feathered wings, glowing eyes, halos, or similar angelic features. However, some take the form of smaller angelic servitors like the winged helmet cassisian angel instead. The two of you are dest

options.name: Undead Eidolon
options.text: Your eidolon is an undead spirit pulled from the Ethereal Plane or the Void, embodied, and bound to your life force in an unusual, potentially antithetical way that even other summoners can't quite understand. Undead eidolons take about every imaginable shape and form, as their bodies manifest from their connection to you. Their ultimate form can be influenced by an amalgamation of the echoes and memories of their ol

options.name: Beast Eidolon
options.text: Your eidolon is a manifestation of the life force of nature in the form of a powerful magical beast that often has animal features, possibly even several from different species. You might have learned the way to connect with the world's life force via a specific philosophy or practice, such as the beliefs of the god callers of Sarkoris, or formed a bond on your own. Regardless, your link to your eidolon allows you bo

options.name: Devotion Phantom Eidolon
options.text: Your eidolon is a lost soul, unable to escape the mortal world due to a strong sense of duty, an undying devotion, or a need to complete a task that was of vital importance to the soul during their life. Most phantom eidolons are humanoid with a spectral or ectoplasmic appearance, though some take far stranger forms. Your link with your eidolon prevents them from succumbing to corruption and undeath, and together, yo

options.name: Ooze Eidolon
options.text: Your eidolon is a simple creature of protoplasm held together by magic and your mind. They often appear as creeping blobs of a single color, but this doesn't mean they can't have distinctive features, such as moss or fungus growing on their surface or bones and other debris floating within. Because they have been formed by your thoughts, your ooze eidolon isn't mindless, but likely doesn't have a complete personality

options.name: Expanded Senses
options.text: Your eidolon evolves more acute senses. Your eidolon gains low-light vision and darkvision, as well as scent as an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet.

options.name: Glider Form
options.text: Your eidolon evolves wings, a buoyant body, or some other means to control descent. They glide slowly toward the ground, 5 feet down and up to 25 feet forward through the air. As long as they spend at least 1 action gliding each round and have not yet reached the ground, they remain in the air at the end of your turn.

options.name: Energy Heart
options.text: Your eidolon's heart beats with energy. Choose acid, cold, electricity, or fire. One of their unarmed attacks changes its damage type to the chosen type, and they gain resistance to that type equal to half your level (minimum 1).

options.name: Advanced Weaponry
options.text: Your eidolon's attack evolves. Choose one of your eidolon's starting melee unarmed attacks to gain one of the following traits, chosen when you gain the feat: disarm; grapple; nonlethal; shove; trip; or versatile B, P, or S.

options.name: Battledancer
options.text: To you, a fight is a kind of performance art, and you command your foes' attention with mesmerizing motions. You are trained in Performance and gain the Fascinating Performance skill feat. When you Perform, the action gains the bravado trait.

options.name: Rascal
options.text: You aren't afraid to use underhanded tactics to get the edge over your opponents. You are trained in Thievery and gain the Dirty Trick general feat. When you use Dirty Trick, the action gains the bravado trait.

options.name: Fencer
options.text: You move carefully, feinting and creating false openings to lead your foes into inopportune attacks. You are trained in Deception. When you Create a Diversion or Feint, the action gains the bravado trait.

options.name: Braggart
options.text: You boast, taunt, and psychologically needle your foes. You are trained in Intimidation. When you Demoralize, the action gains the bravado trait.

options.name: Gymnast
options.text: You reposition, maneuver, and bewilder your foes with daring feats of physical prowess. You are trained in Athletics. When you Grapple, Reposition, Shove, or Trip, the action gains the bravado trait.

options.name: Wit
options.text: You are friendly, clever, and full of humor, always knowing just what to say. Your witticisms leave foes unprepared for the skill and speed of your attacks. You are trained in Diplomacy and gain the Bon Mot skill feat. When you use Bon Mot, the action gains the bravado trait

options.name: Chalice
options.text: Chalice implements are vessels that fill with liquid, associating them with healing, nourishment, and life. Your chalice might be a traditional cup or goblet, but it could also be a small amphora, a polished gourd, or even a hollowed-out skull. Chalice implements are associated with the astrological signs of the mother and the newlyweds, as well as the sea dragon. Initiate Benefit UfUqPcPcrGgRJCO3 inline Adept Benefi

options.name: Lantern
options.text: Lantern implements shine the light of revelation to part shadows and expose truth. You might use a common glass lantern, torch, paper lantern, or other similar light source. Lantern implements are associated with the harrow suit of stars and the astrological signs of the lantern bearer and the archer. Initiate Benefit tBI15UqeQH7PLzAK inline Adept Benefit QK5ojonup9AQBg4O inline Intensify Vulnerability Your lantern's

options.name: Mirror
options.text: Mirror implements represent misdirection, illusion, and sleight of hand, bending and shifting a perspective and the way you look at things. While larger mirrors hold the same mystic connotations, thaumaturges always choose small, portable, handheld mirrors as implements so they can use them easily while adventuring. Mirror implements are associated with the harrow suit of keys, and the astrological signs of the stran

options.name: Wand
options.text: Wand implements are short, lightweight batons, usually made of wood but often incorporating other materials. Due to their association with spellcasters, wand implements are connected to magic and its practice, as well as the direction and manipulation of energy. Wand implements are associated with the astrological signs of the thrush and the sky dragon. Initiate Benefit YbRVsHfmhPXLfCTB inline Adept Benefit pax1pnWW5

options.name: Shield
options.text: As a universal symbol of defense, a shield wards against a variety of effects and is associated with guardianship, vigilance, and guidance. You can choose only shields with a Bulk of 1 or less as an implement, which allows you to position your shield while managing your esoterica. Shield implements are associated with the harrow suit of shields and the astrological signs of the lantern bearer, the bridge, and the pat

options.name: Tome
options.text: Tome implements embody lost knowledge and otherworldly insights. While a weathered book is most common, tome implements can have as many different form factors as there are ways to store knowledge, from carved clay tablets to bundles of knotted cords. Tome implements are associated with the harrow suit of books and the astrological signs of the stargazer and the underworld dragon. Initiate Benefit oADE2kM43wpF7MT5 in

options.name: Regalia
options.text: Regalia implements represent rulership, leadership, and social connections. While they differ in shape depending on regional customs and markers used to signify authority, common regalia implements are scepters, jeweled orbs, and heraldic banners. Regalia implements are associated with the harrow suit of crowns and the astrological signs of the patriarch and the sovereign dragon. Initiate Benefit 3eRkOQa7h1MWmzBh inl

options.name: Weapon
options.text: Weapon implements are the most direct and confrontational, representing battle, struggle, and potentially violence. You can choose only a one-handed weapon as an implement, which allows you to channel energies into your weapon as well as hold your other implements once you gain them. Weapon implements are associated with the harrow suit of hammers and the astrological signs of the rider and the swordswoman. Initiate

options.name: Bell
options.text: Bells symbolize the power that sounds and emotions hold over others, soothing with one tone and startling with another. Bells, drums, finger cymbals, and other percussion instruments are most typical, but these implements can be any type of portable musical instrument that is played with one hand. Bell implements are associated with the astrological signs of the daughter and the blossom. Initiate Benefit M0UnQTqofeg1

options.name: Amulet
options.text: Amulets are items carried for good luck and protection. Your amulet might be a magical diagram, a religious symbol, a preserved body part such as a rabbit's foot, or a lucky coin. Amulet implements are associated with the harrow suit of shields and the astrological signs of the bridge and the ogre. Initiate Benefit ALcWRnRjvuPKu4nV inline Adept Benefit l3X6D8uMlt2y6vGS inline Intensify Vulnerability Your amulet repel

options.name: Censer
options.text: Censer implements are vessels in which incense is burned, producing a haze of smoke that often carries a potent odor. Censers, thuribles, and other similar items are routinely used in religious ceremonies and represent practices that alter the atmosphere of a place, usually to drive off unwanted forces. Censer implements are often associated with the harrow suit of stars and the astrological sign of the underworld dr

options.name: Spinner of Threads
options.text: You met your patron in a memory of an encounter yet to come or a premonition of something long since passed, as they untangled and re-spun the tapestry of time and fate. Was your patron a norn? A herald of a deity like Pharasma, Alseta, or Grandmother Spider? Could it even be a single individual appearing at three or more points in its timeline—multiple versions of the same being, parallel threads converging on a sin

options.name: Paradox of Opposites
options.text: Life and death, good and evil, light and shadow, vitality and void energy—these diametrically opposed concepts exist everywhere, and your patron walks the line between them. You first encountered your patron in a place or situation of such duality, such as witnessing a baby being born in a cemetery or feeling the natural light of a sunbeam in an otherwise dark cavern. There is power to be derived from the interplay b

options.name: The Unseen Broker
options.text: Whether in a dream, answering a feeling in your heart, or enacting a mysterious ritual, you have agreed to act as a mediator between your patron and the rest of the world. Of course, you understand the power of deals and receive further knowledge in exchange for your service. Your patron might be a god, an enigmatic figure like a planar being, or even an alien entity. Regardless of their origin, it is clear that thro

options.name: Ripple in the Deep
options.text: When your patron appeared, it was as an unfathomably large shadow beneath the waves, possibly as an ancient denizen of the vast waters like a kraken. Whether channeling the lethal terror of an oceanic predator or singing the ancestral wisdom of its gentle giants, your leviathan patron brings you lessons from the unplumbed depths of the world. Spell List primal Patron Skill Nature Lesson of Surface and Seas Your patro

options.name: Starless Shadow
options.text: Your patron first contacted you at the witching hour, as your body lay paralyzed by sleep while your mind had yet to escape the waking world. Your patron might be a creature of the Netherworld or a long-forgotten spirit of twilight—all you remember of them are haunting eyes of moonlight, offering you power from the darkness. Spell List occult Patron Skill Occultism Lesson of Night's Terrors Your patron taught you tha

options.name: Devourer of Decay
options.text: Your patron appeared at the end or near the end of a life, flickering in feverish visions or glinting mysteriously in the eyes of waiting scavengers. Although horrifying to many, decay creates the resources needed for new life. This fate awaits you and possibly even your patron, whether they're a towering arboreal, a subterranean fungus creature, or one of the psychopomps that shepherds the entire process along. Spel

options.name: Choir Politic
options.text: When your patron speaks, it is a chorus of voices sounding as one. They first appeared to you in the faces of your neighbors in the middle of a town festival or council meeting, when the success of an endeavor hinged on everyone working together. With the strength of your patron behind you, you then rallied the community together for a common goal. Your patron might be a single entity gathering a coterie of subjects

options.name: Wilding Steward
options.text: When your patron appeared before you, they moved with the grace and ferocity of the wilderness, their voice the creaking of trees and the sound of hoof against unspoiled earth. They might have been a dryad queen or a primeval beast, but it seemed all of nature was theirs to defend. Spell List primal Patron Skill Nature Lesson of Wild Speech Your patron has taught you the complexities of nonverbal speech, letting you

options.name: Whisper of Wings
options.text: Wings and swirling winds announced the approach of your patron. The wings might have been radiantly feathered, jeweled like a dragonfly's, strangely mechanical, or leathery with the scent of sulfur, but the controlled chaos of their movements contained countless teachings. Spell List primal Patron Skill Nature Lesson of the Observed Sky Your patron teaches that the sky can guide you anywhere you let it. You gain the

options.name: Silence in Snow
options.text: Bitter cold heralded your patron's appearance, in the depths of the winter solstice or on a frozen peak at the end of the world. Your patron might be a winter hag, ice yai, or other spirit of the cold, but one thing is clear as ice—their power is not to be underestimated. Spell List primal Patron Skill Nature Lesson of Winter's Chill Your patron taught you the power of winter firsthand by subjecting you to frost and

options.name: The Resentment
options.text: A single feeling radiated from your patron in the moment you met them, as palpable as heat from a fire: the desire to see every tall poppy felled and every proud nail hammered down, whether to righteously bring justice for small folk or the base urge to see the powerful defeated. Your patron is likely far from the upper echelons of its kind, such as a hag ousted from its coven or a quasi-divinity or a lower-rank demo

options.name: Faith's Flamekeeper
options.text: Your patron contacted you in a moment your willpower was close to sputtering out. Their reassuring presence was like breath and kindling bringing an ember back aflame, their magic giving you the strength to carry on and bring others to your cause. Your patron is likely a divine being like an angel or aeon acting covertly, though the possibility exists they might be a more sinister entity, using you to unknown ends. S

options.name: The Inscribed One
options.text: No words passed your patron's lips in the moment you met; instead, words and glyphs danced across their skin while symbols and numbers swam in the depths of their eyes, spelling out their will in a torrent of words and wisdom. Your patron might be a powerful archmage, or even one of their abandoned artifacts, searching for a successor. Spell List arcane Patron Skill Arcana Lesson of Glyph's Supremacy Your patron teac

options.name: School of Quantic Control
options.text: You're an architect, but not merely of buildings. You call upon elemental forces to control the building blocks of reality itself, reshaping the environment and moving creatures like the world is a diorama for you to perfect. Your curriculum draws heavily upon the experience of the geniekin of Quantium's Wish, who maintain the infrastructure of Nex's capital in seeming defiance of physics itself. Curriculum cantrips

options.name: School of Corentyn Armada
options.text: The Corentyn armada is well-known for their fierceness in battle, a reputation owed in large part to their naval wizards, each an expert in both tactics and torrential magic. Many such wizards are assigned to a ship in the armada, and they often take an apprentice along with them for the sea voyage. Curriculum cantrips: Message, Spout 1st: Gust of Wind, Hydraulic Push, Rude Awakening 2nd: Water Breathing, Water Walk

options.name: School of Battle Magic
options.text: Magic is power, and there are always those who will use power for the art of battle. You may have studied in the military of a nation of the brink of war—Cheliax and Andoran perhaps, or Geb and Nex. You summon whirling energies that can lay waste to both soldiers and armies, while being sure not to neglect arcane countermeasures for common tactical complications or the shields and defenses that keep combatants alive

options.name: School of Mentalism
options.text: As a scholar, you know all too well the importance of a sound mind. Thus, you attended a school—like the Farseer Tower or the Stone of the Seers—that taught the arts of befuddling lesser minds with figments and illusions or implanted sensations and memories. Curriculum cantrips: Daze, Figment 1st: Dizzying Colors, Sleep, Sure Strike 2nd: Illusory Creature, Stupefy 3rd: Dream Message, Mind Reading 4th: Nightmare, Visi

options.name: School of Unified Magical Theory
options.text: You eschew the idea that magic can be neatly expressed by the teachings of any single school or college, instead directing your self-study to pick up the best of every school of magic. In doing so, you'll find the truths that lie at the intersection of each school, coming closer to the ideal nature of arcane magic. One day, you'll uncover that single elegant theory detailing all magic (perhaps a theory bearing your n

options.name: School of Nexian Spaces
options.text: Whether your goal is immortality or creating a world with every detail tailored to your liking, retracing Nex's experiments with demiplanes is the road to achieving your desires. Your formal learning starts with reshaping your current reality and drawing power from other planes of existence. You graduate to creating extraplanar spaces and traveling between planes, making time and space yours to mold like clay. Curric

options.name: School of Protean Form
options.text: The uninitiated often think of wizards as cerebral, focused on their studies more than the body, yet your school of magic taught of the relationship between the two. Your magic, whether learned at a storied institution like Kintargo's Alabaster Academy or someplace more sinister, like the Fleshforges of Nex, focuses on the ways that living matter can be convinced into another shape for a time, allowing you to polymor

options.name: School of Ars Grammatica
options.text: Runes and wards, numbers and letters—they underpin all magic, making them the logical subject for a wizard who studies fundamental forces. Perhaps you studied at the Pathfinder Society's School of Spells or a similar institution, but whether you're lacing your words with magic to compel others, casting wards around your workshop, or destabilizing the very structure of an opponent's spells, you know this unassuming sc

options.name: School of Civic Wizardry
options.text: Whether you studied in Manaket's Occularium or the Academy of Applied Magic, you learned that the fruits of arcane studies—like any other field—should ultimately help the common citizen. You've learned the humble art of construction, of finding lost people and things, of moving speedily among buildings and moats—yet these same arts can be turned to demolition, and the constructs you animate to build bridges can just

options.name: School of Keen Inquiry
options.text: You're a scholar of truth, seeking knowledge about the nature of existence and events past, present, and future. Whether you share or obfuscate that truth—best reserve judgment until you know what you're working with. Quantium's elite claim agents of Her Most Keen Eye, Nex's network of spies, developed this curriculum, but it's a staple in many politically oriented colleges. Curriculum cantrips : Detect Magic, Sigil

options.name: School of the Boundary
options.text: Why use your magic to affect something as pedestrian as the physical world? Whether you studied at the College of Dimensional Studies in Katapesh or an underground school in haunted Ustalav, you've turned your magic past the Universe to the forces beyond, summoning spirits and shades, manipulating dimensions and planes, and treading in a place not meant for mortals. Curriculum cantrips: Telekinetic Hand, Void Warp 1s

options.name: Experimental Spellshaping
options.text: Your thesis posits that the magical practice of spellshaping can be realized more efficiently by altering variables and parameters as you cast, imitating the wizards of long ago who had to work out their own spells themselves. This allows you efficient access to various spellshape effects. You gain one 1st-level spellshape wizard feat of your choice. Starting at 4th level, during your daily preparations, you can gain

options.name: Spell Substitution
options.text: You don't accept the fact that once spells are prepared, they can't be changed until your next daily preparations, and you have uncovered a shortcut allowing you to substitute new spells for those you originally prepared. You can spend 10 minutes to empty one of your prepared spell slots and prepare a different spell from your spellbook in its place. If you are interrupted during such a swap, the original spell remai

options.name: Spell Blending
options.text: You theorize that spell slots are a shorthand for an underlying energy that powers all spellcasting, and you've found a way to tinker with the hierarchy of spell slots, combining them to fuel more powerful spells. During your daily preparations, you can trade two spell slots of the same spell rank for a bonus spell slot of up to 2 spell ranks higher than the traded spell slots. You can exchange as many spell slots as

options.name: Improved Familiar Attunement
options.text: You've long held that fine-tuning the magic that bonds a wizard and their familiar can improve the mystic connection and yield greater results, compared to the safe yet generic bond most wizards currently use. You've formed such a pact with your familiar, gaining more advantages from it than most wizards. You gain the Familiar wizard feat. Your familiar gains an extra ability, and it gains an additional extra ability

options.name: Staff Nexus
options.text: Your thesis maintains that early and intense adoption of staves from the first days of study can create a symbiotic bond between spellcaster and staff, allowing them to create remarkable magic together. You've formed such a connection with a makeshift staff you built, and you are ready to infuse any staff you encounter with greater power. You begin play with a makeshift staff of your own invention. skill_feats.text: When you successfully Steal something, observers (creatures other than the creature you stole from) take a –2 circumstance penalty to their Perception DCs to detect your theft. Additionally, if you first Create a Diversion using Deception, taking a single Palm an Object or Steal action doesn't end your Undetected condition.

skill_feats.name: Quick Repair
skill_feats.text: For you, the Repair activity loses the exploration trait and takes 1 minute instead of 10 minutes. If you're a master in Crafting, it takes 3 actions. If you're legendary, it takes 1 action.

skill_feats.name: Quick Squeeze
skill_feats.text: You Squeeze 5 feet per round (10 feet on a critical success). If you're legendary in Acrobatics, you Squeeze at full Speed.

skill_feats.name: Lengthy Diversion
skill_feats.text: When you critically succeed to Create a Diversion, you continue to remain Hidden after the end of your turn. This effect lasts for an amount of time that depends on the diversion and situation, as determined by the GM (minimum 1 additional round).

skill_feats.name: Pickpocket
skill_feats.text: You can Steal or Palm an Object that's closely guarded, such as in a pocket, without taking the –5 penalty. You can't steal objects that would be extremely noticeable or time consuming to remove (like worn shoes or armor or actively wielded objects). If you're a master in Thievery, you can attempt to Steal from a creature in combat or otherwise on guard. When doing so, Stealing requires 2 actions instead of 1, and yo

skill_feats.name: Cat Fall
skill_feats.text: Your catlike aerial acrobatics allow you to cushion your falls. Treat falls as 10 feet shorter. If you're an expert in Acrobatics, treat falls as 25 feet shorter and 50 feet if you're a master. If you're legendary in Acrobatics, you always land on your feet and don't take damage, regardless of the distance of the fall.

skill_feats.name: Lie to Me
skill_feats.text: You can use Deception to weave traps to trip up anyone trying to deceive you. If you can engage in conversation with someone trying to Lie to you, use your Deception DC if it is higher than your Perception DC to determine whether they succeed. This doesn't apply if you don't have a back-and-forth dialogue, such as when someone attempts to Lie during a long speech.

skill_feats.name: Student of the Canon
skill_feats.text: You've researched many faiths enough to recognize notions about them that are unlikely to be true. If you roll a critical failure at a Religion check to Decipher Writing of a religious nature or to Recall Knowledge about the tenets of faiths, you get a failure instead. When attempting to Recall Knowledge about the tenets of your own faith, if you roll a failure, you get a success instead, and if you roll a success, y

skill_feats.name: Recognize Spell

skill_feats.text: You can use the Craft activity to create alchemical items. When you select this feat, you immediately add the formulas for four common 1st-level alchemical items to your formula book.

skill_feats.name: Dirty Trick
skill_feats.text: Requirements You have a hand free and are within melee reach of an opponent. You hook a foe's bootlaces together, pull their hat over their eyes, loosen their belt, or otherwise confound their mobility through an underhanded tactic. Attempt a thievery|defense:reflex check against the target's Reflex DC. Critical Success The target is Clumsy 1 until they use an Interact action to end the impediment Success As critical

skill_feats.name: Armor Assist
skill_feats.text: After your service aiding armored combatants, you are practiced in helping yourself and others don heavy gear. You can attempt an Athletics or Warfare Lore check with a DC determined by the GM (but usually 15 for common armor, DC 20 for uncommon armor, and DC 25 for rare armor) to halve the time you take to don armor. You can halve an ally's time to don armor by working with them to don the armor and succeeding at an
prereq: trained in Athletics or Warfare Lore

skill_feats.name: Forager
skill_feats.text: While using Survival to Subsist, if you roll any result worse than a success, you get a success. On a success, you can provide subsistence living for yourself and four additional creatures, and on a critical success, you can take care of twice as many additional creatures. You can choose to support half the number of creatures with a comfortable living. Increase the number of additional creatures you feed on a succes

skill_feats.name: Experienced Professional
skill_feats.text: You carefully safeguard your professional endeavors to prevent disaster. When you use Lore to Earn Income, if you roll a critical failure, you instead get a failure. If you're an expert in Lore, you gain twice as much income from a failed check to Earn Income, unless it was originally a critical failure.

skill_feats.name: Snare Crafting
skill_feats.text: You can use the Craft activity to create snares. When you select this feat, you add the formulas for four common 1st-level snares to your formula book.

skill_feats.name: Courtly Graces
skill_feats.text: You were raised among the nobility or have learned proper etiquette and bearing, allowing you to present yourself as a noble and play games of influence and politics. Unless you are intentionally presenting yourself differently, anyone who speaks with you will assume you are a noble or closely associated with the nobility (such as a prominent servant). You can use Society to Make an Impression on a noble, as well as

skill_feats.name: Assurance
skill_feats.text: Even in the worst circumstances, you can perform basic tasks. Choose a skill you're trained in. You can forgo rolling a skill check for that skill to instead receive a result of 10 + your proficiency bonus (do not apply any other bonuses, penalties, or modifiers). Special You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, choose a different skill and gain the benefits for that skill.
prereq: trained in at least one skill

skill_feats.name: Multilingual
skill_feats.text: You easily pick up new languages. You learn two new languages, chosen from common languages, uncommon languages, and any others you have access to. You learn an additional language if you are or become a master in Society and again if you are or become legendary. Special You can select this feat multiple times. Each time, you learn additional languages.

skill_feats.name: Experienced Tracker
skill_feats.text: Tracking is second nature to you, and when necessary you can follow a trail without pause. You can Track while moving at full Speed by taking a –5 penalty to your Survival check. If you're a master in Survival, you don't take the –5 penalty. If you're legendary in Survival, you no longer need to roll a new Survival check every hour when tracking, though you still need to roll whenever there are significant changes in

skill_feats.name: Terrain Expertise
skill_feats.text: Your experience in navigating a certain type of terrain makes you supremely confident while doing so. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Survival checks in one of the following types of terrain, chosen when you select this feat: aquatic, arctic, desert, forest, mountain, plains, sky, swamp, or underground. Special You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different type of terrain each time.

skill_feats.name: Train Animal
skill_feats.text: You spend time teaching an animal to do a certain action. You can either select a basic action the animal already knows how to do (typically those listed in the Command an Animal action) or attempt to teach the animal a new basic action. The GM determines the DC of any check required and the amount of time the training takes (usually at least a week). It's usually impossible to teach an animal a trick that uses criti

skill_feats.name: Virtuosic Performer
skill_feats.text: You have exceptional talent with one type of performance. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus when making a certain type of performance. If you are a master in Performance, this bonus increases to +2. Select one of the following specialties and apply the bonus when attempting Performance checks of that type. If it's unclear whether the specialty applies, the GM decides. Specialty Examples Acting Drama, pantomime, puppet

skill_feats.name: Hefty Hauler
skill_feats.text: You can carry more than your frame implies. Increase your maximum and encumbered Bulk limits by 2.

skill_feats.name: Specialty Crafting
skill_feats.text: Your training focused on Crafting one particular kind of item. Select one of the specialties listed below; you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Crafting checks to Craft items of that type. If you are a master in Crafting, this bonus increases to +2. If it's unclear whether the specialty applies, the GM decides. Some specialties might apply only partially. For example, if you were making a morningstar and had specialty

skill_feats.name: Bargain Hunter
skill_feats.text: You can Earn Income using Diplomacy, spending your days hunting for bargains and reselling at a profit. You can also spend time specifically sniffing out a great bargain on an item; this works as if you were using Earn Income with Diplomacy, except instead of gaining money, you purchase the item at a discount equal to the money you would have gained, gaining the item for free if your earned income equals or exceeds i

skill_feats.name: Oddity Identification
skill_feats.text: When you become aware of a magical effect or see a spell being cast, you can immediately determine if it twists minds (with the mental trait), fights against fortune (with the fortune or misfortune trait), or reveals secrets (with the detection, prediction, revelation, or scrying traits). At the GM's discretion, similar effects can also fall into these categories. When you [[/act identify-magic skill=occultism]] or [

skill_feats.name: Concealing Legerdemain
skill_feats.text: Rather than hide an object somewhere the inspectors won't search, you're skilled at keeping the object on the move so it's never where they look. When you Conceal an Object of light Bulk or less, you can use Thievery instead of Stealth for your checks and for the DC of an active searcher's Perception check. You roll the check only once, but you must continue to use actions to Conceal an Object throughout the process.

skill_feats.name: Seasoned
skill_feats.text: You've mastered the preparation of many types of food and drink. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to Craft food and drink, including elixirs if you have Alchemical Crafting and potions if you have Magical Crafting. If you are a master in one of the prerequisite skills, this bonus increases to +2.
prereq: trained in Alcohol Lore, Cooking Lore, or Crafting

skill_feats.name: Dubious Knowledge
skill_feats.text: You're a treasure trove of information, but not all of it comes from reputable sources. When you fail (but don't critically fail) a Recall Knowledge check using any skill, you learn the correct answer and an erroneous answer, but you don't have any way to differentiate which is which. This can occur as knowing something is significant, but not whether it's good or bad.
prereq: trained in a skill with the Recall Knowledge action

skill_feats.name: Combat Climber
skill_feats.text: Your techniques allow you to fight as you climb. You're not Off-Guard while Climbing and can Climb with a hand occupied. You must still use another hand and both legs to Climb.

skill_feats.name: Root Magic
skill_feats.text: Your talismans ward against foul magic. During your daily preparations, you can assemble a small pouch with bits of herbs, hair, sacred oils, and other ritual ingredients, which you give to one ally; the ally cannot be yourself. skill_feats.name: Streetwise
skill_feats.text: You know about life on the streets and feel the pulse of your local settlement. You can use your Society modifier instead of your Diplomacy modifier to [[/act gather-information skill=society]]. In any settlement you frequent regularly, you can use the Recall Knowledge action with Society to know the same sorts of information that you could discover with Diplomacy to Gather Information. The DC is usually significantl

skill_feats.name: Arcane Sense
skill_feats.text: Your study of magic allows you to instinctively sense its presence. You can cast 1st-rank Detect Magic at will as an arcane innate spell. If you're a master in Arcana, the spell is heightened to 3rd rank; if you're legendary, it is heightened to 4th rank.

skill_feats.name: Additional Lore
skill_feats.text: Your knowledge has expanded to encompass a new field. Choose a Lore skill subcategory. You become trained in it. At 3rd, 7th, and 15th levels, you gain an additional skill increase you can apply only to the chosen Lore subcategory. Special You can select this feat more than once. Each time you must select a new subcategory of Lore and you gain the additional skill increases to that subcategory for the listed levels.

skill_feats.name: Glean Contents
skill_feats.text: You are adept at quickly scanning loose papers and carefully discerning the contents of sealed letters without damaging the seal. You can attempt Society checks to Decipher Writing on a message that is only partially glimpsed, upside down or reversed from your perspective, and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the check when doing so. You can also use this feat to decipher sealed letters, adding the manipulate trait to

skill_feats.name: Skill Training
skill_feats.text: You become trained in the skill of your choice. Special You can select this feat multiple times, choosing a new skill to become trained in each time.

skill_feats.name: Quick Jump
skill_feats.text: You can use High Jump and Long Jump as a single action instead of 2 actions. If you do, you don't perform the initial Stride (nor do you fail if you don't Stride 10 feet).

skill_feats.name: Inoculation
skill_feats.text: You have practice combating plague, and your patients are less likely to succumb to the same disease again for a time. When you successfully Treat a Disease on someone and they fully recover from the disease, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against that same disease for 1 week.

skill_feats.name: No Cause for Alarm
skill_feats.text: You attempt to reduce panic. Attempt a diplomacy check, comparing it to the Will DC of creatures in a emanation|distance:10 around you who are Frightened. Each of them is temporarily immune for 1 hour. Critical Success Reduce the creature's frightened value by 2. Success Reduce the creature's frightened value by 1.

skill_feats.name: Schooled in Secrets
skill_feats.text: You notice the signs and symbols that members of mystery cults and other secret societies use to declare their affiliation to fellow members. You can use Occultism in place of Diplomacy to [[/act gather-information skill=occultism]]{Gather Information} about such groups and in place of Deception to [[/act impersonate skill=occultism]]{Impersonate} a member of these groups. If you belong to a secret cult, lodge, sect,

skill_feats.name: Improvise Tool
skill_feats.text: You can jury-rig solutions when you don't have the proper tools on hand. You can attempt to Repair damaged items without a repair kit. If you have the raw materials available, you can Craft a basic Caltrop set, Candle, Compass, Crowbar, Fishing Tackle, Flint and Steel, Hammer, Ladder, Piton, Rope, Ten-Foot Pole, Replacement Thieves Picks, Long Tool or Short Tool, or Torch as if you had their formulas.

skill_feats.name: Underwater Marauder
skill_feats.text: You've learned to fight underwater. You are not Off-Guard while in water, and you don't take the usual penalties for using a bludgeoning or slashing melee weapon in water.

skill_feats.name: Quick Identification
skill_feats.text: You can Identify Magic swiftly. You take only 1 minute when using Identify Magic to determine the properties of an item, ongoing effect, or location, rather than 10 minutes. If you're a master, it takes a 3-action activity, and if you're legendary, it takes 1 action.
prereq: trained in Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion

skill_feats.name: Impressive Performance
skill_feats.text: Your performances inspire admiration and win you fans. You can [[/act make-an-impression skill=performance]] using Performance instead of Diplomacy. If you spend at least 10 minutes performing in front of an audience, you can Make an Impression targeting up to 10 members of the audience who were there for the whole performance, without taking the normal penalty. The number of targets increases to 20 for a 1-hour perf

skill_feats.name: Terrain Stalker
skill_feats.text: Select one type of difficult terrain from the following list: rubble, snow, or underbrush. While Undetected by all non-allies in that type of terrain, you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than 5 feet and do not pass within 10 feet of an enemy during your movement. During exploration, this also allows you to automatically approach within 15 feet of other creatures while Avoiding

skill_feats.name: Bon Mot
skill_feats.text: You launch an insightful quip at a foe, distracting them. Choose a foe within 30 feet and roll a diplomacy|against:will check against the target's Will DC. Critical Success The target is distracted and takes a –3 status penalty to Perception and Will saves for 1 minute. The target can end the effect early with a retort to your Bon Mot. This can either be a single action that has the concentrate trait or an appropriat

skill_feats.name: Deceptive Worship
skill_feats.text: Members of your cult frequently pass themselves off as worshippers of other religions. You can use Occultism instead of Deception to Impersonate a typical worshipper of another faith or to Lie specifically to claim you are a member of the faith you are Impersonating. You still need to use the Deception skill to Impersonate a specific worshipper or to perform other deceptive actions, such as attempting to Lie about an

skill_feats.name: Acrobatic Performer
skill_feats.text: You're an incredible acrobat, evoking wonder and enrapturing audiences with your prowess. You can roll an [[/act perform skill=acrobatics variant=dance]]{Acrobatics} check instead of a Performance check when using the Perform action. If you are trained in both Acrobatics and Performance, you gain a +1 circumstances bonus on Acrobatics checks made to Perform.

skill_feats.name: Pilgrim's Token
skill_feats.text: You carry a small token of protection from a site holy to your faith. You gain a wooden religious symbol for your deity for free. As long as this religious symbol is in your possession, when you tie an adversary's initiative roll, you go first. If you lose this religious symbol, you must purchase or Craft a replacement and attune it. Such a token usually costs at least 1 sp, and the attunement takes 10 minutes of pra

skill_feats.name: Sign Language
skill_feats.text: You learn the sign languages associated with the languages you know, allowing you to sign and understand signs. Sign languages typically require both hands to convey more complex concepts, and they are visual rather than auditory. Sign language is difficult to understand during combat due to the level of attention needed, unlike basic gestures like pointing at a foe to suggest a target. Sign language is hard to use i

skill_feats.name: Trick Magic Item
skill_feats.text: You examine a magic item you normally couldn't use in an effort to fool it and activate it temporarily. For example, this might allow a fighter to cast a spell from a wand or allow a wizard to cast a spell that's not on the arcane list using a scroll. You must know what activating the item does, or you can't attempt to trick it. Attempt a check using the skill matching the item's magic tradition, or matching a tradit

skill_feats.name: Group Coercion
skill_feats.text: You can strong-arm people effectively, even when you don't have them isolated. When you Coerce, you can compare your Intimidation check result to the Will DCs of up to five targets instead of one. It's possible to get a different degree of success for each target. The number of targets you can Coerce in a single action increases to 10 if you're an expert, 25 if you're a master, and 50 if you're legendary.

branchala.anathema: silence a song of truth, destroy a work of art, spread despair

solinari.name: Solinari
solinari.title: the white moon, god of good magic and the White Robes
solinari.edicts: use magic to protect and heal, guard dangerous lore, honour the Orders

shinare.title: the Winged Victory, goddess of commerce, wealth and honest dealing
shinare.edicts: keep your bargains, trade honestly, make wealth work
shinare.anathema: break a contract, cheat a fair customer, hoard what should circulate

sirrion.name: Sirrion
sirrion.title: the Flowing Flame, god of fire, passion and change

zivilyn.name: Zivilyn
zivilyn.title: the Tree of Life, god of wisdom and insight
zivilyn.edicts: counsel wisely, see all sides, learn from every age
zivilyn.anathema: act in ignorance by choice, deny another's wisdom, mock the seeker

lunitari.name: Lunitari
lunitari.title: the red moon, goddess of neutral magic and the Red Robes
lunitari.edicts: pursue magic for its own sake, keep the balance between the Orders, test yourself
lunitari.anathema: become a renegade, use magic only for others' ends

takhisis.name: Takhisis
takhisis.title: the Dark Queen, goddess of evil, ambition and dragons
takhisis.edicts: seize power, dominate the weak, spread the Queen's order
takhisis.anathema: show weakness, serve the gods of light, let an insult go unanswered

sargonnas.name: Sargonnas
sargonnas.title: the Horned One, god of vengeance, rage and the minotaurs
sargonnas.edicts: take vengeance for every wrong, prove your strength, honour the strong
sargonnas.anathema: forgive an enemy who has not paid, show fear in battle

morgion.name: Morgion
morgion.title: the Black Wind, god of disease and decay
morgion.edicts: spread sickness, endure pain in silence, hide your rot
morgion.anathema: cure a disease, reveal the temple

chemosh.name: Chemosh
chemosh.title: the Lord of Bones, god of undeath
chemosh.edicts: seek life beyond death, bind the dead to purpose
chemosh.anathema: destroy undead you could command, accept a natural death

zeboim.name: Zeboim
zeboim.title: the Sea Witch, goddess of storms and the sea's fury
zeboim.edicts: respect the sea's anger, take what the waves give, never forgive a slight
zeboim.anathema: sail without an offering, rescue a drowning enemy

hiddukel.name: Hiddukel
hiddukel.title: the Prince of Lies, god of greed and broken deals
hiddukel.edicts: profit from every deal, lie well, collect secrets
hiddukel.anathema: give something away for nothing, keep a deal you can profitably break

nuitari.name: Nuitari
nuitari.title: the black moon, god of evil magic and the Black Robes
nuitari.edicts: seek power through magic, keep forbidden lore, honour the Orders
nuitari.anathema: share your secrets freely, become a renegade

krynn_notes_mortals.cleric: In these years the gods are gone and no prayer is answered. Agree with the GM where the power comes from: the Power of the Heart, or a god who has not quite left.
krynn_notes_mortals.champion: With the gods gone, a champion's power comes from the heart or from an oath itself. Agree it with the GM; the Knights of Solamnia still fit.
krynn_notes_mortals.druid: With the gods of nature gone, a druid draws on the primal magic of the world itself, as the sorcerers of the Academy do.
krynn_notes_mortals.wizard: The magic of the moons failed with the gods. A wizard in these years studies the new primal sorcery or an old secret; agree it with the GM.
krynn_notes_mortals.magus: The magic of the moons failed with the gods; agree with the GM what this magic draws on.
krynn_notes_mortals.oracle: Fits the mystics of the Citadel of Light and the Power of the Heart.
krynn_notes_mortals.sorcerer: Fits the primal sorcery of the Age of Mortals, taught at the Academy of Sorcery.

adapter.afflicted_kender: An afflicted kender: since the red dragon, this kender feels fear, and loses some of the kender's carelessness and taunts. Agree with the GM how it plays.

krynn_notes.wizard: In Krynn, wizards answer to the Towers of High Sorcery. Agree with the GM whether the character has taken the Test.
krynn_notes.magus: Arcane magic: the same conversation about the Towers of High Sorcery applies.
krynn_notes.witch: The patron is the GM's call; to the Towers, this is renegade magic.
krynn_notes.sorcerer: Sorcery outside the Towers is seen as renegade magic in Ansalon.
krynn_notes.cleric: Only the true gods grant power. The list of Krynn's deities is an adaptation to agree with the GM.
krynn_notes.champion: Needs a Krynn deity (adaptation). The Knights of Solamnia are the natural fit.
krynn_notes.oracle: The mystery is the GM's call; clerics tend to be wary of oracles.
krynn_notes.druid: Fits Krynn's gods of nature (Chislev, Habbakuk), as an adaptation.
krynn_notes.animist: Fits the ancestor spirits of the plains tribes.
krynn_notes.inventor: Fits the tinker gnomes; rare outside them.
krynn_notes.exemplar: A rare class. Only with the GM's approval.
krynn_notes.necromancer: In Krynn, necromancy is linked to the Black Robes and to Chemosh.

background_lives.courier: You carried what others couldn't, and didn't ask what it was.

background_lives.detective: You found the truth others had buried.

background_lives.farmhand: You worked the land, from season to season.
background_lives.field-medic: You patched people up where the fighting was.
background_lives.fortune-teller: You told people their futures, and sometimes you were right.
background_lives.gambler: You lived by the dice and the cards, and by reading faces.
background_lives.gladiator: You fought for a crowd, and the crowd loved you for it.
background_lives.guard: You stood watch and kept the peace, or tried to.
background_lives.herbalist: You knew which plants heal and which ones kill.
background_lives.hermit: You lived apart, and learned what solitude teaches.
background_lives.hunter: You fed people from the wild, and knew every track.
background_lives.insurgent: You fought against those who ruled by force.
background_lives.laborer: You did the heavy work, for whoever paid.
background_lives.martial-disciple: You trained your body as a discipline, every day.
background_lives.merchant: You bought, sold, and knew what everything was worth.
background_lives.miner: You worked underground, where the light doesn't reach.
background_lives.noble: You grew up with a name that opened doors.
background_lives.nomad: You never stayed anywhere long, and the road was home.
background_lives.outrider: You rode ahead of the others, scouting the open land.
background_lives.pilgrim: You walked a long road towards something holy.
background_lives.prisoner: You spent time in chains, and you remember all of it.
background_lives.refugee: You lost your home and made another among strangers.
background_lives.root-worker: You practised the old remedies, half medicine and half something else.
background_lives.saboteur: You knew how to make things break at the worst moment.
background_lives.sailor: You worked on the water, from port to port.
background_lives.scavenger: You lived on what others threw away or left behind.
background_lives.scholar: You studied, and studying became who you are.
background_lives.scout: You went ahead, unseen, and came back to tell.
background_lives.servant: You served in a great house, and saw how it really worked.
background_lives.squire: You served a knight, and learned their code.
background_lives.street-urchin: You grew up on the streets, and the streets taught you.
background_lives.tax-collector: You collected what was owed, and nobody liked you for it.
background_lives.teacher: You taught others what you knew.
background_lives.tinker: You fixed and built things, and often improved them.
background_lives.ward: You were raised by someone powerful who was not your family.
background_lives.warrior: You fought, for pay or for your people.

class_calls.alchemist: Mixtures, reagents and formulas you trust more than spells.
class_calls.animist: The spirits around you have started to answer, and to ask.
class_calls.barbarian: There's a fury in you, and you've learned to ride it.
class_calls.bard: Your songs and stories carry a power of their own.
class_calls.champion: A god's cause, and an oath you will keep at any cost.
class_calls.cleric: A god has answered your prayers, and expects service.
class_calls.commander: People follow you, and you know how to lead them in a fight.
class_calls.druid: The wild speaks to you, and you speak for it.
class_calls.exemplar: Something divine burns in you, and shows in what you do.
class_calls.fighter: Weapons and armour, and the skill to use them better than anyone.
class_calls.guardian: You stand between harm and those behind you.
class_calls.inventor: Your own inventions, and the nerve to use them.
class_calls.investigator: You notice everything, and you put it together.
class_calls.kineticist: A raw force of nature answers you, with no spell at all.
class_calls.magus: Steel and spell together, in the same strike.
class_calls.monk: Your body and mind, trained into a weapon.
class_calls.necromancer: The power over life and death that others fear to touch.
class_calls.oracle: A mystery has marked you; it gives power, and it takes.
class_calls.psychic: Your own mind, opened wider than it should be.
class_calls.ranger: The hunt, the trail, and the quarry that never escapes.
class_calls.rogue: Skill, stealth and a knack for being where you're not expected.
class_calls.runesmith: Runes carved and traced, older than the Cataclysm.
class_calls.sorcerer: Magic in your blood, unasked for and impossible to give back.
class_calls.summoner: A bond with a creature from beyond, who fights at your side.
class_calls.swashbuckler: Flair, speed and a blade that dances.
class_calls.thaumaturge: Strange objects and old lore, used against the things that hunt in the dark.
class_calls.witch: A patron's gifts, and a debt that comes with them.
class_calls.wizard: The study of magic, in books, with discipline and a test ahead.

"Let me tell you a story."
"Nobody owns me."
"Family first. Mine is whoever I say it is."
"Quietly, now."

events.title: The Wedding
events.scene: Someone has been sharing your table for a while now. Their family is asking questions, yours is asking louder. {spouse.name} says it plainly one evening: either this is a life, or it isn't.

choices.text: Make it a life

outcomes.text: A small wedding, a bigger feast, and years that are mostly good. You learn what it is to have someone wait for you.
You marry. It is harder than either of you thought, and you stay anyway, which is its own kind of love.
You marry, and within a few years you are burying them. The house is very quiet after.

choices.text: Say you're not made for it

outcomes.text: They leave. You tell yourself you chose freedom. Some nights that's true.
They stay a friend, which neither of you expected, and which lasts longer than most marriages.

events.title: A Child in the House
events.scene: There is a child in your house now, by birth, by marriage or because nobody else would take them. {child.name} cries at night and laughs at nothing, and the whole shape of your days changes around them.

choices.text: Stay close; be there for every step

outcomes.text: You raise them. It takes everything and gives back more. They grow up and, one day, they don't need you.
A winter fever. You sit up seven nights and they live. You never again believe you are in control of anything.

choices.text: Work harder, so they want for nothing

outcomes.text: They want for nothing, except you. They grow up polite and a little distant.
You come home one evening to a doctor at the door. The child does not live to see spring.
They are raised mostly by others. When they're grown, they tell you so, without anger, which is worse.

events.title: A Business of Your Own
events.scene: A shop is for sale: the old owner is tired, the price is fair and the street is good. It would take every coin you have, and some you don't.

choices.text: Buy it

outcomes.text: It thrives. Your name goes over the door, and people start saying it the way they say the names of the old families.
It survives, barely, year after year. You learn every trick of making little go a long way.
A bad season, then a worse one. You sell it for less than you paid and owe the difference to a patient man.

choices.text: Buy it with a partner

outcomes.text: Your partner is honest and dull, the best kind. You both grow comfortable.
Your partner empties the strongbox and the town between one night and the next.

events.title: A Field of Your Own
events.scene: A plot of land, with a roofless house and a stubborn well. It is cheap because nobody wants to break their back on it.

choices.text: Break your back on it

outcomes.text: Five years of stones and roots. Then a harvest that makes the neighbours stop and look.
Three dry years in a row. You learn what hunger feels like when you are the one who should have prevented it.

choices.text: Let it out to others and live off the rent

outcomes.text: You become, without meaning to, someone people bow to on market day.
Your tenants hate you, politely. One of them hates you a little more than politely.

events.title: The Quarrel at the Well
events.scene: Two families have been feuding over a boundary stone for a generation. Today it came to knives. Someone says: let them settle it in front of you; you're fair.

choices.text: Hear them both out and decide

outcomes.text: Your judgement holds. After that, people bring you their quarrels, and the village learns to wait for your word.
You decide fairly, and the losing family never forgives you.

choices.text: Say it isn't your business

outcomes.text: It goes to blood. You help bury a boy you could have saved with a sentence.
They settle it themselves, badly, and blame you a little for not helping.

events.title: The Coughing Season
events.scene: A coughing sickness goes through the town. Those who can, close their doors. The healer is overwhelmed and asks anyone with steady hands to help.

choices.text: Help the healer

outcomes.text: You carry water, burn bedding, close eyes. Many live who wouldn't have. Afterwards nobody forgets your face.
You catch it. You live, but your lungs never quite forgive you.
Someone of your own house is among the dead. You were helping others when it happened.

choices.text: Close the door and keep your own safe

outcomes.text: Your house comes through. The town remembers who opened their doors and who didn't.
It comes in anyway, through the shutters, through the bread. You learn there is no closing a door on some things.

events.title: The Night the Street Burned
events.scene: Fire. Half the street is already alight when you wake, and the wind is blowing towards everything you own.

choices.text: Save what you can of your own

outcomes.text: You drag out the strongbox and the ledgers. The house goes; the life inside it doesn't.
You save almost nothing and carry the burn on your forearm for the rest of your days.

choices.text: Run for the houses with children in them

outcomes.text: Three children out of a window. Your own house burns while you do it. The street rebuilds it for you, board by board.
You reach the last house too late. You hear about it in your sleep for years.

events.title: Someone Wants to Learn
events.scene: A sharp-eyed youngster has been watching you work for weeks. Today they ask outright to be taught everything you know.

choices.text: Teach them, properly

outcomes.text: They are better than you were at that age, and you are proud of it, most days.
In five years they are better than you. In ten, they are famous and never mention your name.

choices.text: Send them away; you have no time

outcomes.text: They come back every day for a month. In the end you give in, cursing.
They go to someone worse, and pick up all of their bad habits. It annoys you more than it should.

events.title: The New Lord's Tax
events.scene: The new lord's steward rides in with armed men and a new tax that would ruin half the town by spring. People look at each other, and some of them look at you.

choices.text: Speak for the town

outcomes.text: You argue for an afternoon. The tax is halved, and the steward will remember your face.
His men beat you in the square as an example. The town pays, and brings you soup for a month.
You find a quiet way: a debt the steward would rather nobody knew about. The tax goes away. Nobody knows why.

choices.text: Pay and keep your head down

outcomes.text: You pay. Everyone pays. The town is poorer and quieter.
You hide half your goods in the hills, and help your neighbours hide theirs.

events.title: The Last of the Old Ones
events.scene: The last of the people who raised you is dying. They ask for you, and you have to travel three days to get there in time.

choices.text: Drop everything and go

outcomes.text: You get there in time. They tell you something about your family you never knew, and then they sleep.
