You arrive the morning after. They left you a box with your name on it, and a key.

choices.text: You can't leave now; send word

outcomes.text: The word that comes back is that they waited for you until the end.
They held on long enough for your letter to be read to them. It said the right things, and you'll never know if they heard.

events.title: An Old Face in Town
events.scene: Someone from your youth has come to live in town: richer, louder and not one bit changed. They seem delighted to see you. That's the worrying part.

choices.text: Let bygones be bygones

outcomes.text: Over a few years and a lot of wine, you become something like friends.
You let them close, and they use it. You lose something you can't get back.

choices.text: Keep them at arm's length

outcomes.text: A cold peace for years, at every wedding and funeral.
They die suddenly, and you learn they had been helping you in secret all along.

events.title: The Temple Steps
events.scene: The true gods have returned, and a small temple has gone up at the end of your street. They need people who can keep accounts, mend roofs and sit with the dying.

choices.text: Give them your evenings

outcomes.text: Years of evenings. Somewhere in them, you start to believe.
You learn that a temple is also a town council in robes, and become quietly important in it.

choices.text: Keep away from priests

outcomes.text: You've seen what false priests did. You'll wait and see what true ones do.
You keep away, until the night a priest sits with your dying neighbour and asks nothing in return.

events.title: The Itch
events.scene: It comes every spring now, when the caravans leave: a restlessness that makes your house feel smaller and your days shorter.

choices.text: Walk out of town one morning and keep going a while

outcomes.text: Three days on the road. You come back, but you know now you could leave.
On the second day you stumble into someone else's trouble, and handle it better than you'd have thought.

choices.text: Bury it under work

outcomes.text: It works, for years. Then one day it doesn't.
It works, and you grow a little bitter, and you know it.

events.title: The Stranger You Fed
events.scene: A ragged traveller knocks at your door in a storm. You feed them, give them the barn, and in the morning they are gone, leaving a coin of a kind you have never seen.

choices.text: Keep the coin

outcomes.text: Your luck is strangely good after that, for years.
Years later someone very dangerous comes asking about that coin.

choices.text: Follow their tracks in the mud

outcomes.text: The tracks lead to a burned camp and a name scratched on a stone. You remember the name.
You catch up with them on the ridge. You talk until noon and part friends, and the friend matters later.

events.title: Soldiers on the Road
events.scene: An army passes along the road for three days. Some of its soldiers pay for what they take. Most don't. On the third night a sergeant knocks at your door.

choices.text: Give them what they ask

outcomes.text: They take food and leave. You were lucky, and you know it.
They take food, and want a guide through the hills. You go, and see what armies do.

choices.text: Bar the door

outcomes.text: They burn the barn as a lesson. The lesson takes.
The sergeant laughs, says you remind him of his mother, and moves on.

events.title: The Letter From Far Away
events.scene: A letter, years late and much handled, from someone you thought had forgotten you. It asks for help you are not sure you can give.

choices.text: Answer, and send what you can

outcomes.text: A second letter comes a year later: it was enough, and they won't forget it.
No answer ever comes. You still wonder.

choices.text: Put it in a drawer

outcomes.text: It stays in the drawer. You read it again every few years.
Two years later its writer turns up at your door, thinner, and doesn't mention the letter. You both know.

events.title: The Year Everything Went Right
events.scene: A good year, the kind you only notice afterwards: good harvest, healthy house, a feast where everyone you love is at the same table at once.

choices.text: Savour it

outcomes.text: You hold that evening in your memory like a coin in a pocket. On bad nights you take it out.
Halfway through the feast you notice someone at the window, watching. They are gone by the time you reach the door.

choices.text: Wonder when it will end

outcomes.text: You were right to worry. You were also wrong not to enjoy it.
It doesn't end for years. You learn, slowly, to let good things be good.

events.title: The Empty Side of the Bed
events.scene: {spouse.name} falls ill in the winter and doesn't see the spring. The house is full of their things, and empty.

choices.text: Keep the house as it was

outcomes.text: You keep it exactly as it was. Visitors notice and say nothing.
Slowly, you give their things away, one a year, to people who need them.

choices.text: Sell everything and leave

outcomes.text: You sell the house within the month. The road looks very different when nobody is waiting.
The buyer finds a locked box under the floor and brings it to you. Your spouse had secrets.

events.title: The Bandits' Price
events.scene: Bandits in the hills have begun taking a toll from every cart. The town's council meets. Some want to pay; some want to fight; everyone wants someone else to decide.

choices.text: Organise the town to fight

outcomes.text: Pitchforks and two old crossbows. The bandits find easier prey. You find yourself in charge of the town watch.
You win, and bury two neighbours. Their widows still nod to you, and you still can't meet their eyes.

choices.text: Negotiate the toll down

outcomes.text: You get the toll halved, and a promise they keep. You learn that bandits are a kind of lord too.
They take the money and come back for more. Of course they do.

events.title: The First Job
events.scene: Your first real job as a sword for hire: escort a merchant through hills everyone says are clear. {companion.name}, who has done this before, says they're never clear.

choices.text: Do it by the book

outcomes.text: Clean, boring and paid. You learn that boring is the best a job can be.
Ambush at the ford. You live. The merchant doesn't. You keep his ring and never find his family.

choices.text: Push through by night to save a day

outcomes.text: It works, and the merchant pays double. You start to think you're good at this.
You get lost, then found, by people who wanted to find you. Your companion buys your life with theirs.

events.title: The Ruin Under the Hill
events.scene: A map bought in a tavern, a hill with a door in it, and four of you with torches. Inside it is older and colder than anything has a right to be.

choices.text: Go all the way down

outcomes.text: Gold, and something under the gold that hums when nobody is touching it. The gold goes in a year. The other thing you keep.
Two of you come out. You don't speak of the others, even to each other.
Something at the bottom looks at you, and lets you go. You have never understood why.

choices.text: Copy the map, and leave

outcomes.text: You sell the copy for more than the original cost. Somebody else goes down instead.
You keep the map. It is still in your pack, folded small, unopened for years.

events.title: The Thing in the Marsh
events.scene: A village is losing children to something in the marsh. They have little money and a great deal of hope. Your companions look at you.

choices.text: Hunt it

outcomes.text: Three nights in the reeds. You kill it, and the village sings about it for a generation, getting the details wrong.
You kill it. It nearly kills you first. Your leg still aches when rain is coming.

choices.text: Say you're not that kind of adventurer

outcomes.text: Others take the job and the glory. You're alive, which is what you wanted. Mostly.
You leave, then come back alone in the night, because you couldn't sleep. Nobody ever knows it was you.

events.title: The Split of the Spoils
events.scene: The job paid more than anyone expected. Around the fire, the counting goes quiet, and one of your companions keeps their hand near their knife.

choices.text: Insist on equal shares

outcomes.text: Equal shares, grudgingly. The company holds together a while longer.
The knife comes out. You win. The company doesn't survive the night, and neither does a friendship.

choices.text: Let them take more; it isn't worth blood

outcomes.text: They take more. They also remember, years later, that you let them. It matters.
They take more, then all of it, while you sleep.

events.title: A Song About You
events.scene: In a tavern three valleys away, a bard is singing about a deed you did. Badly. With the wrong name. The crowd loves it.

choices.text: Stand up and correct the bard

outcomes.text: The crowd buys you drinks until dawn. Your real name goes into the song, and the song travels.
The bard is humiliated, and bards have long memories and many friends.

choices.text: Finish your drink and slip out

outcomes.text: Somebody else gets your glory. It feels better than you'd have guessed.
Someone in the corner recognises you anyway, and follows you out to ask for help.

events.title: The Wound That Ended It
events.scene: The last job of the road. Nobody knew it was the last. A bad fall, a worse blade, a fever after. When you can walk again, the company has moved on without you.

choices.text: Accept it; the road is over

outcomes.text: You go home with a limp and a purse, and tell yourself you are glad.
You go home, and drink too much for a few years, and then stop.

choices.text: Try to catch up with the company

outcomes.text: They are gone, and so is the road you knew. You find a town that needs someone and stop there.
You find them, and they have replaced you. You wish them well and mean most of it.

events.title: The One on the Road
events.scene: On the road, {love.name}, who laughs at danger and at you, in that order. Neither of you is the kind to stay anywhere.

choices.text: Travel together

outcomes.text: Years of roads, and the best of them together. Then one morning they take a different fork, and you let them.
A year together. Then a bridge, a storm, a rope that held you but not them.

choices.text: Part at the next town

outcomes.text: Letters, for years. Fewer as time goes on. You keep every one.
You part, and never hear of them again, and never quite stop listening.

events.title: The Lord Who Hired You
events.scene: A lord hires your company for a quiet job. Halfway through it becomes clear the job is to frighten some farmers off their land.

choices.text: Walk away from the job

outcomes.text: You walk. The lord doesn't pay, and doesn't forget.
You walk, and warn the farmers on your way out. They hide their families and live.

choices.text: Do the job; a contract is a contract

outcomes.text: You do it. You are paid well. You don't sleep well.
The farmers fight back. People die who didn't need to. You are among those who made sure of it.

events.title: The Library in the Ruins
events.scene: In a ruined tower, a room of books that survived the Cataclysm. Most crumble when touched. A few don't.

choices.text: Stay and read what you can

outcomes.text: Weeks of reading by candle. You come out knowing things the living have forgotten.
You take one book. It has not left your pack since, and you have read it many times, and understood it twice.

choices.text: Carry them off to sell

outcomes.text: A scholar in the city pays well and asks no questions. You spend it fast.
A scholar in the city pays well and asks many questions. Later, other people ask more.

events.title: The Cell
events.scene: A misunderstanding in a city with harsh laws, and now you are in a cell with a stranger who claims to know a way out.

choices.text: Trust the stranger

outcomes.text: Out through the drains on the third night. The stranger vanishes, and you owe them, and you know they'll collect.
The stranger sells you to the guards for their own freedom. You serve the whole sentence.

choices.text: Wait for your companions

outcomes.text: They come, with a bribe and a bad disguise. It works.
They don't come. You serve your time, and you go looking for them afterwards.

events.title: Snowed In
events.scene: A pass in the mountains, a storm that doesn't end, and a hut with you, your companions and two strangers who don't like each other.

choices.text: Keep the peace

outcomes.text: Two weeks of stories and short rations. Everyone walks out alive, which nobody expected.
On the ninth night one stranger kills the other. You never learn why.

choices.text: Try the pass in the storm

outcomes.text: You make it through, frostbitten. You lose two toes and gain a reputation.
You turn back half dead, and the strangers laugh at you, and you deserve it.

events.title: The Last Fire
events.scene: The company's last night together. Everyone knows it, nobody says it. Somebody passes the bottle and asks what you'll do now.

choices.text: Promise to meet again, all of you, in ten years

outcomes.text: You promise, and you mean it. The ten years pass. You are not the only one who forgot.
Ten years pass, and one of you does remember: a letter arrives, naming a place and a date.

choices.text: Tell them the truth: you're tired

outcomes.text: They laugh, because they're tired too. You part well.
The leader takes it as betrayal. You part badly, and that is the last you see of them.

events.title: The Old Company
events.scene: A letter in a hand you haven't seen in years. One of your old company is in trouble, and you were the one they always said could be counted on.

choices.text: Dig out the old sword

outcomes.text: The sword is rusty. So are you. You go anyway.
You go, and arrive too late for them, but not for the people they were protecting.

choices.text: Tell yourself you're too old

outcomes.text: A second letter comes, in another hand, telling you what happened. You leave the next morning.
You hesitate a week. When you go at last, the trail is colder and the company's trouble is now yours.

events.title: The Enemy You Didn't Finish
events.scene: Someone you fought on the road long ago is not dead after all. They have grown powerful, and they have not forgotten your face.

choices.text: Go out and meet it

outcomes.text: Better to choose the ground yourself. You pack quietly and leave your home in other hands.
You leave so that they will follow you, not come here. It works, for now.

choices.text: Hope they don't find you

outcomes.text: They find you. You survive the night, barely, and the next morning there is no choice left.
They don't find you. They find your neighbours instead, and ask about you. You can't let that stand.

events.title: The Map in the Drawer
events.scene: Clearing out an old chest, you find the map from your adventuring days, the one place you never went. Your hands are not steady when you unfold it.

choices.text: One last time

outcomes.text: You tell everyone it's a trip to see relatives. Nobody believes you.
At the first inn on the road you meet someone else with a copy of the same map.

choices.text: Give it to someone young

outcomes.text: You give it to a young fool, then lie awake, then follow them to make sure they live.
The young fool turns out not to be a fool, and asks you to come along as their guide.

events.title: The Song Is Wrong
events.scene: Children in the square are singing about a hero of the old days. It's you. They have made you dead, and very tall, and they have the ending wrong.

choices.text: Go and make the ending right

outcomes.text: There was something you left undone. The song reminded you. You go to finish it.
The ending was wrong because someone made sure it would be. You want to know who, and why.

choices.text: Laugh, and teach them the real verse

outcomes.text: Word gets round that the hero isn't dead. Some people are very glad. Some are not.
A child asks you to show them how it really happened. You end up showing a whole village, and then you have to leave.

events.title: When the House Is Empty
events.scene: The last of those who needed you has gone their own way. The house is quiet. For the first time in decades, nobody is waiting for you to come home.

choices.text: Take the road you didn't take when you were young

outcomes.text: Everyone says you're too old. You are, a little. You go anyway, and feel twenty for a whole week.
Your knees argue with you every morning. Your heart doesn't.

choices.text: Follow the one who left, to make sure they're safe

outcomes.text: They are not safe. They are in over their head. And so, now, are you.
They are safe, and furious that you came. Then trouble finds you both, and they're glad you did.

events.title: What the Town Owes
events.scene: Something has gone wrong that no council can vote away: a debt called in by someone dangerous, a child taken, a seal broken. Everyone turns, as they've always turned, to you.

choices.text: Go yourself; you won't send anyone else

outcomes.text: You leave your keys with the neighbour and your will with the priest.
The young ones of the town won't let you go alone, and you can't stop them.

choices.text: Choose a few young ones and lead them

outcomes.text: They are slow, loud and brave. You remember, uncomfortably, being like them.
Two of the young ones vanish on the first night. Now there is more than one thing to find.

events.title: The Dream You Had Before
events.scene: The dream you had once, as a child, comes back exactly the same, three nights running. This time you know you can't explain it away.

choices.text: Follow it

outcomes.text: You put your affairs in order like someone who doesn't expect to come back, and go.
The dream stops the moment you leave your door. That frightens you more than the dream did.

choices.text: Ask a priest what it means

outcomes.text: The priest goes pale, gives you a name and a road, and asks you not to come back until it's done.
The priest laughs and says it's indigestion. The dream comes back that night, angrier.

events.title: Nothing Left to Keep You
events.scene: In one bad season you lose the business, the house and most of the people who mattered. What's left fits in a pack.

choices.text: Shoulder the pack

outcomes.text: It's strange, how light it is. You don't look back for the first mile, and then you do.
A neighbour runs after you with bread and a name: someone who might give an old hand work, far away.

choices.text: Find out who did this to you

outcomes.text: It wasn't bad luck. Somebody arranged it, and you mean to ask them why.
It was bad luck after all, but in looking you found something else somebody very much wanted hidden.

events.title: The Healer Who Wasn't
events.scene: Three hundred years since the gods turned away, and still no prayer is answered. A priest of some new god has come to town selling cures in little clay bottles, and someone in your house is sick enough to want one.

choices.text: Buy the cure, whatever it costs

outcomes.text: It is coloured water and honey. Your family is poorer, and the fever runs its course anyway.
The fever breaks the same night. The priest takes the credit, and half the street converts.

choices.text: Go to the old woman with the herbs instead

outcomes.text: Willow bark, broth and patience. It works, slowly. She teaches you what she gave and why.
The priest calls her a witch from the square. You learn how fast a town can turn.

events.title: The Hungry Year
events.scene: The rains come wrong again, as they have so many times since the Cataclysm. The harvest rots in the fields, bread doubles in price by midwinter, and the roads fill with families walking to wherever they think there is food.

choices.text: Share what your family has with the people on the road

outcomes.text: Your family eats less all winter. In spring, one of the families you fed comes back to help with the planting.
Word spreads that your house gives. One night someone takes the rest.

choices.text: Go out and find food where nobody else is looking

outcomes.text: Roots, birds' eggs, fish from the cold pools. You learn the land that winter better than in ten years of plenty.
You poach a lord's deer, and are nearly caught. Your family eats well and asks no questions.

events.title: The Man with the Green Gem
events.scene: Strangers in dark cloaks come through, asking the same question in every inn: have you seen a man, grey-haired, quiet, with a green jewel set in his chest? They pay well for any answer. They don't say why they want him.

choices.text: Tell them about a man you think you saw

outcomes.text: They pay you in good steel and ride off. You never find out whether you sent them after the right man.
They ask too many questions about you afterwards. For a month you feel watched.

choices.text: Say nothing, and warn anyone who looks like him

outcomes.text: An old fisherman you warn goes white and leaves town that night. You'll wonder about him for years.
The strangers notice your silence. One of them smiles at you on his way out, and it's worse than a threat.

events.title: Smoke in the East
events.scene: Traders bring strange news from the east: the volcanoes around Sanction have woken, the sky over the Khalkist Mountains glows at night, and there are soldiers in the hills under banners nobody recognises.

choices.text: Ask every trader what else they saw

outcomes.text: Put together, the stories make a shape you don't like: an army, being built, a long way off. Nobody believes you.
One trader sells you a map of the passes, cheap. You don't know yet why you'll be glad of it.

choices.text: Shrug; the east is far away

outcomes.text: It is far away, for a while. You remember this conversation later.
A cousin goes east to see for himself, and doesn't come back.

events.title: Coin for Soldiers
events.scene: A recruiter in good armour sets up a table in the market: steady pay, food, boots, and a war somewhere in the east against 'the enemies of order'. He doesn't say whose army it is. Young men and women are signing.

choices.text: Ask what the army is for

outcomes.text: He doesn't answer straight. You don't sign, and three friends do. Two of them you never see again.
He's drunk enough to tell you: a Dark Queen, dragons, an empire. You laugh. Later, you stop laughing.

choices.text: Run him out of the market

outcomes.text: The market backs you. The recruiter leaves, promising to remember your face.
His guards beat you in an alley that night. You heal; the recruiter doesn't come back.

events.title: The Summer of Chaos
events.scene: 383. First come the Knights of Takhisis, black-armoured and disciplined, taking cities that surrender without a fight. Then something worse: fire that falls from a clear sky, shadows that touch people and leave no one behind to remember them, the ground itself shaking. They say the Father of All has come back to unmake the world.

choices.text: Get your people underground and wait

outcomes.text: Weeks in a cellar, listening. When you come up, the world is quieter, emptier and very strange.
Someone you love goes out for water and a shadow takes them. Nobody but you remembers they existed.

choices.text: Join whoever is fighting it

outcomes.text: Knights of Solamnia and Knights of Takhisis, side by side against the same fire. You learn that enemies can be worse things than people.
You fight, and the fire marks you. The scar never quite cools.

region.thorbardin.scene: 383. The creatures of Chaos come up from the deep places under the mountain: fire in the tunnels, the ground shaking, things in the dark that unmake whatever they touch. Thorbardin, that no army ever broke, is breaking from the inside.

region.blood_sea_isles.scene: 383. The sea itself turns on the islands: serpents of Chaos and the sea-creatures of the deep come up out of the Blood Sea against the minotaur ports. Every house is called to the walls.

events.title: The Empty Sky
events.scene: After the Summer of Chaos, the sky is wrong. The three moons are gone, and a single pale moon no one recognises has taken their place. The stars are strangers. Clerics pray and nothing answers. Wizards reach for their spells and find nothing there. The gods, everyone says, have gone, and this time they took the magic with them.

choices.text: Pray anyway, every night

outcomes.text: Nothing answers. You keep at it, out of stubbornness more than hope, and the stubbornness becomes a kind of faith.
Nothing answers from outside. But once, holding a sick child, you feel something answer from inside you.

choices.text: Stop waiting for the sky and get on with living

outcomes.text: The world still needs bread, roofs and mended nets. You decide that's enough to be going on with.
You decide the gods were never worth the fuss. You say so, loudly, at a funeral.

events.title: Dragons Over the Hills
events.scene: Great dragons, bigger than any the war knew, have come to Ansalon and are fighting each other for land. Today two of them fight in the sky over the hills, for most of an afternoon. Towards evening one falls, and the other lands on it, and does something to the body that makes everyone watching look away.

choices.text: Watch until it's over

outcomes.text: You see the winner rise heavier than it landed, glowing with what it took. You understand, without being told, that it ate more than flesh.
Days later you go out to the place where it fell and find a scale as big as a shield.

choices.text: Get everyone indoors and keep them there

outcomes.text: The village waits it out in the dark. For years afterwards, the children play dragons, and you can't bear to watch.
A stray gout of fire takes the barn. Nobody dies. You stop sleeping well.

events.title: The Knights in Black
events.scene: The Knights of Takhisis, who call themselves the Knights of Neraka now, hold the roads: a garrison in the old keep, tolls at every bridge, and a tax the dragon that rules this land expects to be paid on time. Today their officer is choosing young people to work on the new walls.

choices.text: Work, and keep your head down

outcomes.text: A season of hauling stone. The knights are hard, fair in their way, and terrifying in it.
The officer notices how well you work, and offers you a place in the order. You say you'll think about it. You keep thinking about it.

choices.text: Slip away to the people who fight them

outcomes.text: You carry messages for the resistance in the hills. When the knights hang a courier in the square, you keep carrying them.
You're caught, and spend a winter in their stockade. You come out knowing exactly who you hate.

events.title: The Power of the Heart
events.scene: Two mystics from the Citadel of Light come through, a woman and an old dwarf. They say Goldmoon has found a new power without gods: healing that comes from the heart of the healer. They lay hands on a boy who fell from a roof, and he gets up.

choices.text: Ask them how it works

outcomes.text: They teach you to breathe and to listen inside yourself. Something stirs. They tell you where the Citadel is.
You listen all evening and feel nothing. But you can't stop thinking about the boy getting up.

choices.text: Watch them closely for the trick

outcomes.text: There is no trick. That is more frightening than a trick would have been.
You're not the only one watching. Knights in black come for the mystics at dawn, and you help them out the back way.

events.title: The Citadel of Light
events.scene: On the island of Schallsea, Goldmoon's Citadel of Light takes students: no gods, no temples, only the power that lives in every heart, and years of discipline to find it. A mystic has seen something in you and offers you passage.

choices.text: Sail for Schallsea

outcomes.text: Years in the crystal domes, learning to heal with nothing but yourself. Some days it works. Some days it is the most exhausting thing in the world.
The power comes to you differently: in dreams and visions, things that haven't happened yet. The mystics are unsettled. So are you.
Goldmoon herself, old now, teaches your class for a week. You remember every word.

choices.text: Stay; your place is here

outcomes.text: The mystic nods and sails without you.
You stay, and practise what little she showed you, alone, at night.

events.title: The Legion of Steel
events.scene: A quiet woman with a soldier's hands drinks alone at the inn and watches you all evening. Before she leaves she tells you who she is: a member of the Legion of Steel, a knighthood with no god and no king, that fights for whoever needs it, in secret cells. She needs someone here.

choices.text: Join her cell

outcomes.text: Years of training in barns and cellars, of small rescues and smaller victories. The Legion's oath becomes the spine of your life.
They use you as eyes, not a blade: inns, garrisons, gossip. You become very good at being nobody.
Your cell is betrayed in the second year. You are the only one who gets out.

choices.text: Say you're no knight

outcomes.text: She says nobody is, at first, and leaves a token in case you change your mind.
You decline, and for months afterwards you notice the people the Legion saves.

events.title: The Storm and the Girl
events.scene: 421. A storm unlike any other covers all of Ansalon for days, and when it lifts, there is talk of a girl called Mina: young, shaven-headed, with eyes like amber, who works miracles in the name of the One God and leads the Knights of Neraka from victory to victory. The dead, they say, march with her.

choices.text: Go and see a miracle for yourself

outcomes.text: You see her heal a dying man with a word. You feel the pull of it, and you are afraid of how much you want to kneel.
You kneel. For a while, the One God is enough. Later, you will have to live with that.

choices.text: Stay away from her and her dead

outcomes.text: You stay away. Some of your neighbours don't. Not all of them come back as themselves.
One night the dead pass through your village on their way to her. You will never forget the sound.

events.title: The Gods Return
events.scene: The end of 421. The One God is fallen, and the old gods are back: the stars return to their places, the three moons rise again, and in every village someone who prayed without hope for forty years feels, all at once, an answer.

choices.text: Go to the old shrine and pray

outcomes.text: Something answers. Warm, vast and patient. You weep without meaning to.
Nothing answers you, but the old woman next to you is laughing and crying at once, and that's almost as good.

choices.text: Wonder where they were all this time

outcomes.text: You ask the question out loud at the shrine. Nobody has an answer, and some people stop talking to you.
You notice the old magic is back too, and the wizards in the next town are already arguing about it.

events.title: The Seekers Take Haven
events.scene: The priests who call themselves the Seekers, searching for new gods to replace the old, have won another seat on Haven's council. Their preachers are in every market now, and the town that ignores them finds its taxes doubled.

choices.text: Go to their meetings

outcomes.text: For a while the Seekers give you what you needed: an answer, a community, a reason. Later you will see what that cost.
You see how the council really works from the inside: who pays, who prays, who decides.

choices.text: Laugh at their new gods

outcomes.text: Plenty of people laugh with you, quietly, at home.
Someone reports you. Your family pays the fine, and the warning.

events.title: Dragons Over Solace
events.scene: 388. Two great dragons fight over Solace for a whole night, and the vallenwoods burn. In the morning the Inn of the Last Home is ash on the ground, and Caramon Majere, grey now, stands in the ruins and says they'll build it again.

choices.text: Help rebuild the Inn

outcomes.text: Six years of work. When the Inn opens again in its tree, you drink the first ale and Caramon calls you by name.
While you work, Caramon tells you stories of the war. You realise half the legends are true and the other half were worse.

choices.text: Leave Solace for somewhere without dragons

outcomes.text: You find out there is nowhere without dragons now. But you find somewhere.
On the road you lose everything to bandits. You arrive with nothing, and start again.

events.title: The Green Dragon's Tribute
events.scene: The green overlord who took Qualinesti claims the lands around it too. Her Knights of Neraka collect the tribute twice a year, and her draconians hunt anyone who practises magic without her leave. The forests around the towns are growing thicker, and wrong.

choices.text: Pay, and keep the family safe

outcomes.text: You pay. It's a hard winter, and you're alive at the end of it.
You pay, and hide the rest in the woodpile. The draconians don't find it. The next time they might.

choices.text: Hide the mage they're hunting

outcomes.text: She lives in your loft for a month and teaches you a word of power to pass the time.
They find her. You escape out the back and can't go home again.

events.title: The Academy of Sorcery
events.scene: Near Solace, Palin Majere and his son have opened an Academy of Sorcery: the new magic, the wild magic of the world itself, taught to anyone who can learn it, no Test and no robes. A teacher passing through has seen sparks around you, literally.

choices.text: Enrol at the Academy

outcomes.text: Years of lessons in a stone house near Solace. The magic of the world answers you more easily than anyone expected.
You turn out to be better at the theory than the casting. The Academy keeps you to teach.
Your first real spell sets the dormitory on fire. It is, everyone agrees, extremely promising.

choices.text: Decline; magic draws dragons

outcomes.text: You're not wrong. In 420, the green dragon burns the Academy to the ground.
You decline, and the sparks keep coming anyway, when you're angry.

events.title: The Academy Burns
events.scene: 420. The green dragon comes for the Academy of Sorcery near Solace. By morning it is a black ring in the forest, and the students who got out are scattered across Abanasinia with whatever they could carry.

choices.text: Help the survivors get away

outcomes.text: You hide three students in your cart under the turnips. One of them leaves you a book of spells in thanks.
Draconians follow the cart. You lose them in the woods, and your cart, and very nearly yourself.

choices.text: Watch from the hill

outcomes.text: You watch it burn, and something in you hardens towards every dragon that ever lived.
You count the dragon's servants as they come and go. Someone in the Legion will want that count.

events.title: The Waterfront
events.scene: The waterfront: pirates, minotaur sailors, smugglers, a kender selling maps of places that don't exist. A sailor has left his purse on a barrel while he argues with a captain, and three children besides you have noticed.

choices.text: Take it before they do

outcomes.text: Quick hands, and gone. Your family eats meat that week and doesn't ask.
The sailor catches your wrist, then laughs and lets you keep one coin for the nerve of it.

choices.text: Tell the sailor

outcomes.text: He gives you a coin and a job carrying messages. Half the waterfront knows your face by summer.
The other children remember who spoiled it. You learn to watch your back early.

events.title: The Tribes at the Market
events.scene: The savannah tribes come to Port Balifor twice a year with hides and horses, and the town treats them like a weather to be endured. A tribal rider your age has been cheated by a merchant and is reaching for his knife.

choices.text: Step between them

outcomes.text: You talk the merchant into paying fairly. The rider owes you, and the tribes don't forget a debt.
The knife comes out anyway and you get the edge of it. The rider stays to bind the cut.

choices.text: Watch and learn

outcomes.text: You learn how the bay cheats the tribes, and how the tribes cheat back.
It ends in blood on the market stones. You don't sleep that night.

culture.balifor_tribes.scene: Twice a year your tribe rides to Port Balifor with hides and horses, and the town looks at you like weather to be endured. Today a merchant has cheated your cousin, and your cousin is reaching for his knife.

events.title: The Night Run
events.scene: A boat, no lantern, a cargo nobody names, and a patrol cutter somewhere out on the dark bay. The captain needs one more pair of hands at the oars, tonight, and pays in silver.

choices.text: Take the oar

outcomes.text: In and out under the cutter's nose. The silver is good, and so is the feeling.
The cutter spots you. You dump the cargo and row till your hands bleed. You get away, and get nothing.

choices.text: Say no

outcomes.text: The boat goes without you. In the morning there are bodies on the beach. Not all of them are the cutter's.
The captain doesn't forget a no. Doors close quietly on the waterfront.

events.title: A Berth Out of Flotsam
events.scene: A captain with a fast ship and no questions about her past needs crew: Flotsam to Saifhum to the Blood Sea and back, a year at a time. She has watched you on the docks and says you'll do.

choices.text: Sign on

outcomes.text: Years of salt and storms. You learn every port of the eastern seas and how to leave each one in a hurry.
The ship fights as often as it trades. You learn the cutlass better than the rigging.
A storm drives you to the edge of the Maelstrom, and the captain gets you out. You never sail with anyone else.

choices.text: Stay ashore

outcomes.text: The ship sails without you. Every sail on the horizon looks like hers for a year.
You stay, and the port is enough. Mostly.

events.title: Riders from Khur
events.scene: Khurish riders and men from Sanction have been seen on the roads inland, and envoys come and go at the harbour master's house. The old sailors say the bay smells of war, and that they've smelled it before.

choices.text: Find out what the envoys want

outcomes.text: They want the port opened to an army, when the time comes. The council is already counting the gold.
One of the envoys notices you listening, and smiles.

choices.text: Go about your business

outcomes.text: Business is good while armies are buying. You don't ask what for.
A cousin goes off with the riders for good pay. You never hear from him again.

events.title: The Captains' Council
events.scene: With no king and no law worth the name since the Cataclysm, the bay is ruled by whoever has ships. Today the captains of Flotsam meet to decide who gets which waters, and the whole waterfront crowds round to watch them argue.

choices.text: Run messages between the captains

outcomes.text: You carry offers and threats all night and never mix them up. A captain remembers that.
You read one of the messages. Now you know which captain is about to betray the others.

choices.text: Watch from the rooftops

outcomes.text: You watch how power works when nobody pretends otherwise.
It ends in knives. You see who wins, and how.

events.title: The Dragonarmies Take the Bay
events.scene: 348. Out of the mountains and down the roads from Khur come the dragonarmies, with dragons over the harbour, and Balifor falls in days. The council opens the gates. The soldiers take the warehouses, the ships and anyone who argues.

choices.text: Keep your head down and keep working

outcomes.text: You work the docks under the soldiers' eyes, and learn to be invisible.
You're pressed into loading their ships. You see what they're shipping, and where.

choices.text: Take a boat and run

outcomes.text: You slip out on a fishing boat at night and don't come back until it's over.
You come back, again and again, to smuggle others out.

events.title: Strangers in Flotsam
events.scene: 352. Flotsam is full of the Blue Lady's soldiers, and rumours: a band of strangers, an elf and a big swordsman and a kender among them, was in town looking for a ship, and the Highlord herself was seen in the inn where they stayed. Then a ship called the Perechon slipped out of harbour, and the soldiers turned the town upside down.

choices.text: Help hide whoever the soldiers are looking for

outcomes.text: You hide a frightened man in your cellar for two days. You never learn who he was.
The soldiers search your house and find nothing. It was close.

choices.text: Collect every rumour

outcomes.text: You piece together the story and tell it in taverns for twenty years.
You sell what you heard to a soldier. It doesn't sit well later.

events.title: Fire Over the Bay
events.scene: 386. The great red dragon Malystryx comes to the Bay of Balifor. The savannah burns, the towns burn, and the land around the bay is scorched into a waste of ash and steam. When the smoke clears, the dragon's sorcery has done something to the water too: the fish are dying.

choices.text: Get your people onto the boats

outcomes.text: Three days at sea in a crowded boat. You land on a strange shore with what you're wearing.
You go back for the ones who couldn't reach the boats. You're not sure, afterwards, how you lived.

choices.text: Stay and dig in

outcomes.text: A stone cellar and a wet blanket. You come up into a world of ash.
You live. Too many of your neighbours don't.

events.title: The Dead Bay
events.scene: The bay the town lived on is dead: the red dragon poisoned it, and the nets come up empty or worse. Goblins, half-ogres and bandits have moved into the ash lands behind the town. Every family must decide how to live now.

choices.text: Go into the ash lands for whatever's left

outcomes.text: Old cellars, buried tools, a strongbox nobody came back for. It's enough to live on.
Bandits catch you out there. You get away with your life and nothing else.

choices.text: Work the ships that still come in

outcomes.text: Smugglers and the dragon's own servants still need a port. You learn to deal with both.
One day you take passage on one and don't come back.

events.title: The Port After the War
events.scene: The dragonarmies have left Balifor, and the kender who fought them in the east are coming home as heroes. The port is full of leftover soldiers selling their swords and leftover ships with no flag. Everyone is looking for a new way to get rich.

choices.text: Buy a share in an abandoned ship

outcomes.text: She floats, she sails, she pays. For a few years you're somebody on the waterfront.
She sinks in her first storm, with your money. You learn about inspecting hulls.

choices.text: Hire one of the soldiers as a teacher

outcomes.text: A tired veteran teaches you the sword for a bed and a meal. He's good.
He teaches you a little, then vanishes with the silver.

events.title: The Great Circus
events.scene: The Great Circus of Nethosak, on a day of games: twenty thousand voices, the sand raked smooth, and a challenger in the ring who means to fight his way to a seat on the Supreme Circle. Among minotaurs, any office can be won here, even the emperor's. Your elder has brought you to watch, and asks what you see.

choices.text: Say you see the stronger fighter

outcomes.text: You're right, and your elder nods. You go home with your heart pounding and your mind made up.
The stronger one loses to the cleverer one. Your elder laughs and says that's the lesson.

choices.text: Say you see someone fighting for his house's honour

outcomes.text: Your elder tells you the whole history of that house, and of yours, until the sun goes down.
The fight ends in blood. Your elder says honour costs, always, and watches to see if you look away. You don't.

mark.born_in_servitude.scene: The Great Circus of Nethosak, on a day of games, and you are there because your masters need someone to carry their cushions. Down on the sand, minotaurs fight for honour and office. Sometimes, between bouts, they put slaves in the ring for sport.

events.title: Your First Bout
events.scene: Young minotaurs prove themselves in the ring before they are counted as adults. Your opponent is from a rival house, bigger than you, and grinning. The crowd is small, but your whole house is in it.

choices.text: Fight to win

outcomes.text: You win, on the third exchange, and your house roars. Your opponent's house will remember your name.
You lose, well, still on your feet at the end. That counts for more than winning badly.

choices.text: Fight to outthink him

outcomes.text: You let him tire himself out and take him at the end. Some call it cunning; some call it cowardice.
He's cleverer than he looks. You end up flat on the sand, laughing at yourself, which nobody expects.

region.blood_sea_isles.scene: Young minotaurs prove themselves in the Circus before they are counted as adults, and today is yours. Your opponent is from a rival house, bigger than you, and grinning. The stands of the lesser arena are full, and your whole house is in them.

events.title: The Maelstrom
events.scene: On a clear day from the cliffs you can see it: the great whirlpool in the middle of the Blood Sea, where Istar went down when the gods threw the mountain. The water there is red, they say, with the blood of the drowned. A boat is out there now, too close, and going in circles.

choices.text: Watch until you know what happens

outcomes.text: It breaks free at the last moment, and the sailors aboard row like madmen. You understand the sea better after that.
It goes under. Nobody on the cliffs says anything. You dream about the red water for years.

choices.text: Ask the old sailors about Istar

outcomes.text: They tell you about the Kingpriest, the pride, the burning mountain and the city under the water, still lit, some swear, on certain nights.
One of them shows you a coin of Istar, pulled from a net. He gives it to you, for luck.

events.title: The Raid
events.scene: The ship you crew on has sighted a merchantman running for the coast, low in the water with cargo. The captain calls it a lawful prize; the merchant would call it piracy. Either way the grapples are going over in the next minute, and you're at the rail.

choices.text: Go over first

outcomes.text: The merchant crew surrenders without a fight. Your share of the prize buys your family a winter.
They fight. You come back with a cut across the ribs and a captain who now knows your name.

choices.text: Hold back the ones who want blood

outcomes.text: Nobody dies. The merchant captain looks at you, afterwards, in a way you don't forget.
The crew calls you soft for a season. You decide that's their problem.

culture.saifhum.scene: A minotaur raider has come out of the haze at your ship, grapples ready. Saifhum sailors don't surrender to minotaurs; it's practically the island's only law. The captain is shouting for everyone at the rail, and that includes you.

events.title: The Overseer
events.scene: You were born a slave in a minotaur household. The overseer is not cruel, by minotaur standards, which means he hits only when he has a reason. Today the reason is an older slave who dropped a jar, and the overseer has noticed you watching.

choices.text: Step in and say you dropped it

outcomes.text: The overseer looks at you a long time, and hits you instead, once. Then, oddly, he nods. Minotaurs respect a challenge.
The master hears of it, and puts you to work where courage is useful: the docks, the ships, the dangerous jobs.

choices.text: Look away, and learn how the house really works

outcomes.text: You learn every door, every key and every habit. Someday that will be worth more than courage.
You start, very quietly, to plan how to get out.

events.title: A Matter of Honour
events.scene: Someone has insulted your house in public: a minotaur of another house, who says your grandfather won his place in the Circus by a trick. Among minotaurs there is one answer to that. The whole street is waiting to hear yours.

choices.text: Challenge him, here and now

outcomes.text: You fight in the street, by the old rules. You win, and he apologises, and means it. That is the end of the matter.
You lose, honourably. He withdraws the insult anyway, for the way you fought. Minotaurs are strange that way.

choices.text: Prove him wrong with the records instead

outcomes.text: The Circus keeps records. You find them, and read them out in the same street. He has to laugh, and so do you.
The records show he was right. You keep that to yourself, and carry it.

events.title: The Circus Master's Offer
events.scene: A master of the Circus has watched you, and makes an offer: train under him, fight in the ring, and earn fame, money and perhaps a seat that no birth could give you. Or, he says, refuse, and stay whatever you are now.

choices.text: Train for the Circus

outcomes.text: Years of the sand. You learn every weapon and every trick, and the crowd learns your name.
Years of the sand, and of healers. You win more than you lose, and you lose things you don't get back.
You win your freedom, or your house's honour, in a single famous bout. They still talk about it on the docks.

choices.text: Refuse; there are better ways to win

outcomes.text: He shrugs. The ring has plenty of volunteers.
He tells you that you'll regret it. Some days, you do.

events.title: The Elven Fleet
events.scene: 349. Envoys of the dragon emperor have come to the Supreme Circle with gold and promises, and the islands' ships are going to war on his side. The first order: catch the Silvanesti fleet fleeing west across the sea. Every crew is called.

choices.text: Sail with the hunting ships

outcomes.text: You sail too late. The elven sails are already over the horizon. The captains blame each other for a month.
You catch two stragglers. What happens to the elves aboard is something you don't talk about.

choices.text: Find a reason to stay ashore

outcomes.text: You stay. Some call it cowardice. You call it not being anyone's dog.
With half the fleet at war, someone has to run the trade. You run it, well.

culture.saifhum.scene: 349. The minotaurs have sold their ships to the dragon emperor, and their galleys go hunting an elven fleet to the west. Saifhum's captains meet: stay out of it, warn the elves, or take advantage of the minotaurs' empty harbours.

events.title: Sailing for the Queen
events.scene: 351. Minotaur warriors are wanted in the dragonarmies: the Black wing, the White wing, anyone who pays and lets them fight. Ships leave Nethosak full and come back half-empty. Your house is asked to send someone.

choices.text: Go to war for the dragon emperor

outcomes.text: You fight across half of Ansalon and see things that make the Circus look like a children's game. You come home in 352, when it's all lost.
You are sent south, to an ice castle at the bottom of the world, under an elf highlord. You hate every day of it.

choices.text: Refuse; minotaurs don't serve

outcomes.text: Your elders call it pride and they are proud of it. The war passes your house by.
The house that went instead is honoured; yours is not. It takes a generation to forget.

events.title: The Ship in the Maelstrom
events.scene: 352. Word goes round the harbours: a ship called the Perechon, with a famous half-elf captain and a minotaur mate, was chased by a blue dragon straight into the Maelstrom, and went down. A month later, the same sailors are swearing they've heard it came out the other side.

choices.text: Believe it came out

outcomes.text: If a ship can come out of the Maelstrom, anything can. You start taking bigger risks.
You start charting the Maelstrom's edges from the cliffs, every day, to find out how.

choices.text: Say nothing comes out of the Maelstrom

outcomes.text: You stay well clear of it all your life, and live to tell people so.
You say it in a dockside tavern, and a sailor with a far-off look tells you, very quietly, that you're wrong.

events.title: The Night of Blood
events.scene: 421. Under cover of the great storm that covers all of Ansalon, a general named Hotak de-Droka strikes in a single night: the emperor dead, his supporters dead, their houses burned. By morning, the empire has a new master, and everyone must decide which side of the night they were on.

choices.text: Bow to the new emperor

outcomes.text: Your house is spared, and then favoured. You try not to remember the houses that weren't.
You bow, and the new emperor's protectors watch you anyway. Everyone is watched now.

choices.text: Hide the survivors of the old emperor's houses

outcomes.text: You get a family out on a fishing boat to Saifhum. If anyone finds out, your house will burn too.
Someone talks. You flee the islands with the people you were hiding, and can never go back.

events.title: The Old Emperor
events.scene: Emperor Chot has held the throne a long time, mostly by making sure the Circus never offers him a real challenger. His favourites grow rich; the legions who came home from the war grow angry. In the taverns of Nethosak, people have started to say so, quietly.

choices.text: Seek a place among the emperor's favourites

outcomes.text: Gold, a house above the harbour, and a seat at the Circus near the throne. You try not to listen to the taverns.
You get close enough to see how the throne is really kept. It's worse than the taverns say.

choices.text: Drink with the angry veterans

outcomes.text: They talk about a general who could do better. You remember his name.
Someone reports the conversation. The emperor's guards come asking. You answer carefully.

events.title: Envoys from Sanction
events.scene: Envoys from Sanction have come to Nethosak with chests of steel and promises: an alliance, a share of an empire, a war worth fighting. The Supreme Circle debates for a month while the envoys watch the games.

choices.text: Argue that minotaurs should take the offer

outcomes.text: The Circle agrees, in the end. You are thanked, and you will see what you voted for.
An envoy rewards you privately for your speech. The steel is very good.

choices.text: Argue that minotaurs serve no one

outcomes.text: You lose the vote, and win respect from the old houses.
An envoy marks your name. Years later, that matters.

events.title: The Empire Takes Silvanesti
events.scene: After the Night of Blood the new emperor's fleets sail west and take Silvanesti from the elves, the first green land minotaurs have held in centuries. Families are being chosen to settle there, and soldiers to keep it.

choices.text: Go to settle the new land

outcomes.text: Trees taller than any mast, soil that grows anything. The elves in the woods hate you, with reason.
Settling turns out to mean fighting, every season, against elves who won't leave.

choices.text: Stay on the islands

outcomes.text: Someone has to keep the old ports. You do.
You hear what's done in the new lands, and stop cheering at the docks.

events.title: The Lean Centuries
events.scene: The Blood Sea gives little since Istar drowned: thin fishing, bad timber, and the Maelstrom always turning at the centre. The houses that prosper are the ones whose ships go raiding along the coasts, and this year the emperor's champion calls for more ships.

choices.text: Crew a raiding ship

outcomes.text: A coastal town pays to be left alone. Your share feeds your house all winter.
A storm off Saifhum nearly sinks you. You learn the sea's moods the hard way.

choices.text: Work the island's poor fields instead

outcomes.text: Stony ground and salt wind. You coax a harvest out of it, and the old ones nod.
The raiders' families sneer at farmers. You decide you don't care what they think.

events.title: The Robed Stranger
events.scene: A stranger in a travelling robe stops at the well, and while the bucket comes up she watches the children, then the young people, then you. She asks you to hold out your hand, and lays a smooth grey stone in it. 'Tell me what it feels like.' Her robe, you notice, is a colour that changes when she moves: white, then red, then nearly black.

choices.text: Tell her the truth: it feels warm, and it hums

outcomes.text: She nods slowly. 'The Towers want to know of you.' Within the year a letter comes, and a master who teaches you the first cantrip and the first rule: magic has a price.
She gives you a small book, copied in her own hand, and tells you to learn it by the time she passes this way again. You do.
She takes the stone back and says that those who use magic outside the Towers are hunted as renegades. Then she leaves. You start hiding what you can do.

choices.text: Say it feels like a stone

outcomes.text: She smiles as if you'd told her the truth anyway, and walks on. That night the stone is under your pillow, and you never find out how.
She shrugs and goes. You spend the next ten years wondering what would have happened.

choices.text: Ask her what the colours of her robe mean

outcomes.text: White for the good, red for the balance, black for the rest, she says, and all three for the magic. She stays for supper and talks until the candles are gone.
She tells you about the Test at the Tower, which some don't survive. You can't stop thinking about it.

year<=350.scene: A stranger in a travelling robe stops at the well. People step back from her: magic-users are not loved since the Cataclysm, and the Towers have been burned or abandoned. She watches the young people, then you, and lays a smooth grey stone in your hand. 'Tell me what it feels like.' Her robe changes colour when she moves: white, then red, then nearly black.

events.title: The Spellbook in the Attic
events.scene: Under a loose floorboard, wrapped in oilcloth: a book with a lock, and inside it pages of writing that crawls a little when you look straight at it. On the first page, someone has written a name and the words 'Tower of Wayreth'.

choices.text: Study it in secret, night after night

outcomes.text: One night a word on the page makes the candle flare blue. You don't sleep at all.
Years of it, and you understand only a little. But the little you understand, you understand properly.

choices.text: Take it to someone who might know what it is

outcomes.text: The old apothecary turns pale and says to bury it. Then, at the door, he asks if he can see it again tomorrow.
Your parents burn it in the stove. Your mother cries, and won't say why.

events.title: The Medallion
events.scene: A follower of the new clerics, the ones who came with Elistan and the plainswoman with the blue staff, is passing through. She wears a medallion of a god nobody has prayed to with an answer in three hundred years, and she is looking for anyone who will listen. You listen.

choices.text: Ask her to teach you to pray

outcomes.text: For a month you pray and feel nothing. Then, kneeling by a sick child, you feel something answer. She gives you her own medallion.
She sends you to the nearest new temple, a barn with an altar in it. You stay, and help, and learn the prayers, and wait.

choices.text: Ask her to prove it

outcomes.text: She lays her hand on your old scar and it fades. You stop asking questions for a long while.
She refuses: the gods aren't a trick for the market. You respect that more than any miracle.

choices.text: Walk with her to the next town

outcomes.text: Three towns, then six. You carry her pack and learn the old stories of the gods, and by the end you're telling them yourself.
In the fourth town, followers of a false god throw stones. You stand in front of her. She heals your cut that night.

events.title: The Knight in the Common Room
events.scene: Since the war, the Knights of Solamnia are welcome again in most places, and here is one in the inn's common room: grey-moustached, armour polished thin, eating stew. He says the Orders are taking squires from anywhere now, if their hearts are right. He says it to the room, but he's looking at you.

choices.text: Ask him what the Measure asks of a squire

outcomes.text: He tells you until the fire burns down: honour, the Oath, the Measure, and what it costs. At the end he asks if you'd ride with him in the spring.
He gives you a worn copy of a few chapters of the Measure. You read it until you know it by heart.

choices.text: Ask him where the Knights were in the Cataclysm

outcomes.text: He doesn't get angry. He says: in the wrong place, and they've spent three hundred years paying for it. You don't forget the answer.
The room laughs with you, and he leaves early. You feel worse than he looked.

events.title: The Woman at the Edge of the Wood
events.scene: Everyone knows the old woman at the edge of the wood: she cures warts, finds lost things, and is not invited to weddings. Today she has sent for you, by name. On her table: a cat that isn't asleep, a bowl of water that doesn't reflect the ceiling, and a cup of tea she's already poured.

choices.text: Drink the tea

outcomes.text: In the bottom of the cup there is a voice. It offers to teach you, in return for a favour to be named later. You say yes before you can think.
You see your own face in the water, older, and somewhere far away. She says you have her grandmother's eyes, which is impossible.

choices.text: Leave the tea and ask what she wants

outcomes.text: She wants someone to learn the herbs before she dies. You spend three summers in her garden, and learn more than herbs.
She laughs and lets you go. The cat follows you home, and stays.

events.title: The Smiling Recruiter
events.scene: A well-dressed man with a warm handshake has started holding meetings in a back room: free bread, a lot of talk about a god who rewards the loyal, and very little about what that god wants. Your friend has been going for a month and wants you to come. 'They're good people,' she says, too quickly.

choices.text: Go, for your friend's sake

outcomes.text: The bread is good, the people are kind, and somewhere in the third month you notice you've stopped asking questions. It takes something bad to wake you.
You go, and keep going, and quietly learn who runs it and where the money goes. It's worse than you thought.

choices.text: Refuse, and try to get your friend out

outcomes.text: It takes a year, and you nearly lose her friendship doing it. But she comes out.
She chooses them. One day the meetings stop, and she's gone with them.

events.title: Too Far From Home
events.scene: You followed something (an animal, a sound, an idea) and when you looked around, nothing was familiar any more. The light is going.

choices.text: Climb the highest thing around and look for a sign of home

outcomes.text: From up high you spot chimney smoke and walk back alone, filthy and proud.
The branch gives way. They find you in the morning with a crooked arm and a story.
From up high you see lights where nobody lives. You never told anyone where.

choices.text: Stay put and wait for someone to come

outcomes.text: Voices calling your name before midnight. Nobody scolds; everybody cries.
The one who finds you isn't family. They walk you to the road and vanish before you can thank them.
Nobody comes. You stay awake all night and find the way at sunrise.

place.solace.scene: You followed something into Darken Wood, where no child from Solace should ever go. When you looked around, every tree was the same and the light was going.

culture.plains.scene: You followed an animal's trail past the stones that mark the tribe's land. The grass is taller than you, and the light is going.

region.solamnia.scene: You followed something into the standing wheat, and the wheat on the Solamnic plains is taller than a child and goes on for miles. When you looked around, there was only gold and sky, and the light was going.

events.title: The Fever
events.scene: The fever hasn't broken in days. In the next room the adults argue about whom to send for, and what it will cost.

choices.text: Cling to every spoonful and every story they tell you

outcomes.text: The fever breaks one dawn. You never fall ill the same way again.
You get up after weeks. You spent all that time listening and thinking.
Someone who knows healing sits up the whole night with you and refuses payment.

choices.text: Ask, with what voice you have left, for the healer the neighbour mentioned

outcomes.text: The healer comes, does what they know, and it works.
The "healer" takes the household's savings, and you get better in spite of them.
You recover, but the short breath stays with you for years.

events.title: The Thing That Shone in the Mud
events.scene: After the rain something glints in the mud: a piece of worked metal, older than anyone you know, with symbols nobody uses any more.

choices.text: Hide it and tell no one

outcomes.text: You move the hiding place three times. It is the first thing that is only yours.
An adult finds it, takes it, and never speaks of it again. You never forgot.
At night the thing grows warm in your hand. You keep it anyway.

choices.text: Run with it to an adult you trust

outcomes.text: The adult knows the symbols and tells you, quietly, about the world before the Cataclysm.
The family sells it. Nobody goes cold that winter.
The adult goes pale, buries it again and forbids you to go back there.

events.title: The Biggest Kid on the Street
events.scene: {rival.name} is bigger, older, and has decided you are this season's target. Today they are waiting on the path you have to take.

choices.text: Face them head-on, whoever ends up hurt

outcomes.text: You hit first and hard. They never wait on that path again.
You take a beating, but they bleed too. Next day they pretend not to see you.
The fight settles nothing. It becomes a feud that lasts years.

choices.text: Talk your way around them with a well-told lie

outcomes.text: They believe every word. You find out you can do that.
They see through the lie, and things get worse for a while.
They laugh at your nerve. Against all odds, you end up friends.

choices.text: Tell an adult and live with being called a tattletale

outcomes.text: The adult sorts it out. The other children ignore you for a while.
The adult tells you to learn to handle it. You learn.

events.title: Fire in the House
events.scene: You wake to smoke. The adults are shouting for each other. There is a moment when you could run out the door, and in it you remember what was left inside.

choices.text: Go back for whoever or whatever was left

outcomes.text: You come out coughing, with what you went for in your arms. People talk about it for years.
You make it, and pay with the skin of your arm.
Someone drags you out before you get there. You never knew if you would have made it.

choices.text: Get out and shout for help until your voice is gone

outcomes.text: The neighbours form a bucket line. Half the house is saved because of you.
Nobody is hurt, and nothing is left. The family starts over.

events.title: The Storyteller
events.scene: A traveller trades stories for supper. Knights, dragons nobody sees any more, cities across the sea. The adults laugh. You can't.

choices.text: Stay to the end and ask every question

outcomes.text: The traveller draws the world in the dust for you. You memorise every line.
The traveller teaches you an old song. You still know every verse.
The traveller looks at you for a long time and says something that only made sense years later.

choices.text: Retell it all to the other children the next day, with better details

outcomes.text: They come back the next day asking for more. You make up what's missing.
They call you a liar. You keep telling stories, just to fewer people.

events.title: The Wounded Animal
events.scene: Behind the shed there's a hurt animal, too big to be a pet and too frightened to run. The adults would say leave it.

choices.text: Look after it in secret, with scraps from the table

outcomes.text: It heals and leaves. Sometimes you think you see it in the distance.
It heals and doesn't leave. The family gives up arguing.
It dies on the third night. You bury it alone.

choices.text: Fetch someone who knows what to do

outcomes.text: They show you how to clean a wound and let you do the rest.
They do what they think is right, quickly. You understand, and take a while to forgive.

events.title: Light Fingers at the Fair
events.scene: In the press of the fair you see it clearly: a child you know lifts a trader's purse. They notice you saw. The trader hasn't noticed anything.

choices.text: Look the other way

outcomes.text: Later they turn up with half the coins and a nod.
Nothing happens. For days you wait for someone to come asking.

choices.text: Warn the trader

outcomes.text: The trader gets the purse back and gives you a coin, and tells you to look them up when you're grown.
The child is beaten in front of everyone. They and their friends never forget your face.

choices.text: Bump into the trader to give them time to vanish

outcomes.text: It works. Next day they ask you to run with the group.
You're the one who gets grabbed. Your family pays for the loss and the shame.

events.title: It Happened Again
events.scene: You were angry, or scared, and the candle lit itself. This time you weren't alone: someone saw, and they're staring at you.

choices.text: Swear it was the wind

outcomes.text: They choose to believe you. You learn not to feel too much around other people.
The rumour spreads. Some doors start closing when you arrive.

choices.text: Try to do it again, on purpose

outcomes.text: The flame obeys. The witness promises to keep it secret, and does.
Nothing happens, however hard you try. They laugh at you, and it's a relief.
The flame leaps higher than it should. Nobody is hurt, and nobody laughs.

events.title: The Pack Behind the Door
events.scene: {sibling.name}, who always looked after you, has packed a bag and hidden it behind the door. Only you know. Their eyes beg you to say nothing.

choices.text: Help them slip away unseen

outcomes.text: They vanish down the road before sunrise, promising to send word.
Before leaving, they give you the only thing of value they owned.

choices.text: Wake your parents

outcomes.text: They stay, and barely speak to you for a year.
The row wakes the street. They leave anyway, in daylight, slamming the door.

choices.text: Ask to go along

outcomes.text: They laugh, ruffle your hair and say they'll come back for you. They don't say when.
They take you as far as the next village and send you home with a carter. Best three days of your childhood.

events.title: Cold Water
events.scene: The bank gives way. The water is colder and stronger than it looked from above, and the child who fell in with you can't swim.

choices.text: Hold on to the other child and kick with everything you have

outcomes.text: You reach the bank clinging to each other. They never forgot.
An adult jumps in and pulls you both out. You owe them for that.
The current carries you both far downstream. You come out alive, with a fear of water that takes years to fade.

choices.text: Grab a root and scream for help

outcomes.text: People come running and pull you both out. They praise your cool head.
They get you out first, and the other child only just. Their mother looks at you differently ever since.

culture.plains.scene: The riverbank gives way in the flood. The water is colder and stronger than it looked, and the other child from the tribe who fell in with you can't swim.

events.title: What Is Said Quietly
events.scene: You were meant to be asleep. Through the crack of the door the adults talk quietly about something that happened before you were born, and your name comes up.

choices.text: Stay and listen to the end

outcomes.text: You hear it all. From then on you look at your family knowing what it hides.
You hear half and fill in the rest wrongly for years.
The door opens. Instead of scolding, they tell you everything, and ask you to carry it with them.

choices.text: Next day, ask them straight out

outcomes.text: After a long silence, they tell you.
They deny everything, badly. You learn to tell when someone is lying.

events.title: Festival Day
events.scene: At the harvest festival there's a contest just for children, with a real prize. Everyone will be watching.

choices.text: Compete to win

outcomes.text: You win. For one whole day everyone knows your name.
You come second, and find out you hate coming second.
You fall in front of everyone. You get up and finish anyway.

choices.text: Find a way nobody will notice

outcomes.text: You win and nobody notices. The prize weighs more than it should.
They notice. The prize goes to another child, and the story stays.

choices.text: Drop out to help a friend win

outcomes.text: Your friend wins, and knows why.
Neither of you wins. You split a sweet and laugh about it for years.

culture.plains.scene: At the gathering of the tribes there's a race just for children, and the winner receives a feather from an elder's hands. Every village will be watching.

events.title: The New Word
events.scene: Someone has arrived claiming to speak for the old gods, the true ones. The adults, burned by the Seekers, listen with folded arms. The stranger lays a hand on a sick man, and you are close by.

choices.text: Get closer to see

outcomes.text: You see the wound close. Nothing the adults say afterwards undoes that.
The stranger notices you and answers your questions as if you were grown.
Nothing happens that day. You're left with the question.

choices.text: Stay behind the adults, arms folded like theirs

outcomes.text: You learn early to ask for proof before believing.
Even from a distance, something of it stays with you.

culture.plains.scene: A woman of the tribe has come back bearing the name of Mishakal and the power to heal. The elders remember what it cost to believe new things. She lays her hand on a sick man, and you are close by.

region.solamnia.scene: A cleric in white has come from Palanthas, speaking for Paladine, the god of the Knights. The adults remember who was blamed for the Cataclysm and listen with folded arms. The cleric lays a hand on a sick man, and you are close by.

region.kalaman.scene: A cleric of Kiri-Jolith has come down the Vingaard with the army, and preaches in the fish market. The adults remember three hundred years of silent temples and listen with folded arms. The cleric lays a hand on a sick fisherman, and you are close by.

region.goodlund.scene: A kender has come home from the war saying she is a cleric now, of Branchala, and everybody wants to see. Kender are never short of stories, so the grown-ups are politely doubtful. She lays a hand on a sick old kender, and you are close by.

region.thorbardin.scene: A priest of Reorx speaks in the Valley of the Thanes, the first whose prayers have been answered since the Cataclysm. The old dwarves fold their arms; they have kept the shrines for three hundred years without an answer. The priest lays a hand on a sick miner, and you are close by.

region.qualinesti.scene: An elf who went into exile a doubter has come home a cleric of E'li, the god the humans call Paladine. The elders remember that the gods came back to a human first, and listen with folded arms. She lays a hand on a sick child, and you are close by.

region.southern_ergoth.scene: A cleric has come to the island: a healer, they say, of the old gods, the true ones. The adults have heard such things before and listen with folded arms. The stranger lays a hand on a sick hunter, and you are close by.

events.title: The Compulsory Sermon
events.scene: Everyone in the square to hear the Seeker. He speaks of the new gods and of those who disobey. His gaze rests a moment on your family.

choices.text: Stand still and draw no attention

outcomes.text: His gaze moves on. You learn the art of not being noticed.
That week the temple guards visit your house. They take little and leave fear.

choices.text: Ask aloud the question nobody asks

outcomes.text: The square holds its breath. The Seeker laughs awkwardly and changes the subject.
Your father pays a fine and you get a hiding. The question was never answered.

events.title: Higher
events.scene: The bet was who could climb highest. You're winning when you hear your friend below say they can't get down.

choices.text: Climb down and help, and lose the bet

outcomes.text: You come down slowly, holding each other up.
You both fall the last stretch. You break their fall with your shoulder.

choices.text: Reach the top first; they can wait

outcomes.text: From the top you can see further than you thought the world went.
Your friend falls while you climb. The leg heals; the friendship takes longer.
You're the one who falls, from high up. You spend a season in bed staring at the ceiling.

place.solace.scene: The bet was who could climb highest in the vallenwood, above the last walkways. You're winning when you hear your friend below say they can't get down.

events.title: The Friend You Weren't Allowed
events.scene: Your best friend is from a people your folk don't want around. Today the adults found out, and said in no uncertain terms that it's over.

choices.text: Keep the friendship going in secret

outcomes.text: You invent signals and hiding places. The friendship lasts your whole childhood.
You're caught again. Your friend's family moves away. You'd learned their language by then.

choices.text: Stand up for your friend in front of everyone

outcomes.text: Grudgingly, the adults give in. Your friend starts eating at your table.
You're punished, and you don't take back a word.

choices.text: Obey

outcomes.text: You stop seeking them out. They pass you in the street without looking.
Years later it's your friend who seeks you out, without bitterness.

people.half_elf.scene: This time the people nobody wants around are yours. Your best friend's family found out who their child spends time with, and said in no uncertain terms that it's over.

events.title: People in Hiding
events.scene: There are people hiding where nobody should be: two thin adults, one of them hurt. They signal you to keep quiet. Someone is looking for them.

choices.text: Bring food and say nothing

outcomes.text: They're gone on the third night. They leave a thank-you scratched into the wood, and a name.
While they wait, one of them teaches you something no child in the village knows.
They leave in the night taking more than you gave.

choices.text: Run and tell the adults

outcomes.text: They're taken away. You never found out what they had done.
To your surprise, it's your own family who hides them best.

events.title: Someone Notices You
events.scene: {mentor.name} has worked in the same corner for longer than you've been alive. Today they stopped, watched you fiddling with their things, and instead of shooing you away, asked a question.

choices.text: Come back every day to learn

outcomes.text: You have a knack. They start saving the small jobs for you.
You have no knack for it at all, and they like you anyway. The talks are worth more than the trade.
One day they show you what they really do when the door is shut.

choices.text: Answer, then run back to the street

outcomes.text: The street teaches other things, faster.
Months later you come back of your own accord. They don't mention the delay.

events.title: The Long Winter
events.scene: The larder won't last until spring, and everyone in the house knows it. Nobody says so, but the adults' plates grow emptier so yours can stay full.

choices.text: Go out and look for food yourself

outcomes.text: You learn where the land hides food in the cold. The household gets through the winter.
What you bring home wasn't found, and nobody at home asks.
You come back empty-handed with frostbitten fingers.

choices.text: Secretly pass part of your share to whoever is worse off

outcomes.text: They notice, and nobody says a word. Nobody treated you as a child after that.
A neighbour notices and leaves a sack of grain at the door, with no note.

events.title: The Old Woman Who Knew Your Name
