events.scene: An old woman you've never seen calls you by name in the middle of the street. She says she remembers the day you were born, and has something to tell you, if you want to hear it.

choices.text: Listen

outcomes.text: She tells you three things. Two have already happened.
She doesn't speak of the future. She speaks of someone you have yet to meet, and asks you to be patient with them.
What she says makes no sense. The adults confirm it: she's just an old woman.

choices.text: Run away

outcomes.text: You never see her again. For years you wonder what it was.
She shouts one sentence after you, and you hear it whether you want to or not.

choices.text: First ask what she wants in return

outcomes.text: She laughs until she coughs and says you'll go far. Then she says what she came to say.
She asks a small favour, to be repaid one day. You agree without knowing what you agreed to.

events.title: It Must Have Fallen In
events.scene: You find, at the bottom of your pouch, a silver thimble, a key, and a little carved horse. You have no idea how they got there. The key, at least, belongs to the baker, who is shouting in the street that someone has locked him out of his own shop.

choices.text: Run and give the baker his key: he must have dropped it

outcomes.text: He's so relieved he gives you a bun. You decide that finding things is a public service, and keep doing it.
He looks at you, at the key, at you again. From then on he counts his spoons when you come in.

choices.text: Keep the horse; nobody's asked about the horse

outcomes.text: The horse becomes your favourite thing in the world for a year. Then you find something better.
It turns out to belong to a human child visiting with her trader father. She cries. You give it back and feel strange for a week.

choices.text: Draw a map of everywhere you've been today, to work out where they came from

outcomes.text: The map doesn't solve anything, but it's a very good map. It's the first of hundreds.
The map shows you passed the baker's, the thimble-maker's and the toy stall, in that order. You return all three, and the toy-seller hires you to find things people lose.

region.goodlund.scene: You find, at the bottom of your pouch, a silver thimble, a key, and a little carved horse. You have no idea how they got there. The key, at least, belongs to the baker on Something Street, who is shouting that someone has locked him out of his own shop. In Kendermore this happens most mornings.

events.title: The Kender Moot
events.scene: A moot: kender from three villages in one meadow, with games, stories, dares and a great deal of noise. The young ones show off their new skills, and the old ones pretend to judge. This year there's a contest for the best trick of the season.

choices.text: Show off your best trick with the sling

outcomes.text: You knock an apple off an elder's head, and the cheer is the loudest of the day. The elder eats the apple.
You knock the elder's hat off instead. He laughs harder than anyone. You practise for a year.

choices.text: Tell the tallest story of the moot

outcomes.text: Your story involves a woolly mammoth, three wizards and a cousin. Somebody's grandmother swears it's true.
A girl from Legup tells a taller one. You spend the rest of the day finding out how she did it.

choices.text: Wander off to see what's past the meadow

outcomes.text: A ruined tower, a fox's den and a hole that goes down further than you can see. You are late for supper by a day.
You get properly lost, for the first time. It's wonderful.

events.title: The Street That Ends in a Wall
events.scene: Kendermore was laid out by kender, which means that several streets end in a wall, one goes in a circle, and two have the same name. A human trader has been lost in them since breakfast. He's offering a whole silver piece to anyone who can get him to the Council Hall.

choices.text: Guide him there, the direct way

outcomes.text: You get him there by noon. He pays, and asks you to be his guide every time he comes. He comes twice a year.
You take him the interesting way. He sees most of Kendermore and pays you two silvers to stop.

choices.text: Sell him a map instead

outcomes.text: You draw it on the spot. It's accurate, which surprises him and slightly surprises you.
Your map is accurate, but it's of a different part of the city. He's found two days later, cheerful, having learnt a great deal.

events.title: The Taunt
events.scene: A big human lad has been throwing rocks at a dog outside the inn. He's twice your size, and a crowd is gathering. Your aunt once told you that the most dangerous weapon a kender has is the truth, said at exactly the wrong moment.

choices.text: Tell him, in front of everyone, exactly what he is

outcomes.text: He goes red, then purple, then charges, and trips over the dog's water bowl into the horse trough. The crowd will never let him forget it.
He goes purple and chases you through four alleys and over a roof. You get away, mostly, and the dog gets away entirely.

choices.text: Just take the dog and walk off with it

outcomes.text: Nobody stops you. The dog follows you for the next nine years.
He stops you. You bite him. You and the dog both get away bruised.

year>=350.scene: A dragonarmy soldier has been throwing rocks at a dog outside the inn, laughing with his friends. He's twice your size and has a sword. Your aunt once told you that the most dangerous weapon a kender has is the truth, said at exactly the wrong moment.

events.title: The Arranged Match
events.scene: Kendermore has laws, which surprises everyone who isn't a kender, and one of them is about marriage: families arrange matches between grown kender, and the arrangement is written down at the Council Hall. Your parents have just told you they've found you one. The other kender is very nice, and has never once stopped talking.

choices.text: Agree; it might be an adventure

outcomes.text: It turns out you like each other enormously. You're promised, with a date set for whenever you're both back.
You're promised, and you both privately decide to go on very long journeys first.

choices.text: Run away before the date is set

outcomes.text: You're over the hills before anyone notices. Somewhere in Kendermore there is a piece of paper with your name on it, waiting.
The council sends a bounty hunter, a human with a sense of humour, who catches you at the border and lets you go if you promise to write.

choices.text: Argue the law in front of the council

outcomes.text: You find a clause nobody's read in sixty years. The arrangement is void. The council is delighted; nobody's done that before.
You lose, gloriously, after four hours. You're still promised, but now everyone knows who you are.

events.title: Your First Hoopak
events.scene: Old Uncle Somebody carves you a hoopak: a staff of springy willow, forked at the top for a sling, shod with copper at the foot. Whirl it and it moans like the wind; brace it and it vaults you over a stream; load it and it throws a stone further than you can see.

choices.text: Practise until you can hit a crow on the wing

outcomes.text: By the end of the summer you can. You decide you'd rather not, and hit pinecones instead.
You turn out to be better at vaulting with it than shooting. Fences are no longer a problem.

choices.text: Learn to make it sing

outcomes.text: You can make it moan like a ghost, which is useful at night in a strange town, and drives dogs and sentries mad.
You find three notes in it that nobody else can. You play them at the moot and an old kender cries.

events.title: The Ruins
events.scene: Not far from Kendermore are the Ruins: the bones of an old city that was there before the kender, which kender have been exploring for three hundred years without running out of it. Today you and two friends find a stair nobody has been down before. You're nearly sure.

choices.text: Go first

outcomes.text: A hall of broken statues, and on the wall an inscription you copy carefully, and later find nobody can read.
The third step drops away. You fall into a dark room and break an arm, and find a ring on a skeleton's finger. You call it even.

choices.text: Map it properly, one room at a time

outcomes.text: It takes a summer. Your map of the lower Ruins is copied by every kender who goes down after you.
Your map shows the stair should go somewhere it doesn't. You decide to find out where, some day.

events.title: Wanderlust
events.scene: It comes the way it came to your parents and theirs: one morning the road outside looks different. Every horizon itches. You can't sleep for thinking of places you haven't been, which is nearly all of them. Every kender knows what this is.

choices.text: Pack a pouch and go, today

outcomes.text: You're three hills away by sunset, whistling. Your family waves; they knew.
You go, and forget to say goodbye to someone. You'll write. You probably won't.

choices.text: Wait; someone at home needs you

outcomes.text: You stay a season, then a year. The itch doesn't go away; it just waits with you.
You last until midsummer, then leave a note on the table and go in the night.

events.title: The Mapmaker
events.scene: An old kender mapmaker, back from sixty years of wandering with a pack full of maps of everywhere, needs someone young to carry the pack and finish the maps she hasn't got to. She has seen yours. She says they're nearly good.

choices.text: Shoulder the pack

outcomes.text: Years of roads, coasts and ruins, measured and drawn. You learn that the world is bigger than any map, which is the point.
She cares more about getting there than drawing it. You learn to live off the land in nine countries.
She dies in the third year, peacefully, in a nice inn. You inherit the pack and every unfinished map.

choices.text: Say you'd rather make your own maps

outcomes.text: She laughs and says that's the right answer. She gives you a pen.
You watch her go and wonder for years where she went.

events.title: The Dragonarmies Come to Goodlund
events.scene: The dragonarmies have taken Nordmaar and Balifor, and now they come into Goodlund: columns on the roads, dragons over the woods, soldiers in Kendermore's crooked streets looking for someone in charge. The kender are, for once, not sure whether to be curious or frightened, and choose curious.

choices.text: Go and get a good look at the soldiers

outcomes.text: You see a draconian up close and ask it several questions. It doesn't answer any. You write them all down.
A soldier chases you off. You go back the next day with a hoopak, which is how most kender resistance started.

choices.text: Help your family hide in the woods

outcomes.text: Weeks in the woods with half the village. It's almost a holiday, until the smoke from Kendermore.
When you come back the house has been searched and everything worth anything is gone. Kender know how that feels, now.

events.title: The Grand Marshal
events.scene: The Black Wing holds Kendermore. Against it, small bands of kender who have never organised anything in their lives, and one who has: Kronin Thistleknot, quiet and deadly, who has gathered the bands into a resistance. The kender council has made him Grand Marshal. He needs eyes, hands and very good shots.

choices.text: Join the Grand Marshal's bands

outcomes.text: Two years of raids, ambushes and vanishing. The Black Wing comes to dread the sound of hoopaks in the trees.
You learn what it costs. A friend who laughed at everything doesn't come back from a raid on the supply wagons.

choices.text: Make the occupiers' lives a misery in your own way

outcomes.text: Missing boots, missing keys, missing sentries' trousers, insults at the worst possible moment. The officers start drinking.
They catch you with an officer's seal. You're in a cell for a month, until the cell door is found open.

events.title: The Kender Who Saved the World
events.scene: Every kender in Ansalon has heard it by now: a kender walked with the Heroes of the Lance, all the way to the Dark Queen's temple, and smashed a dragon orb, and came back. Every kender has also met someone who knew him. Tonight a stranger at the inn claims to be his cousin.

choices.text: Believe every word

outcomes.text: You decide that if a kender can save the world, so can you, possibly by Tuesday.
The stranger turns out to have actually met him, once, and tells you one small true thing about him that nobody else knows.

choices.text: Tell a better one

outcomes.text: Yours has two dragons and a moon in it. The stranger buys you a drink out of professional respect.
Yours is better, and you point out three holes in his on the way. The whole inn applauds, and he leaves, sulking.

events.title: Soldiers in Balifor
events.scene: Kender coming home from Balifor have stories even for kender: soldiers drilling outside the port, Khurish horsemen, and envoys from somewhere called Sanction buying up every ship. Kendermore holds a meeting about it, which turns into a party, which is how most meetings in Kendermore end.

choices.text: Go and see for yourself

outcomes.text: You see the soldiers. You also 'find' a very interesting map in an officer's tent.
You're chased out of the camp with a soldier's helmet, which you keep.

choices.text: Go to the party

outcomes.text: It is a very good party. You will remember it later, when things are less fun.
Halfway through, you notice the oldest kender in the room isn't smiling.

events.title: The Red Dragon Comes
events.scene: 386. The great red dragon Malystryx comes to Goodlund. Kendermore burns; the woods burn; the land itself is torn up and scorched into a waste. Riverwind of the plains leads an army of kender against her and dies. Thousands of kender die with him. Some of those who live through it have lost something no kender ever had to lose before: they feel fear.

choices.text: March with Riverwind's kender

outcomes.text: You live. When it's over you find you are afraid, for the first time in your life, of almost everything.
You're beside him when he falls. You carry his last words west, to his daughters.

choices.text: Get the little ones out

outcomes.text: You lead a line of kender children west, singing so they won't hear the screaming. It works, mostly.
You get them out. Somewhere on the road, you stop being able to laugh, for a long time.

events.title: Life at the Edge of the Desolation
events.scene: Goodlund is the Desolation now: scorched rock, steaming vents, strange beasts the dragon has bred, and her mountain lair on the horizon. The kender who stayed live in camps at its edges, and the afflicted ones among them flinch at every shadow.

choices.text: Go into the Desolation for what's left

outcomes.text: You find a kender treasure-cache, intact under the ash. It feels like robbing your own grandmother, and it feeds the camp.
One of the dragon's beasts finds you. You outrun it, barely, and leave half your pack behind.

choices.text: Look after the afflicted

outcomes.text: Kender who are afraid are like children who are old. You learn great patience.
Caring for them, you catch a little of their fear. It never quite leaves.

events.title: The Red Dragon Falls
events.scene: 421. The news crosses Ansalon like a shout: Malystryx is dead, killed by the girl Mina who serves the One God. In the Desolation camps the kender don't know whether to celebrate who died or fear who killed her. Being kender, they celebrate first.

choices.text: Celebrate

outcomes.text: The first real party in thirty-five years. Even the afflicted dance, a little.
You and three friends go to look at the empty lair. You come back with a scale and a very long story.

choices.text: Wonder who could kill a dragon like that

outcomes.text: You're right to wonder. You keep your pack ready.
Nobody wants to hear it. Worrying, in a kender, is not a social skill.

events.title: The Wanderer Comes Home
events.scene: An ancient kender walks into Kendermore after fifty years away, with a pack of maps of the world as it was before the Cataclysm's aftershocks settled: coasts that moved, cities that sank, roads that end in the sea. The whole town comes to hear him, and stays three days.

choices.text: Copy his maps

outcomes.text: You copy every one, by candlelight. Half of them are wrong now. That makes them more interesting, not less.
He gives you one, the best one, and says you'll know when to use it.

choices.text: Ask about the places that aren't there any more

outcomes.text: He tells you about a city of white towers that sank under a red sea. You dream about it for a year.
Half his stories are invented, and you can tell which half. You tell them better anyway.

events.title: The Friend Who Is Afraid
events.scene: Your best friend in the camp is an afflicted kender: since the red dragon came, she's afraid of the dark, of strangers, of the sound of wings. Today the other children are going to explore an old burned house in the Desolation, and she won't come, and she won't say why.

choices.text: Stay behind with her

outcomes.text: You spend the day inventing a game that has no frightening parts. She laughs for the first time in a month.
She tells you what she saw in 386. You don't understand all of it. You understand enough.

choices.text: Go, and bring her back something brave

outcomes.text: You bring her a dragon's scale from the ruins. She keeps it under her pillow, and sleeps better.
Something in the ruins chases you all home. Now you know a little of what she feels.

events.title: The Dragon's Creatures
events.scene: The red dragon breeds creatures in her Desolation: things with too many legs, wrong colours and clever eyes. One has started taking goats from the camp's edge. The elders want someone to follow its tracks back to wherever it sleeps.

choices.text: Follow the tracks

outcomes.text: You find its den, and what it was guarding: eggs. You smash them, and run.
The tracks lead in circles. Then you realise it was tracking you.

choices.text: Build a trap at the camp's edge

outcomes.text: The trap works. The creature is horrible up close. Half the camp comes to look, from a safe distance.
It steals the bait and leaves the trap sprung, neatly. You've never been so insulted by an animal.

events.title: The Serpent God
events.scene: All Haven talks of is the new cult: a god in the shape of a serpent who appears in person to the faithful and heals those who pay. The queues go round the block. Someone close to you wants to take a sick relative there.

choices.text: Go along and see with your own eyes

outcomes.text: The serpent appears, huge, amid smoke and screams. You leave not knowing what you saw, and with a lighter purse.
You notice the wires, the smoke, the helper behind the curtain. It's theatre, and good theatre.

choices.text: Try to talk them out of it

outcomes.text: You convince them. The sick one gets better, or doesn't, by the usual means, and the money stays home.
They go anyway and come back devout. For months, you're the unbeliever of the house.

events.title: What the Refugees Say
events.scene: People are arriving from the north and east with everything they own on a cart. They speak of armies, of cities taken, and of things with wings. The Seekers say not to listen: they're beggars, and beggars lie.

choices.text: Sit with them and hear it all

outcomes.text: The details match too well from one to the next to be made up. You start preparing without telling anyone.
You help a family settle. They teach you how to flee a city in an hour.

choices.text: Get on with life; the north is far away

outcomes.text: You get on with life. When the war comes, it comes without warning for those who wouldn't listen.
You repeat to the temple what the refugees are saying. They're gone from town that same week.

events.title: The Day the Trees Burned
events.scene: The dragons come from the east at dusk. The vallenwoods, which held Solace aloft for three hundred years, burn like torches. Below, the army is waiting for whoever comes down.

choices.text: Stay and get people out of their houses

outcomes.text: You get three people off a burning walkway before soldiers with scales seize you.
A beam falls. You wake on the ground, your back raw, in a line of prisoners.
In the confusion you lead a group along the lake shore into the brush. Looking back, you see the red sky.

choices.text: Run for the forest without looking back

outcomes.text: You spend the winter in hiding, eating what you find, listening to patrols go by.
The forest was already surrounded. You're in the prisoners' line before dawn.

events.title: The New Masters of the Town
events.scene: The Red Army came in with no resistance worth the name. The priests of the false gods were given a choice: serve the Queen of Darkness or die in the square. For the rest of the town the choice is smaller, and daily.

choices.text: Keep your head down and get through it

outcomes.text: You work, keep quiet, and learn not to look a soldier in the eye. You come out whole, and without pride.
Keeping your head down isn't enough: your name goes on a list and you're taken south in a caravan.

choices.text: Do what you can against them, in secret

outcomes.text: Messages, food for those in hiding, a cartwheel loosened at the right moment. You're part of something.
A neighbour informs on you. The slave caravan has room for one more.
One night it goes beyond messages: there's a dead soldier in an alley, and it was you.

choices.text: Make yourself useful to the occupiers

outcomes.text: Your work for them puts food on the table and takes names off lists. The neighbours only see the first part.
You're useful until you're not. When the caravan leaves for the south, you're on it with the rest.

culture.hill.scene: The Red Army took the lowland towns and sent word to the hill villages to hand over iron, coal and hands. Whoever refuses is taken. For your people, the choice is small and daily.

events.title: The Village That Is No More
events.scene: The smoke is visible two days away. When the scouts return, they can't say what they saw at Qué-Shu. Your village's elders argue all night: fight, flee, or hide in the mountains.

choices.text: Go there, to know

outcomes.text: You see it. Melted stone, posts, and the silence of a place where hundreds lived. You never sleep the same way again.
Among the ruins you find someone alive, hidden in a well. You carry them on your back to your village.

choices.text: Help take your people to the mountains

outcomes.text: The tribe gets through the winter in caves, hungry and alive. You learn to carry the old and hush the children.
A patrol catches the column. You're among those who stay behind to hold the pass.

events.title: The Southern Road
events.scene: Cages on wheels, hauled towards the mines of Pax Tharkas. The guards are hobgoblins and worse. In your cage there's an old man who never stops talking and a child who never speaks.

choices.text: Try to escape on the way

outcomes.text: A wheel breaks, a guard is distracted, and you run. Forest elves find you before the soldiers do.
They catch you within the hour. The punishment is public, so the others will learn.

choices.text: Look after the child and save your strength

outcomes.text: At the mines they separate men, women and children. You memorise the child's face for the day you can search.
The chatterbox notices what you do and says, very seriously, that kindness is the only magic that never fails. Then he's gone.

events.title: The Fortress Opens
events.scene: Months in the mines. Then one morning, shouting in the corridors, gates thrown open, and a handful of strangers saying it's now or never. Outside, hundreds of people and the mountains, with the army behind.

choices.text: Help organise the escape

outcomes.text: You carry, count heads, break up fights. In the hidden valley, people come to you when there's a decision to make.
You stay among the last, pushing the slow ones. You see up close those who freed you, and they're younger and more tired than the songs will say.

choices.text: Think only of getting out alive

outcomes.text: You make it. You spend the winter as a refugee among the mountain dwarves, who don't like you and shelter you anyway.
You make it. Someone who left the mines beside you doesn't.

events.title: The Empty Forest
events.scene: The Speaker has decided: Qualinesti will be abandoned before the army arrives. Ships wait on the coast to carry a whole people into exile. Qualinost, of rose quartz and gardens, will be left to the dragons.

choices.text: Board with your people

outcomes.text: You watch the coast disappear. In Southern Ergoth, your people build a refugee city and learn to live on little.
In exile you see your people treat the wild elves there as servants. You don't forget, and don't entirely forgive.

choices.text: Stay behind, with those covering the retreat

outcomes.text: You spend the war in the occupied forest, in groups of three, striking and vanishing.
Cut off from your people, you end up fighting beside humans escaped from the mines. You find more courage in them than you were taught to expect.

events.title: Hundreds at the Gate
events.scene: There are hundreds of starving humans begging Thorbardin for shelter, fled from the mines of Pax Tharkas. Among your people the argument is old: the last time someone asked for shelter at that gate, dwarf fought dwarf.

choices.text: Speak in favour of sheltering them

outcomes.text: Yours is one voice among many, and the decision is made. You're set to watch the guests, and end up teaching some of them to work stone.
The refugees come in, and your people don't forget which side you spoke for.

choices.text: Speak against; human troubles are humans' business

outcomes.text: You lose the argument and stand your watch grudgingly. By winter's end you find yourself sharing a pipe with one of them.
You lose the argument and don't change your mind. When the war ends and they leave, you check the locks.

events.title: The Reckoning
events.scene: The war has ended, far away, and the occupiers are gone. Now the town wants to know who did what. There's a list of names nailed up in the square, a rope, and a crowd.

choices.text: Ask for trials instead of the rope

outcomes.text: To your surprise, someone older backs you. There are trials, slow and imperfect, and nobody hangs that night.
They jeer you. The rope does its work. Years later, one or two of those who jeered come to say you were right.

choices.text: Say aloud the name of someone you saw collaborate

outcomes.text: The name was right, and the guilt was real. That doesn't make the memory lighter.
Later you learn the person was feeding the occupiers information to get other names off the lists.

choices.text: Stay home with the door shut

outcomes.text: Someone you once got off a list speaks for you. Your family is spared, and marked.
Your family is given a week to leave town.

events.title: Playing in the Rubble
events.scene: The whole town is a building site, and for the children that's a playground. Under a fallen wall, you and the others find something the soldiers left behind.

choices.text: Keep it

outcomes.text: It's a soldier's short sword, serrated. You hide it on the roof and practise in secret.
It's a badge with a five-headed dragon. An adult sees it, goes white, and explains what it meant.
It's a skull that isn't human. You never play on that side again.

choices.text: Call an adult

outcomes.text: The adult takes it away and, on the way, tells you for the first time what they did during the occupation.
The adult takes it away without a word. You understand there are questions that generation doesn't answer.

events.title: The Chief's Daughter Has Returned
events.scene: Goldmoon and Riverwind have come back to the plains to gather what's left of their people. They bring an ancient goddess and new ideas. Half the village welcomes them as saviours; the other half remembers that Riverwind's family were once branded heretics and driven out by their own tribe.

choices.text: Stand with them

outcomes.text: You hear Goldmoon speak and watch her hands at work. The faith of the plains has a name now.
Riverwind needs young people to patrol the plains. You learn from the quietest man you've ever known.

choices.text: Stand with those who defend the old ways

outcomes.text: You learn the ancestors' rites from those who still know them, while the world changes around you.
The village splits. Your family goes with those who leave to found another camp, further away.

events.title: War in the North Again
events.scene: Traders bring news that the Blue Lady has led what's left of her army against Palanthas, in the north, with a dead knight among her troops, and that a black-robed wizard born in Solace attempted something nobody can explain. The war, the adults say quietly, could come back.

choices.text: Take the fear seriously

outcomes.text: Your house gets a hiding place and a bag packed and ready. The habit stays for life.
You dream of the dead knight for weeks. Then you start asking what makes a dead man walk.

choices.text: Want to know everything

outcomes.text: You chase every traveller for details, and put the whole story together better than the adults.
It's the wizard part you can't shake: someone born nearby, who went so far and so deep.

events.title: Those Who Come Home
events.scene: Ten years after the war, the elves of Qualinesti begin returning from exile. The columns pass near Gateway, silent. What they find in the forest, they say, is worse than expected: whole regions burned.

choices.text: Offer help to those passing

outcomes.text: A family accepts water and a roof for one night. It's little, and it's more talk between the two peoples than there has been in years.
They decline with icy courtesy. You learn that pride is also a way of carrying loss.

choices.text: Go and work on rebuilding the forest

outcomes.text: You spend seasons replanting what the dragons burned. Trees are something you plant for your grandchildren.
Clearing ruins, you find things the occupiers left behind, and things the elves hid before they left.

events.title: The Man Looking for the Best
events.scene: An immaculately mannered stranger watches the drills for a few days and then seeks you out. He speaks of a new order of knights, with honour, discipline and a vision for each member, and of a future where Ansalon will have true order. He doesn't say whom the order serves.

choices.text: Ask whom they serve

outcomes.text: He smiles and says you asked the right question too soon. He leaves the next day, and you're left with a chill.
He tells you. Calmly, as if he sees no problem at all. You refuse, and he writes down your name.

choices.text: Hear the offer to the end

outcomes.text: The part about honour and discipline speaks deep to you. You refuse in the end, barely, and keep what you learned about how they think.
You refuse. A friend of yours accepts, and leaves before dawn without saying goodbye.

events.title: The Ice Boat
events.scene: The Ice Folk's boats sail on the ice itself, on runners, with sails that catch the wind off the glacier and carry them faster than any horse. Today your uncle lets you hold the tiller for the first time. The wind is rising.

choices.text: Let her run before the wind

outcomes.text: You fly across the ice, faster than you've ever moved, and your uncle laughs the whole way. You're never the same after.
A ridge in the ice, a crack, and you're both in the snow. The boat survives. Your uncle teaches you about ridges.

choices.text: Keep her steady, as you were taught

outcomes.text: A steady run home. Your uncle says you'll be a good sailor, and he doesn't say that to everyone.
You're more interested in how the runners are made. Your uncle takes you to the boat-builders that winter.

events.title: The White Bear
events.scene: A great white bear has been taking seals from the tribe's fishing holes. The hunters are going out after it, and for the first time you are allowed to come, to carry spears and keep quiet.

choices.text: Creep closer than you were told

outcomes.text: You see the bear before anyone else, and your whistle brings the hunters round. The bear's claw hangs at your neck after.
The bear sees you first. A hunter steps between you. He carries the scar from it; you carry the debt.

choices.text: Stay with the spears, as told

outcomes.text: A long cold day. At dusk the hunters bring the bear down, and the oldest gives you the first slice of the liver.
You lose two toes to the cold that day, and never complain once. The tribe notices.

events.title: The Frostreaver
events.scene: The Ice Folk's warriors carry frostreavers: axes made from a special ice that only a few know how to find and shape, harder than steel and colder than death. The old weapon-maker has agreed to make you one, if you go with her to find the ice.

choices.text: Go deep into the glacier with her

outcomes.text: Days in the blue dark under the glacier, then the vein of ice that sings when you touch it. Your frostreaver is cut from it.
A crevasse opens under you. She pulls you out, barely. You get your frostreaver, and a fear of the deep ice.

choices.text: Ask her to teach you to shape it instead

outcomes.text: She teaches you the secret, slowly, over three winters. You become the one the tribe goes to.
She says the secret is for her own daughter. You get the axe, and a grudge.

events.title: Tusks in the Night
events.scene: The thanoi, the walrus-men of the ice, raid the camp in the long dark: tusks, harpoons and a stink you can smell before you hear them. The camp's dogs are howling. The warriors are still pulling on their furs.

choices.text: Grab a spear and fight

outcomes.text: The thanoi are driven back onto the ice. You killed one, and you'll dream about its eyes.
A harpoon through the thigh. The raid is beaten off; you walk with a limp for a season.

choices.text: Get the children to the boats

outcomes.text: You get every child onto an ice boat and away. The tribe gives you a seat at the next council for it.
You get all but one. You go back for her, and the thanoi take you instead. You escape three days later.

events.title: The Chieftain's Adviser
events.scene: The chieftain never decides anything without the tribe's holy one at his side. She is old now, and needs someone to learn her prayers, her herbs and her silences. She has watched you for a year, and today she asks.

choices.text: Learn her ways

outcomes.text: Years of prayers to gods who were silent until, one winter, one of them wasn't. She weeps when it happens. So do you.
You learn the silences more than the prayers: when to speak to a chieftain, and when not.

choices.text: Say you belong with the hunters

outcomes.text: She nods and teaches you one prayer anyway, for the hunt. You use it all your life.
She says you'll come back to her. You don't. You think about it often.

events.title: The Trader from the North
events.scene: Once a year a trader comes down from the north with a sledge of clear spirit, distilled from potatoes, as strong as fire, and goes home with fish. This year he wants twice as much fish for the same spirit, and the chieftain sends you to bargain.

choices.text: Bargain hard

outcomes.text: You get the old price, and a story about his grandmother. He respects you after that, and comes back every year.
He out-bargains you, cheerfully. The tribe drinks less that winter, and you learn something.

choices.text: Ask him about the world up north

outcomes.text: He talks all night: cities, wars, dragons, kings. By morning you've agreed the price and lost interest in it.
He offers to take you north with him next year. You think about it all winter.

events.title: The Chieftain's Hunters
events.scene: The chieftain's own hunting band, the ones who go out furthest and come back last, has a place empty after the winter. The leader asks for you. It means the far ice, the long dark, and the tribe's life in your hands.

choices.text: Take the place

outcomes.text: Years on the far ice. You learn to read the glacier like a book and to hunt anything that lives on it.
The band fights as often as it hunts: thanoi, raiders, bears. You become its spear.
A storm separates you from the band for nine days. You come back alone, alive, and changed.

choices.text: Stay with the camp

outcomes.text: The place goes to a friend. You're glad for them, mostly.
You stay, and every time the hunters go out, you watch them until they're gone.

events.title: The Castle on the Ice
events.scene: Strangers have taken Icewall Castle, the old fortress high on the glacier: an elf with a white dragon, soldiers, minotaurs and the thanoi, all serving him. Now the thanoi raid with dragonarmy steel, and the tribes that won't bow are hunted.

choices.text: Fight the raiders with the hunters

outcomes.text: A winter of ambushes on the ice. The tribe holds its hunting grounds, just.
You see the white dragon, once, and its breath turns a whole ice boat to frost. You'll never be warm again inside.

choices.text: Move the camp further from the castle

outcomes.text: The tribe moves west across the ice. The hunting is worse, and nobody dies.
You go back alone to watch the castle, and learn its patrols. That knowledge will matter.

events.title: The Assault on Icewall
events.scene: Winter, 351. Strangers have come to the chieftain's tent: a knight, an elf woman, a cleric with a white beard and a kender. They want to go up to Icewall Castle and end the elf lord. The chieftain listens, and then calls for volunteers to guide them up the glacier.

choices.text: Volunteer to guide them

outcomes.text: You lead them up the ice and wait at the cliff foot. They come back with the elf lord dead and a crystal globe wrapped in a cloak.
You go in with them. The castle is full of things you'll never describe, and you walk out alive.

choices.text: Stay and guard the camp

outcomes.text: While they're gone the thanoi attack the camp, and you hold it. Nobody sings about that part.
You stay, and later hear the whole story from the tribe's poet, who wasn't there either, and tells it better than anyone.

events.title: The Song of the Ice Reaver
events.scene: Around the fires, every winter, an old warrior sings the song of the assault on Icewall: the strangers, the castle, the elf lord's fall. The song gets longer every year. This winter, he asks you to sing the next verse.

choices.text: Sing it as he taught you

outcomes.text: You sing it well enough that the old man nods. From then on, the verse is yours.
You forget a line and make one up. It's better. He's furious, and then he steals it.

choices.text: Sing a verse of your own instead

outcomes.text: You sing about the ones who stayed and held the camp. The fire goes quiet, and then the whole tribe joins in.
Your verse is about the old singer himself, and how the song grows with every winter. Everyone laughs, him loudest.

events.title: The Long War with the Thanoi
events.scene: As long as anyone remembers, the Ice Folk and the thanoi have fought over the hunting grounds. This winter the thanoi come in greater numbers than the old songs say they ever did.

choices.text: Hold the fishing grounds

outcomes.text: The tribe holds. The song of that winter has your name in it, near the end.
The tribe loses the northern holes. Hunger follows.

choices.text: Try to understand why they've come

outcomes.text: They're starving too: the ice is moving. Knowing that doesn't stop the fighting. It changes how you fight.
The warriors laugh at you. The old cleric doesn't.

events.title: White Wings over Icewall
events.scene: 400. Two white dragons have taken Icewall Castle, the old fortress on the glacier, and claim the ice for themselves. The thanoi serve them gladly. The Ice Folk must choose between paying tribute in fish and furs or moving camp further than they've ever gone.

choices.text: Carry the tribute to the castle

outcomes.text: You walk up the glacier with the sledges, and walk down again alive. Others weren't so lucky.
Inside the gate you see what the dragons keep there. You tell the chieftain, and only the chieftain.

choices.text: Move the camp beyond their reach

outcomes.text: A long march across the ice to new grounds. The hunting is poor, and nobody is eaten.
A storm catches the march. You dig in and survive three days under the snow.

events.title: The Kingfisher Festival
events.scene: The Kingfisher Festival in Vogler: boats hung with blue ribbon, fish grilling on every doorstep, and games on the green for the children. This year there is a race along the riverbank, and a prize nobody has won twice.

choices.text: Run the race to win

outcomes.text: You win by a nose. The prize is a carved kingfisher, and an old fisherman tells you he won the same one forty years ago.
You go into the river at the last bend, to a roar of laughter, and come out holding a fish. People remember that longer than the winner.

choices.text: Slip off to watch the boat-builders instead

outcomes.text: An old boat-builder lets you hold the pitch-pot all afternoon and tells you every boat's name and story.
You hide in a boat to see where it goes. It goes to Kalaman, with you aboard. Your mother does not find it funny.

choices.text: Sit with the elders telling the festival's story

outcomes.text: They tell of a battle long ago, and the kingfisher that warned the village. Every year the story is a little different. You keep all the versions.
You ask which version is true. The oldest fisherman says all of them, and gives you the job of telling it next year.

year>=352.scene: The Kingfisher Festival again, the first since the dragonarmies burned Vogler. Half the boats are new, half the families are smaller, and everyone has decided to be very loud about it. There is a race for the children, as there always was.

events.title: Ships from Everywhere
events.scene: Kalaman harbour on a busy morning: ships from Palanthas, from Flotsam, from places you can't pronounce. A minotaur sailor is unloading barrels with a casualness that frightens you, and a barrel has just split open on the quay. It's full of something that smells like the sea's own spices.

choices.text: Help gather up what spilled

outcomes.text: The minotaur flips you a coin from a country you've never heard of. You keep it for years.
The quartermaster sees you work and gives you odd jobs for a season. You learn every ship by its flag.

choices.text: Fill your pockets while everyone shouts

outcomes.text: You get away with a handful of something the apothecary pays good money for. You learn what things are worth.
A huge hand closes on your collar. The minotaur doesn't hurt you; he just looks at you until you empty your pockets, and that's worse.

events.title: The Keep in the Mountains
events.scene: Winter, and the old people are telling the story of Dargaard Keep, in the mountains to the south: the knight who could have stopped the Cataclysm and didn't, and still sits on a burned throne while his dead knights sing to him. Your cousin dares you to go and look at it from the ridge.

choices.text: Go to the ridge and look

outcomes.text: You see the keep, black against the snow, and a light in one window. You run the whole way home.
Fog, and nothing else. You tell everyone you saw the light anyway. After a while you believe it.

choices.text: Refuse; the story is enough

outcomes.text: Your cousin goes alone, and comes back quiet. He never says what he saw.
They call you chicken until spring. You decide you will never be called that again.

mark.grew_up_near_dargaard.scene: Winter in the hamlet under the mountains. Everyone here knows which path leads to Dargaard Keep, and nobody takes it. Tonight the old people are telling the story again, and your cousin dares you to go up to the ridge where you can see it.

events.title: The Guild Test
events.scene: Kalaman is run by a governor, a marshal and a council of guild masters, and the guilds decide who works. To be taken as an apprentice you must pass a test in front of three masters. One of them is plainly bored, and one plainly wants the place for her nephew.

choices.text: Do the work as well as you can, and nothing else

outcomes.text: You pass, on the strength of the work. The bored master, it turns out, was paying attention.
The nephew gets the place. You learn something about Kalaman, and find work outside the guilds.

choices.text: Win over the bored master

outcomes.text: You make him laugh. You pass, and he keeps an eye on you for years, for better and worse.
He stays bored. The nephew gets the place.

choices.text: Point out the nephew, in front of everyone

outcomes.text: The guild council hears of it and gives you the place to avoid a scandal. Nobody in that guild likes you.
You're shown the door. The story follows you around the market for a year, and a few people admire you for it.

events.title: Down the Vingaard
events.scene: Grain and wool come down the Vingaard from the plains of Solamnia to Kalaman on flat barges, and someone always needs a hand on the pole. This barge master pays well, asks no questions, and wants no questions asked about the crates under the canvas.

choices.text: Take the work and ask nothing

outcomes.text: A season on the river. You learn every sandbar from Vogler to the sea, and you never learn what was in the crates.
You find out what was in the crates. So does the river watch, one night. You get away; the barge master doesn't.

choices.text: Look under the canvas first

outcomes.text: Wine, with the excise seals scraped off. You laugh, take the job, and the barge master likes you for it.
Swords, packed in straw, with no maker's marks. You walk away, and remember the barge's name.

events.title: The Marshal's Muster
events.scene: Raiders from Estwilde have hit the farms again, and the marshal of Kalaman calls a muster. Every able body on the city's lists turns out in the square. A sergeant walks the line, picking who goes east with the column and who stays to man the walls.

choices.text: Step forward for the column

outcomes.text: Two weeks in the hills, one sharp fight at a burned farm. You come home with a scar and a friend for life.
Two weeks of marching, no raiders, blisters the size of coins. You learn to march, which is most of soldiering.

choices.text: Ask to serve on the walls

outcomes.text: Nights on the old Istarian walls with the city lights below. A veteran teaches you to read the land from up there.
You're sent to guard a postern and find it opens on old tunnels under the walls, older than the city's records.

choices.text: Make sure your name isn't called

outcomes.text: It isn't. It costs you a bribe and the respect of one neighbour.
It's called anyway, last. The sergeant has seen your sort before.

events.title: The Istarian Walls
events.scene: Kalaman was a fishing village until Istarian merchants came to build a port, long before the Cataclysm. Their walls still stand, and so do the cellars under the oldest guildhall. A collapse has opened a sealed room, and somebody has to go down before the guild masters decide it's a matter for them.

choices.text: Go down with a lamp

outcomes.text: Shelves of Istarian trade ledgers, in perfect order. Somebody will pay a fortune for them, and somebody would kill for one page.
A small shrine to a god nobody in Kalaman worships any more, with fresh candle stubs on the floor.

choices.text: Tell the guild council and let them deal with it

outcomes.text: The council thanks you and seals the room again. Someone sends you a cask of good wine with no note.
Nobody thanks you. A month later, the room is empty.

events.title: A Berth on the Turbidus
events.scene: A merchant captain who trades between Kalaman, Palanthas and the eastern ports needs a hand who can count and climb. The pay is poor, the share of the cargo is good, and the voyage is a year at least. She has heard your name on the quay.

choices.text: Sign the ship's articles

outcomes.text: A year becomes three. You learn to bargain in four ports and to read a captain's face in a storm.
You turn out to belong on the water more than on the ledgers. The captain makes you her mate.
The ship goes down off the Goodlund coast. You come ashore with two others and a lot of kender.

choices.text: Stay; Kalaman is enough world

outcomes.text: The ship sails without you. You watch it from the walls, and go back to work.
You stay, and for years every sail on the horizon looks like that one.

events.title: Villages Burning
events.scene: 351. Smoke on the horizon, one village after another: the Red Dragonarmy has come into the Kalaman country, and it leaves nobody behind. Then Vogler burns, and for once there are survivors: a whole village on the road to Kalaman, carrying what it could.

choices.text: Help the refugees on the road

outcomes.text: You carry a stranger's child for two days. At the city gate her mother takes her back and you never learn either name.
Draconians catch the tail of the column. You see one up close, and what it does to the man in front of you.

choices.text: Get your own family behind the walls first

outcomes.text: You're inside before the gates close. From the walls you watch the smoke and count the villages.
In the crush at the gate, someone's hand slips out of yours.

place.vogler.scene: 351. The Red Dragonarmy comes to Vogler at dawn. The village had seen the smoke from the other villages for weeks; now it's their turn. The mayor orders everyone onto the Kalaman road, and the dragon's shadow passes over the river.

events.title: The City Under the Dragonarmies
events.scene: Late 351. Kalaman has opened its gates to the dragonarmies rather than burn like the villages. Soldiers in the guildhalls, a Highlord's governor in the castle, curfews and lists. Neighbours watch neighbours, and some neighbours write things down.

choices.text: Pass messages for the people who are fighting back

outcomes.text: Notes in bread, in boots, in fish. Nobody catches you, and in the spring you know who in the city can be trusted.
A soldier catches you with a note. Someone you barely know swears you're simple, and you're let go. You owe them your life.

choices.text: Keep your head down and your family fed

outcomes.text: Months of it. You come through, with a bitterness you didn't have before and a lot of patience.
Feeding a family means selling to the occupiers. You do it, and you know the guilds keep lists too.

events.title: The Golden General
events.scene: Spring, 352. The dragonarmies are gone from the walls, and an army comes down the Vingaard behind an elf woman in golden armour, with knights on silver and bronze dragons. Kalaman throws open its gates and its wine cellars. Days later, word runs through the streets: the Golden General rode out to meet someone, and has been taken.

choices.text: Be in the square for the parade

outcomes.text: You see her ride past, close enough to touch the stirrup. You will tell the story until you die.
You cheer her in, and a week later you watch her captains search the hills for her with faces like stone.

choices.text: Go to the army's camp and offer to serve

outcomes.text: They take you as a runner. You see the end of the war from closer than most.
You end up mucking out the stables of a bronze dragon, who is courteous and terrifying and calls you little one.

events.title: Kalaman Rebuilds
events.scene: The years after the war. The port fills again, the burned quarter goes up in new stone, and the guild council argues over who pays for it. There's money to be made rebuilding, and money to be lost, and a lot of people who did well in the occupation trying to look as if they hadn't.

choices.text: Get in on the rebuilding

outcomes.text: You do well out of it. Some people say too well.
Hard work and fair pay. The houses you helped build will still be standing when you're gone.

choices.text: Help the council find out who collaborated

outcomes.text: Some of the names are true. You make enemies who never forget.
One name on the list was wrong. You find out after.

events.title: News from Across the Water
events.scene: The ships coming into Kalaman from the east carry worse news every season: Nordmaar has fallen to armies with dragons in them, then Balifor, then the kender country. Refugees come off the boats with nothing, and some of the sailors won't say what they saw.

choices.text: Go down to the quay and listen to the sailors

outcomes.text: You hear about dragons, real ones, and soldiers with scales. The grown-ups say sailors exaggerate. You don't think so.
A kender off a Goodlund boat tells you the whole thing, twice, with different dragons each time. Under the jokes she's crying.

choices.text: Help the refugees find somewhere to sleep

outcomes.text: A family sleeps in your loft all winter. When they move on, they leave a carved charm on the beam.
The guild council says the city can't feed everyone. You learn how a city decides who it can afford.

events.title: Strange Ships in the Harbour
events.scene: Ships from the east have been putting in at Kalaman with odd cargoes: steel, horses, iron collars, paid for in good gold. Their crews don't drink in the dockside taverns, and their captains meet the governor's men at night.

choices.text: Get a look at their manifests

outcomes.text: Weapons, enough for an army, bound for Sanction. You take it to the marshal. He thanks you and does nothing.
A sailor catches you on the dock and throws you in the harbour. The message is clear.

choices.text: Sell them what they want

outcomes.text: Good gold for a good season. Two years later you see your iron on draconian wrists.
One captain takes a liking to you and tells you more than he should.

events.title: Kalaman and the Emperor
events.scene: Jaymes Markham, who beat the half-ogre Ankhar, has named himself Emperor of Solamnia. Now Kalaman's guilds and governor must decide whether to ask to join his empire, and the city argues about nothing else.

choices.text: Speak for joining the empire

outcomes.text: The petition goes north with your name on it. For the first time in a century, Kalaman has a place in something larger.
You win the vote and lose half your friends among the guilds.

choices.text: Speak for staying free

outcomes.text: You lose. The city remembers that you spoke, and some admire you for it.
The emperor's agents take note of who spoke against him.

events.title: The Pirate Years
events.scene: With Solamnia broken into quarrelling provinces, nobody guards the coast but Kalaman itself. Pirates take a grain ship within sight of the harbour, and the guilds argue about who will pay for a war galley while the town goes hungry.

choices.text: Sign on to the galley the guilds finally build

outcomes.text: A summer of chasing pirates along the coast. You catch one, and it is enough to make the others careful.
The galley runs aground on its third voyage. You walk home along the shore.

choices.text: Work the guildhall to get it paid for

outcomes.text: You learn how the guilds really decide: in back rooms, over wine, by favours owed.
You make sure your family's guild pays least. Not everyone forgets.

events.title: The Gathering of the Tribes
events.scene: Once a year some of the seven tribes camp together by the great well: races, weddings, feuds settled and new ones started. The tribes all descend from the seven sons of Keja, the khan who first united them, and every child is expected to know which son is theirs. An old woman asks you, in front of everyone.

choices.text: Recite your line, all the way back

outcomes.text: You get every name right. The old woman nods, and your family is proud for a week.
You miss a name. The children of a rival tribe never let you forget it.

choices.text: Make them laugh instead

outcomes.text: The whole fire laughs, the old woman too. You're a storyteller now, whether you like it or not.
Your father is not amused. You learn that some things are not for joking.

events.title: The Horse Race
events.scene: The great race of the gathering: twenty riders, a day's ride across stone and sand, and the winner's tribe takes the best well for a year. Your tribe's best rider has broken his arm. Everyone is looking at you.

choices.text: Ride to win

outcomes.text: You win by a length. Your tribe drinks from the best well all year and says your name at every fire.
Your horse falls in a gully. You walk it home rather than leave it, and that is remembered too.

choices.text: Ride to make the rival tribe lose

outcomes.text: Their rider takes the wrong path because of you. Your tribe wins; theirs swears revenge.
The elders see what you did. Winning that way shames your tribe.

events.title: The Blood Feud
events.scene: A man of your tribe has killed a man of another in a quarrel over a well, and now the other tribe wants blood. The elders send you, of all people, to their camp under truce to talk.

choices.text: Offer a blood-price in horses

outcomes.text: It costs your tribe forty horses. Nobody else dies. That is a good bargain, and you made it.
They refuse, and the feud goes on. You did what you could.

choices.text: Offer to settle it by combat, yourself

outcomes.text: You win, and spare their champion. The feud ends, and both tribes tell the story.
You lose, and live. The feud ends anyway; they respect the offer.

events.title: The Khan's Riders
events.scene: The khan's own riders, chosen from every tribe, guard the caravan roads and carry his word across the desert. Their captain needs young riders, and someone has told him about you.

choices.text: Ride for the khan

outcomes.text: Years of desert roads, wells and raiders. You learn the land as well as your own hand.
The riders fight more than they scout. You become one of the best blades among them.
The khan uses you to carry words between feuding tribes. You learn more of politics than of swords.

choices.text: Stay with your tribe

outcomes.text: Your tribe needs you more. You're sure of that, most days.
You watch the riders go with the dust in your eyes.

events.title: Seven Tribes, No Khan
events.scene: Since Keja's sons quarrelled, the seven tribes have had no single khan, only feuds, raids and broken truces. This year two tribes fight over the wells your family depends on, and both expect you to choose a side.

choices.text: Choose your kin's side, whatever it costs

outcomes.text: You ride with your kin. You win the wells, and lose a friend on the other side.
You ride with your kin and come home with a wound that aches every winter.

choices.text: Try to make peace between them

outcomes.text: A truce, for a season. Both tribes think you're mad, and both drink from the wells.
Both sides call you a traitor. You learn why nobody tries.

events.title: Salah-Khan
events.scene: 348. The dragonarmies have come to Khur, and the tribes don't bow. Then Salah of the Khur tribe crushes the rebels for them, and the dark emperor makes him a Highlord: the first khan of all seven tribes since Keja, riding at the head of the Green Dragonarmy.

choices.text: Ride with Salah

outcomes.text: You ride against Silvanesti and Goodlund. You're paid well, and you see things you don't talk about.
For the first time in your life, the seven tribes are one. It feels like glory, whatever it serves.

choices.text: Ride with the tribes that refuse

outcomes.text: Salah breaks your tribe in a single summer. You flee into the mountains with the survivors.
You hide among the hill villages and fight on in small ways.

events.title: The New Khan
events.scene: Salah-Khan is dead, and a new khan, Matarc, holds the tribes together with the old khan's fear and none of his dragons. The tribes that bled under Salah want their own back, and every gathering ends in an argument.

choices.text: Support the new khan

outcomes.text: The tribes stay one, barely. You're glad of it when the raiders come.
The khan remembers who stood by him.

choices.text: Speak for your own tribe's freedom

outcomes.text: Your tribe gets its wells back. The khan gets a grudge.
You speak too loudly, and leave Khur for a while to let it cool.

events.title: The Elves in the Desert
events.scene: Elves are coming into the desert: thousands of them, Qualinesti driven from their drowned city, walking in long columns under the sun with their old and their children. Some of the tribes want to help them. Some want what they carry. The khan has not decided.

choices.text: Show them the wells

outcomes.text: You guide a column to water. An elf of three hundred years thanks you like an equal.
Your tribe's elders are furious you gave away the wells' secret.

choices.text: Trade with them, hard

outcomes.text: Water is worth more than elven silver out here. You come out of the year rich.
You drive a hard bargain with a mother and two children. You don't feel rich.

events.title: What Time Perfects
events.scene: The short-lived learn a trade in ten years. You had decades, and the question stopped being whether you'd be good at something: it became what was worth being excellent at.

choices.text: Go deeper into what you already did

outcomes.text: You reach the point where others stop giving advice and start asking for it.
You get so good you lose patience with anyone who isn't. People drift away, little by little.

choices.text: Drop everything and start something else from scratch

outcomes.text: Starting again as an apprentice, already long in the tooth, teaches more humility than any sermon.
The something else is arms. Learning to fight as an adult means unlearning your whole body.
The something else is the books your people keep and almost nobody reads any more.

events.title: The Short-Lived Friend
events.scene: You befriended a human when they were young. You blinked, and they had grandchildren. Now they're dying of old age, clear-headed, and have sent for you.

choices.text: Stay with them to the end

outcomes.text: They ask you to look after their family once they're gone. You promise, knowing you'll bury them too.
They laugh at your sadness and say those with little time learn to spend it well. You start living faster.

choices.text: Send an excuse; you don't want to see them like this

outcomes.text: News of the death comes in a short letter. The regret lasts longer than the friendship did.
They leave you a letter with no bitterness at all, and an object they carried all their life.

events.title: The Closed House
events.scene: Before the elders, you said something true that shouldn't have been said. Among your people, decades don't erase that. There's a way to mend it: recant in public.

choices.text: Recant

outcomes.text: They accept. You have a place at the table again, and weigh every word from then on.
They accept, and never forget. You stay, with a seat a little further from the fire.

choices.text: Stand by what you said and bear the consequences

outcomes.text: The door closes behind you without ceremony. You go to live among other peoples, where nobody knows what you were accused of.
You leave, and not alone: a few young ones think you were right and come with you.
Years later, events prove you right. Nobody apologises; they simply act as if they'd always agreed.

events.title: Decades on Watch
events.scene: Your people expected a long service from you: guarding a border, a gate, a road. You did it. In all those years of watching, there was one night unlike the others.

choices.text: That night, you followed the rule

outcomes.text: You turned away those who asked to pass, as ordered. You never knew what became of them on the other side.
You turned them away, and later learned they were exactly what the order feared.

choices.text: That night, you made an exception

outcomes.text: You let a fleeing family through. Years later, one of them sought you out to thank you.
You were found out. They took your post, and with it the only place you had among your own.

events.title: A Life's Work
events.scene: Among your people, whoever has no great work hardly has a name. You chose yours long ago, and it chose you back: it eats your nights, your savings and your conversation.

choices.text: Carry on, whatever it takes

outcomes.text: After decades, a real breakthrough. Small from outside; for you, proof it isn't madness.
You conclude the missing piece doesn't exist in Abanasinia. Maybe not in Ansalon. You'll have to go looking.
The work explodes, again. You pick up the pieces whistling, which worries the neighbours.

choices.text: Admit it won't work and let it go

outcomes.text: The relief is enormous, and so is the shame before your people.
You give up one work and, the same week, have the idea for another, far better.

events.title: What Lasts
events.scene: You had someone for longer than a human lives. It ended, or changed, and the way it ended still lives in you.

choices.text: It was good, and you remember it with gratitude

outcomes.text: They died, young by your people's reckoning. You wear a ring and talk to them when you're alone.
You drifted apart without a quarrel, like rivers. You still write.

choices.text: It ended badly, and you'd rather not remember

outcomes.text: There was a betrayal, on one side or the other. Your people have long memories for such things.
They were of another people, and that cost you both more than it should have.

events.title: The False Gods
events.scene: You watched the humans of Abanasinia hand their cities over to priests of new gods. Your people remember the old ones and know these are false. A human you care for is about to give everything they own to the temple.

choices.text: Tell them what you know

outcomes.text: They listen. They keep their faith private, and the two of you share a dangerous secret.
They tell the temple, in good faith. You're watched from then on, and your business in town dries up.
They call you arrogant, like all your kind. The friendship doesn't survive.

choices.text: Stay out of human affairs

outcomes.text: They give everything to the temple. After the war, when the truth comes out, they ask why you said nothing.
You watch the Seekers for years, unnoticed, and learn how people are ruled through fear.

events.title: The Road Years
events.scene: There was a time when you simply left, for ten years or more. You came back with another accent and stories your people think exaggerated.

choices.text: You went north, to the knights' lands

outcomes.text: You saw a whole order trying to live up to an oath, and failing with dignity.
You spent years in a city of books, where one man writes down everything that happens in the world.

choices.text: You went to sea

outcomes.text: You came to own a boat. You lost it in a storm, and regret neither.
You visited the minotaur isles and came back alive, which over there counts as a compliment.

choices.text: You went where nobody lives

outcomes.text: Ten years of silence teach you to listen. You came back speaking less and noticing more.
At the end of the world you found a whole ruin from before the Cataclysm, and spent years reading its walls.

events.title: The One You Raised
events.scene: You raised someone: a child, a nephew or niece, an apprentice. You taught them what you knew. One day they said they were leaving, for a reason you didn't approve of.

choices.text: You let them go, with your blessing

outcomes.text: News arrives now and then. They did better than you expected, and differently than you wanted.
No news for years. You pretend not to count the months.

choices.text: You forbade it

outcomes.text: They left anyway, at night. The last words between you were the worst.
They stayed, and withered. You understood too late what you'd done.

events.title: What's Still Missing
events.scene: After so long, you know every stone of your world, and it has grown small. The elders say it passes. You suspect you don't want it to.

choices.text: Spend the restlessness learning something that was never yours

outcomes.text: You look for someone to teach your body to obey: breath, balance, empty hands.
You go back to the magic books you put aside in youth, and this time they answer.
You learn the long songs, the ones that take a whole night and tell where your people came from.

choices.text: Go and live among the short-lived, where everything changes fast

outcomes.text: It's loud, dirty, hurried, and you wouldn't trade it. In ten years you make more friends than in a hundred.
You never stop being the stranger on the street. You learn to make a living of it.

events.title: Payday
events.scene: The debt has come due, and the one collecting wants no more delays. What you owe can't be earned here by honest work, not in ten years.

choices.text: Go out into the world after big money, the kind only risk pays

outcomes.text: The creditor grants a year, and keeps a hostage: something or someone that matters to you.
The creditor proposes another currency: a dangerous job, done far from here, and the debt is gone.

choices.text: Disappear

outcomes.text: You disappear well. Now and then, at an inn, someone asks after a name a lot like yours.
A collector catches up with you in the second village. You escape, and now the debt carries interest of another kind.

events.title: Nowhere Left to Hide
events.scene: Whoever wishes you harm finally has the means. The first attempt failed by luck. While you stay, your family is in the line of fire.

choices.text: Leave, to draw the danger away from your people

outcomes.text: It works: the danger follows you. That's what you wanted, and it makes the nights no easier.
On the road, someone with the same enemy finds you. Two hunted people together are nearly a plan.

choices.text: Go after the enemy before they come back

outcomes.text: You find out they're only the hand. Whoever gives the orders is far away, and has more names on the list than yours.
You wound them, and don't kill them. Now it's personal for both of you.

events.title: The Missing Word
events.scene: News arrives about the one your family lost: a name on a list, an object recognised at a distant fair, a traveller who swears they saw them. It could be true. It could be cruelty.

choices.text: Follow the lead

outcomes.text: The lead is real and points to another, further away. You write home that you won't be back soon.
The lead is false, planted by someone who wanted you away from home. Finding out who becomes the new question.

choices.text: Pay someone to go in your place

outcomes.text: The messenger returns with a letter: "Send no one else. Come yourself, or no one at all."
The messenger doesn't return. Now two are missing, and one because of you.

events.title: The Door Left Open
events.scene: Someone who once said "come and find me when you're ready" has sent word: the time is now, and the offer won't be repeated. The place is weeks away.

choices.text: Pack your bag

outcomes.text: You leave with some people's blessing and others' scowls. Halfway there, you realise the journey is already the beginning.
When you arrive, the one who invited you is gone. They left instructions, and a problem that's now yours.

choices.text: Send word you won't come

outcomes.text: The answer comes in person: they appear at your door and explain why they need you, and nobody else.
Within a month you can't stand your own decision, and set out after what you refused.

events.title: Time's Up
events.scene: Your magic has grown beyond hiding. Those who watch for such things send word: you have until the end of the season to present yourself, or they'll come for you.

choices.text: Set out for the Tower

outcomes.text: The road is long on purpose. They say the Test begins on the road, and nobody comes back from it the same.
Before the Test, you need things you don't have: a component, a book, an answer. Finding them is the first trial.

choices.text: Vanish before they come

outcomes.text: You choose the road and the name of renegade. You learn never to repeat a spell in the same village.
Some teach outside the Tower, for a price. You go looking for one.

events.title: The Dream That Wasn't a Dream
events.scene: Three nights running, the same dream: a place you've never seen, with too much detail to be invented, and the certainty that something there is waiting for you.

choices.text: Set out to find the place

outcomes.text: On your first day on the road you see, on a sign, the symbol from the dream. That's enough to go on.
You find you're not the only one who dreamed it. Others are on the road, heading for the same place, and not all with the same intent.

choices.text: Stay and try to forget

outcomes.text: The dream gets worse every night, and starts happening while you're awake. You leave so you can sleep.
You don't go to the place; someone from the place comes to you, with months of dust on their boots.

events.title: The Business of the Dead
events.scene: What a dead person left with you sat untouched for years. Now the missing piece has turned up: a name, a place, a date that's drawing near.

choices.text: See it through

outcomes.text: What has to be done is far away and can't be done alone. You'll need people you can trust.
You're not the only heir to it. Someone else wants the same thing, for the opposite reason.

choices.text: Pass it on to whoever will pay for it

outcomes.text: The buyer pays, smiles, and you know at once you've handed it to the wrong person. Undoing that becomes your business.
Nobody wants to buy what they don't understand. It stays yours, and the clock keeps running.

events.title: Someone Has to Go
events.scene: Something threatens your people: a sickness with no known cure, raiders too well organised, a well gone dry for no reason. The answer, if there is one, lies far away. At the meeting, silence falls, and everyone waits for someone else to speak.

choices.text: Raise your hand

outcomes.text: They give you what the village can: a little money, a good staff and everyone's trust, which weighs more.
Someone else raises a hand right after, someone you've never got on with. You both go.

choices.text: Wait for someone else to go

outcomes.text: Nobody goes. A week later things get worse, and you leave without any meeting, before dawn.
Someone else goes, and doesn't come back. Now the village must be saved and you must learn what happened to them.

events.title: By Sundown
events.scene: The decision was made without you in the room: you have until sundown to leave, and never return. It may be fair or not. It's final.

choices.text: Leave with your head high, asking for nothing

outcomes.text: At the edge of the village, someone is waiting with a bundle of food and no words.
You look back once and promise yourself that one day they'll ask you to return.

choices.text: Leave to find proof of your innocence

outcomes.text: Whoever can prove what happened left long ago. Finding them is the beginning.
Piecing it together on the road, you realise you were framed, and by whom.

events.title: The Man Who Never Arrived
events.scene: A wounded stranger collapses in front of you, puts a bundle in your hands, says a name and a place, and dies. Ten minutes later, armed men arrive asking about him.

choices.text: Hide the bundle and say you saw nobody

outcomes.text: They believe you, for now. The bundle holds something you don't understand and a map you understand all too well.
They don't believe you. You have one night's head start before they come back with more men.

choices.text: Hand the bundle to the armed men

outcomes.text: They pay well, and the way they smile keeps you awake. You decide to find out what you handed over.
They take the bundle and look at you anew: you've seen their faces.

choices.text: Take the bundle to the name and place he gave

outcomes.text: You don't know why you took on a dead man's errand. You only know that if you don't, nobody will.
You slip out the back with the bundle under your clothes. At the first bend you notice one of the armed men behind you.

events.title: The One You'd Go For
events.scene: The person who matters most to you is in danger nobody here can solve: an illness the healers don't recognise, a disappearance on the road, or an accusation from far away.

choices.text: Go and find what can save them

outcomes.text: A traveller knows a name: someone, in another land, who has seen this before. It's all you have.
There's someone who can help, and they charge in service, not coin. You agree before hearing what.

choices.text: Stay by their side and send others to search

outcomes.text: The people you sent come back empty-handed. They themselves tell you that you have to go.
There isn't time. After the funeral the house becomes unbearable, and the road doesn't.

events.title: The Road, At Last
events.scene: There's no disaster. Just an ordinary morning when you look at the road and understand that if it isn't now, it will be never.

choices.text: Say a proper goodbye

outcomes.text: There are tears, advice, and a useful gift from the person you least expected.
Since you're going anyway, they ask a favour: to carry something to someone, in a place on the way to nowhere.

choices.text: Leave before anyone wakes

outcomes.text: You leave a short note and feel the weight lift from your shoulders at the first hill.
On the second day you notice someone from home following you, stubborn, to come along.

events.title: Now I'm the One Asking
events.scene: Someone you share a history of debt with, yours or theirs, sends an urgent message: they're in serious trouble, far from here, and you're the only one they trust.

choices.text: Answer the call

outcomes.text: The trouble is bigger than the message said, and involves people who don't like witnesses.
On the way you realise the message may not have been written by them. You go anyway, eyes open.

choices.text: Pretend the message never arrived

outcomes.text: A second message arrives, in another hand: they can no longer write.
Their trouble comes knocking at your door, with names attached.

events.title: The Old Thing Wakes
events.scene: The thing you've kept so long has changed: it warms, grows heavy, points. That same week, three different strangers arrive in the area asking the same questions.

choices.text: Take it to someone who can explain what it is

outcomes.text: Only a handful of people alive can read it, and none live nearby.
It needs no explanation: it points in one direction, always the same. You decide to follow.

choices.text: Get rid of it

outcomes.text: You throw it in the river. Next morning it's on your table, dry.
You give it to the first of the strangers. The other two explain, too late, why you shouldn't have.

events.title: The Wrong Summer
events.scene: Something is out of place: the heat came too early, travellers speak of men in dark armour on the northern roads, and the clerics are quieter than usual. Nobody can say what it is. Everyone feels it.

choices.text: Go and see for yourself

outcomes.text: You see enough to know the rumours are smaller than the truth, and not enough to know what to do.
What you see must be told to someone who can act. That person doesn't live nearby.

choices.text: Prepare for the worst, in your own way

outcomes.text: You sharpen what needs sharpening and look for others who felt it too. You find a few.
You move your family somewhere safer. On the way back, the road feels more yours than the house.

events.title: The Night You Stayed
events.scene: {love.name} walks you home after a long evening, and at the door neither of you says goodnight. {love.They} asks, plainly, whether you'd like {love.them} to stay. It's the kind of question that deserves a plain answer.

choices.text: Say yes

outcomes.text: The door closes on the rest of the night, which is yours. In the morning {love.name} makes breakfast badly and you both laugh about it, and something has begun.
