It's awkward and kind and real, and not at all like the songs. You talk until dawn about why the songs get it wrong.

choices.text: Say not yet, and mean it kindly

outcomes.text: {love.name} smiles and says there's no hurry. There isn't. When you're ready, months later, it's better for the waiting.
{love.They} understands, and the moment passes. You stay friends, and you never quite know what you'd have been.

events.title: Letters Across the Miles
events.scene: Work, war or family has put a hundred miles between you and {love.name}. The letters come every month, folded small, smelling faintly of somewhere else. The latest one asks a question you've both been avoiding: is this going anywhere?

choices.text: Write back that it is

outcomes.text: You find a way to the same town by spring. The first evening, neither of you can stop smiling at the table.
It is, but not yet. You keep writing. A box of letters becomes the most valuable thing you own.

choices.text: Write back the honest, harder answer

outcomes.text: You end it gently, on paper. Their reply is gentle too, and that makes it worse and better.
The honest answer turns out to be the one {love.they} needed to hear. It changes everything, slowly, for the better.

events.title: When It Ends
events.scene: It's over with {love.name}. Nobody did anything terrible; you simply want different lives, and you've both known it for a season. Tonight you say it out loud.

choices.text: End it as kindly as you began

outcomes.text: You stay friends, in time. At {love.their} wedding years later you are the one who makes the toast.
It's kind, and it still aches for a year. You learn that both can be true.

choices.text: Fight for it one last time

outcomes.text: You both try again, differently. This time it holds.
It ends anyway, with words you both regret. You learn something about yourself you didn't want to know.

events.title: Someone You Used to Love
events.scene: Years on, in a market far from where you met, there is {old_love.name}: greyer, kinder around the eyes, and just as surprised to see you. You end up talking until the stalls close.

choices.text: Ask if there's room for a second chance

outcomes.text: There is. It's quieter than it was the first time, and steadier, and it's yours.
There isn't, and that's all right. You part as people who once mattered to each other, and still do, a little.

choices.text: Let the past stay where it is

outcomes.text: You buy {old_love.them} a cup of wine, wish {old_love.them} well, and walk away lighter.
You let it be, and wonder all the way home whether you should have.

events.title: Finding Out
events.scene: You've never been sure who you're drawn to, and you've stopped expecting to be. Then someone you've known a while sits close beside you at a fire, and something in you goes very quiet and very clear.

choices.text: Follow the feeling and see where it goes

outcomes.text: It's women. It has always been women. Everything you didn't understand about yourself rearranges itself into sense.
It's men. You laugh out loud at how long it took you. The one beside you asks what's funny, and you tell him.
It's more than one kind of person; it's whoever they are. That's why it never fit the questions people asked.
Sitting there, you understand the opposite: you love this friend dearly, and you don't want anyone, not in that way. It's a relief, not a loss.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself a while longer

outcomes.text: You don't need to know tonight. But you know more than you did, and that's enough to be going on with.
You tell an old friend instead, who listens without a word and then says, 'Whoever it is, I'll like them.'

events.title: Telling Your Family
events.scene: Your family knows you, mostly. They don't yet know who you love, or all of who you are. You've decided to tell them at supper, and the soup is going cold while you work up to it.

choices.text: Tell them, simply and all at once

outcomes.text: There's a pause, and then the oldest at the table says, 'Well. Bring them to supper, then.' Nobody makes a fuss, which is the best possible fuss.
Not everyone takes it well at first. A season later, the one who took it hardest knocks on your door with a pie and an apology.
Some of them can't accept it. You grieve that. You also build a family of friends who can, and it holds.

choices.text: Tell the one person you're surest of first

outcomes.text: A sibling, a grandparent, a cousin: they squeeze your hand and help you tell the rest.
They keep your secret kindly until you're ready. It takes you another year.

people.kender.scene: You've decided to tell your family who you love. You're a kender, so the family is about forty people, and most of them are already at supper, and one of them has already guessed.

culture.silvanesti.scene: In Silvanost, everything is about the House: its name, its standing, its matches. Tonight you will tell the head of your House who you love, and the soup at the long table is going cold while you find the words.

events.title: A Life Shared Another Way
events.scene: You've never wanted romance, or bed, with anyone, and you've stopped apologising for it. What you do want is {love.name}: your closest friend, who has proposed, half joking, that the two of you take a house together and grow old arguing about the garden.

choices.text: Take the house

outcomes.text: It's the best decision of your life. The garden is a disaster. The house is full of friends every winter.
The neighbours ask questions. You answer them once, cheerfully, and they stop asking.

choices.text: Keep your freedom, and your friend

outcomes.text: You go your separate ways and write every month for thirty years. Some loves don't need a roof.
You choose your own company, gladly. Solitude, for you, is not loneliness.

events.title: When Will You Marry?
events.scene: At every wedding, every feast, someone asks it: when will you marry? Today it's an aunt with a candidate already chosen and waiting by the cakes.

choices.text: Explain, kindly and plainly

outcomes.text: She listens, frowns, and then says her own sister was the same, and lived the happiest life of any of them. You never knew.
She doesn't understand, but she stops asking. That will do.

choices.text: Talk to the candidate anyway, as a friend

outcomes.text: The candidate turns out to be dreading this too. You become fast friends and conspire to escape the cakes.
It's awkward for everyone. You laugh about it for years.

events.title: Loving Across the Years
events.scene: You've fallen for {lover.name}, who isn't of your people. You'll age differently, pray differently, perhaps never see each other's homes the same way. {lover.They} says none of that matters tonight. You both know it will matter someday.

choices.text: Love {lover.them} anyway, and fully

outcomes.text: You build a life between two peoples, with two sets of festivals and twice the arguments. It's worth every one.
It's wonderful, and the years run differently for each of you. You learn to treasure what you have, now.

choices.text: Talk honestly about the years ahead first

outcomes.text: The hardest conversation of your life, and the best. You go in with your eyes open.
You decide, together, that it's too much. You part with great tenderness.

events.title: Two Loves
events.scene: You love {love.name}, and {love.name} loves you, and you have both come to love {partner.name} too, who loves you both back. Some places would call it scandal. Some would shrug. All three of you have to decide what to call it.

choices.text: Make a household of three

outcomes.text: Three chairs at the table, three opinions on everything, and more warmth than the house can hold.
The neighbours talk. You let them. The three of you are too busy being happy to notice.

choices.text: Decide it can't work for you

outcomes.text: You choose, gently, and stay close to the one you didn't. It's harder than either path would have been alone.
In trying to choose, you lose both. It takes you years to stop wondering.

events.title: A Year and a Day
events.scene: At the spring moot, kender who fancy each other can be handfasted: a ribbon round both wrists, a promise for a year and a day, and then you see. {love.name} has a ribbon in one hand and a stolen pie in the other, and is looking at you hopefully.

choices.text: Hold out your wrist

outcomes.text: A year and a day of adventures, arguments and pie. At the end you both tie the ribbon again, without discussing it.
A wonderful year, and then wanderlust takes you both in different directions. You keep the ribbon.

choices.text: Take the pie and keep things friendly

outcomes.text: {love.name} laughs and offers you half the pie anyway. Kender don't hold grudges; there's too much else to do.
Next spring, {love.they} tries again. This time, you hold out your wrist.

events.title: The Long Courtship
events.scene: Elves court the way they do everything: slowly. For eleven years {love.name} has sent you one gift each spring, each more thoughtful than the last. This spring's gift is a seed from {love.their} family's oldest tree, which is a question with only one possible meaning.

choices.text: Plant it beside your door

outcomes.text: In twenty years it's a tree, and you are bonded under it, with both families watching and only some of them disapproving.
Your House has other plans for you. You plant the seed anyway, and the quarrel lasts a century, and the tree outlives it.

choices.text: Send a gift back instead, and take another decade

outcomes.text: {love.name} understands perfectly. A decade is nothing. The gifts continue, and so does the question.
War comes before the decade is out. You keep the seed in a box, unplanted, for a very long time.

events.title: Before the Clan
events.scene: Among dwarves, no one marries a person; they marry into a clan. Tonight you bring {love.name} before your clan's elders, who will ask {love.them} hard questions about stone, debt and loyalty, and harder ones about you.

choices.text: Speak for {love.them} yourself

outcomes.text: The eldest strikes the table once: approved. The feast lasts three days, and your beard (or your braids) will never be the same.
Approved, grudgingly, with conditions. You meet every one of them, out of pure stubbornness.

choices.text: Let {love.name} answer for {love.them}self

outcomes.text: {love.They} answers better than you could have. Your grandmother laughs for the first time in a decade.
The elders refuse. You marry anyway, outside the clan's hall, and the clan comes round in its own slow time.

events.title: An Alliance of Houses
events.scene: Your house has found you a match: {partner.name}, of a house whose alliance would double your family's standing. The match is sensible, respectful and entirely arranged. There is also {love.name}, whom you actually love.

choices.text: Accept the alliance

outcomes.text: To everyone's surprise, including your own, respect becomes affection, and affection becomes something better.
A proper, polite marriage. You and {partner.name} become excellent allies, and never more.

choices.text: Choose {love.name}

outcomes.text: Your house is furious for a year and resigned for ten. You're happy for all of them.
It costs you your place in the house. You've never regretted it, not even on the hungry days.

events.title: The Insult
events.scene: In the market, someone with money and friends says, loudly, that the person who taught you is a fraud and a drunk. People turn to see what you'll do.

choices.text: Answer them, here and now

outcomes.text: Your answer is better than their insult. The crowd laughs at them, and they will not forget it.
Words become fists. You win, and spend a night in the watch-house for it.
They say something true about your teacher that you didn't know. You go home and ask.

choices.text: Walk on

outcomes.text: Your teacher hears of it and says nothing, but the next lesson is the best you ever get.
Word gets round that you can be insulted for free. It costs you, for a while.

events.title: Too Much Work
events.scene: Your master falls ill and the work doesn't stop. For a month you do two people's jobs on half the sleep.

choices.text: Carry it all

outcomes.text: You carry it. When your master returns, everything is done, and they look at you differently after.
On the twenty-third day you fall asleep standing and wake up in bed with a doctor's bill.
Tired hands make a mistake that costs money and nearly a life. You learn your limits the hard way.

choices.text: Ask a friend to share the load

outcomes.text: They come every evening for a month and won't take a coin. You owe them, and you're glad to.
They help, and help themselves to your master's best customers.

events.title: The Patron
events.scene: A rich stranger has noticed you and offers to pay for your training, your tools and your lodging. In return, they say, only loyalty. They don't say to what.

choices.text: Accept

outcomes.text: They are generous and distant. Years later, they come to collect.
The money comes with orders, small at first, then not small.
They are exactly what they seem: someone who once had a patron and wanted to pass it on.

choices.text: Refuse, politely

outcomes.text: You stay poor and free. Your teacher approves, and buys you supper.
They are offended in a way that rich people stay offended.

events.title: What They Say About You
events.scene: A story is going round about you: something you did, or didn't, with someone you shouldn't have. It isn't true. People like it anyway.

choices.text: Find out who started it

outcomes.text: You find out. It was someone you trusted. You never trust quite so easily again.
It was someone who wanted your attention, clumsily. You end up friends, oddly.

choices.text: Let it run until it dies

outcomes.text: It dies, as stories do, and leaves a stain only you can see.
It grows, as stories do. In some towns you're still famous for it.

events.title: The Festival Night
events.scene: One night off a year. Lanterns, music, too much wine and everyone you know out in the streets.

choices.text: Dance until dawn

outcomes.text: You dance with {love.name} until the lanterns gutter. Nothing is the same after.
You dance with everyone and remember none of it, which is the point.

choices.text: Find the dice game behind the inn

outcomes.text: You win a month's wages and a lifelong taste for it.
You lose a month's wages and promise yourself never again. You keep the promise, mostly.
You see the cheat and say so. The table goes quiet, then dangerous.

events.title: Something Missing
events.scene: Money has gone missing where you work. Everyone is being watched, and you can feel the eyes on your back most of all.

choices.text: Find the real thief

outcomes.text: Two nights hidden in the storeroom. You catch the thief, and it's the last person anyone suspected.
You find them: hungry, with children. You put the money back yourself and say nothing.

choices.text: Keep your head down and wait

outcomes.text: The thief is caught by others, and your master apologises, which masters never do.
Nobody is caught. You leave a year later, with a reputation you didn't earn.

events.title: Trouble at Home
events.scene: A letter from home: money is short, someone is sick, and they don't ask you to come back. They don't need to.

choices.text: Go home for a season

outcomes.text: You help them through the winter. Your training waits, and so does your master, grumbling.
You get there in time to help, and too late for one of them.

choices.text: Stay, and send every coin you have

outcomes.text: It's enough, just. You eat less and train harder.
It isn't enough. They don't blame you. You do.

events.title: The Open Contest
events.scene: The town holds an open contest for the young of every trade: best work, best feat, best answer. The prize is small. The attention isn't.

choices.text: Enter, and give it everything

outcomes.text: You win. Strangers know your name for a week, and one of them remembers it for years.
Second, by a hair. You go home and practise until your hands bleed.
You should have won. Everyone knows it. The judge's nephew wins.

choices.text: Help a friend enter instead

outcomes.text: They win, and give you half the prize and all the credit, in private.
They lose, and blame your advice. Friendship is complicated.

events.title: The Wrong Crowd
events.scene: New friends: funny, brave, always with money nobody asks about. They want you along tonight, and they won't say where.

choices.text: Go along

outcomes.text: A rooftop, a stolen cask, a sunrise. Nothing worse. This time.
It's a job. You're the lookout. You're good at it, which worries you.
The watch catches you all. Your master pays the fine and doesn't speak to you for a month.

choices.text: Say you have work in the morning

outcomes.text: Two of them hang the next spring. You go to watch, and wish you hadn't.
They don't ask again. The evenings are long after that.

events.title: Another Way of Doing It
events.scene: A traveller from far away does the thing you're learning in a completely different way, and it works just as well. Your master calls it nonsense.

choices.text: Learn it in secret

outcomes.text: You end up with two ways of doing everything, and you choose by the job.
Your master finds out. It's a bad week, and then, oddly, a long conversation.

choices.text: Stay loyal to your master's way

outcomes.text: You master one way completely. It's enough for most things.
Years later you meet a problem only the traveller's way would solve.

events.title: The First Real Wage
events.scene: For the first time, money that is yours, earned with your own hands. More than you've ever held.

choices.text: Save it

outcomes.text: You save it, and the next, and the next. Money stays with you after that.
You save it under the floorboard. Someone else finds the floorboard.

choices.text: Give it to your family

outcomes.text: Your mother cries. Your father pretends not to. It's the best money you ever spend.
Someone at home drinks it. You don't make that mistake twice.

choices.text: Spend it on something beautiful

outcomes.text: A good cloak, a fine knife, a book. You still have it.
The beautiful thing is a fake. You learn to look closer.

events.title: The Accident
events.scene: A beam gives way, a horse bolts, a pot boils over. Someone is hurt badly, and in the confusion, everyone looks at you.

choices.text: Help the hurt one first, explain later

outcomes.text: You keep them alive until the healer comes. Nobody asks whose fault it was after that.
They live. The blame falls on you anyway, and you carry it.

choices.text: Say what really happened

outcomes.text: They believe you. The real cause is fixed, and you get a reputation for honesty.
The real cause was your master's carelessness. Saying so costs you your place.

events.title: Nothing Left Behind
events.scene: The house burns in the night. Everyone gets out. Nothing else does. Standing in the ashes at dawn, you realise there's nothing left to stay for.

choices.text: Take what you can carry and go

outcomes.text: You walk out of town with a borrowed cloak and a strange lightness.
On the road, you hear the fire was no accident.

choices.text: Go to earn the money to rebuild

outcomes.text: You swear to come back with enough. The road is longer than you thought.
You borrow to start again, and now the lender wants it back faster than the land can give it.

events.title: The Job With Odd Pay
events.scene: A stranger at the inn offers good money for a simple job far from here, paid half in advance. The coins are old, minted somewhere that no longer exists.

choices.text: Take the job

outcomes.text: You take it for the money and keep going for the question.
The job is bait, and you are the fish. You get away, and now you want to know who.

choices.text: Ask about the coins

outcomes.text: A scholar goes pale at the sight of them, and points you somewhere.
The stranger is gone by morning. The coins in your hand aren't.

events.title: The Friend Who Didn't Come Back
events.scene: Your closest friend went away on some business a season ago and never came back. Their family has stopped asking. You haven't.

choices.text: Go after them

outcomes.text: Their last letter names a town. It's a start.
Someone warns you not to look. That settles it.

choices.text: Promise their family you'll bring news

outcomes.text: Their mother holds your hands and doesn't let go for a long time.
Their father mutters something as you leave: they weren't going where they said they were.

events.title: What the Fortune Teller Saw
events.scene: A fortune teller at the fair takes your coin, looks at your palm, and gives the coin back. Then she tells you what she saw, very quietly.

choices.text: Believe her

outcomes.text: She named a place and a danger. You've never been there, and you're going.
She named something that will come for you. You'd rather meet it on the road than at home.

choices.text: Laugh it off

outcomes.text: The first thing she said comes true within the week. You pack.
Nothing happens, which bothers you more than anything would have. You go to find her again; she's gone.

events.title: The Match They Made for You
events.scene: Your family has arranged a marriage: a good family, a good match, a person you've met twice. The date is set. Everyone is very pleased.

choices.text: Leave before the wedding

outcomes.text: You leave a letter and climb out of a window, like in the songs.
They send someone after you to bring you back.

choices.text: Ask for a year to see the world first

outcomes.text: A year, they agree. You don't intend to come back in a year.
Your intended asks for the same year, quietly. You set out together, as friends.

events.title: The Crime You Didn't Do
events.scene: A merchant is dead, and the watch has a witness who swears it was you. You were somewhere else, with someone who will never admit it.

choices.text: Run, tonight

outcomes.text: You're three towns away by the time they post your description.
You run, and you find, on the road, the first thread that leads to the real killer.

choices.text: Stay and clear your name

outcomes.text: The trail leads out of town, and you follow it, with the watch a day behind you.
Your alibi speaks up, at great cost to themselves. You owe them everything, and they ask you to go.

events.title: The Heirloom
events.scene: The one valuable thing your family ever owned, the thing that was going to be yours, is stolen in the night. The thief left a mark you've seen before.

choices.text: Go after it

outcomes.text: You know the mark. You know the people. You go.
The more you learn, the less it looks like a theft and the more like a recovery. Whose was it first?

choices.text: Ask your family what it really was

outcomes.text: Your grandmother tells you, at last, and then tells you to get it back.
Nobody will tell you what it was. The silence tells you enough, and you go to find out.

events.title: The Cure Far Away
events.scene: Someone you love is sick with something the local healer can't treat. There is said to be a cure, far away, in a place most people only know from stories.

choices.text: Go and get it

outcomes.text: You leave the next morning, with a list of symptoms and a name.
Someone else is seeking the same cure for someone else, and there may only be enough for one.

choices.text: Learn what the healer knows first

outcomes.text: Three days of lessons, then the road. You'll recognise the cure when you see it.
The illness worsens while you study. You leave in a hurry, with half an education.

events.title: The Recruiters
events.scene: Recruiters come to town with a list and soldiers. Your name is on the list. They aren't asking.

choices.text: Leave before they find you

outcomes.text: Out the back, over the wall, and onto the road you'd always meant to take.
They find you on the road, and you get away again, and now you're a deserter from an army you never joined.

choices.text: Go with them, for now

outcomes.text: Six weeks of marching. On a dark night near the border, you walk away from the camp and keep walking.
They send you on an errand that takes you far from the army, and you decide to do it properly.

events.title: The Last Wish
events.scene: A dying friend asks one thing: take something of theirs to someone, somewhere, and tell them a message. They make you repeat it until you have it word for word.

choices.text: Swear on it

outcomes.text: You swear. They die easier for it. You leave after the burial.
The thing they give you is heavier than it should be, and warm.

choices.text: Ask who the someone is

outcomes.text: Their child, whom nobody knew about. You'll find them.
Their oldest enemy. The message is an apology. You'll deliver it, carefully.

events.title: The Stray
events.scene: A thin, filthy dog has followed you home three days running. Your family says there's no food to spare for it.

choices.text: Hide it and share your own food

outcomes.text: It grows fat on your suppers, and you grow thin, and it is the best friend you have for years.
Your family finds it, and lets it stay, because of the look on your face.

choices.text: Chase it off

outcomes.text: It goes. You think about it more than you'll admit.
It comes back in the night and barks at a fire before anyone else smells it.

events.title: The Coins for Market
events.scene: Sent alone to market for the first time with the family's coins knotted in a cloth. Halfway there, the knot is loose and the cloth is lighter.

choices.text: Retrace every step

outcomes.text: You find them, coin by coin, in the dust. You count everything twice for the rest of your life.
A boy has them. He gives them back, all but one, and becomes your friend.

choices.text: Buy what you can with what's left

outcomes.text: You haggle like a grown merchant and come home with everything. Nobody ever knows.
You come home short and tell the truth. Your mother says that was the right thing, and makes you work it off.

events.title: The Hard Winter
events.scene: Snow comes early and stays. The woodpile shrinks. One night your family has to choose between warmth and bread.

choices.text: Go out in the snow for wood

outcomes.text: You come back with your arms full and your fingers white. You never forget the cold.
You get lost in the white and are found at dawn, half frozen, by a neighbour.

choices.text: Give your bread to the youngest

outcomes.text: You go hungry for a month, and learn you can.
A neighbour sees and brings a sack of meal. Nobody asks how they knew.

events.title: Your Sibling's Secret
events.scene: You catch {sibling.name} doing something they shouldn't, somewhere they shouldn't be. They beg you not to tell.

choices.text: Keep the secret

outcomes.text: It binds you together, the way only shared secrets do.
The secret gets bigger, and you get dragged into it.

choices.text: Tell your parents

outcomes.text: It was the right thing. It takes your sibling years to agree.
It was worse than you knew. Telling saved them, and one day they thank you.

events.title: The Old Soldier's Stories
events.scene: An old soldier with one arm sits by the well every afternoon and tells stories to any child who'll listen, about wars nobody else remembers.

choices.text: Listen every day

outcomes.text: You learn the names of battles and the price of them.
He teaches you to hold a stick like a sword, and to never be proud of using one.

choices.text: Ask about his arm

outcomes.text: He tells you the truth, which is not a story. You come home quiet.
He says a dragon ate it, then winks. You believe him for years.

events.title: The Travelling Players
events.scene: A wagon of players stops in the square: masks, a painted backdrop, a dragon made of sheets. They need a child for one small part.

choices.text: Put your hand up

outcomes.text: You forget your line, make one up, and the crowd roars. Something wakes in you.
You freeze. A player covers for you so smoothly nobody notices but you.

choices.text: Sneak behind the wagon

outcomes.text: You learn how the dragon flies: ropes, timing and a man with a bellows.
You see one of the players do something that isn't a trick at all.

events.title: The Locked Room
events.scene: There is a room in the house of the old woman next door that she never opens. One day she leaves the key on the table.

choices.text: Open it

outcomes.text: Books, dozens of them, in languages you can't read. She catches you, and starts teaching you instead of scolding.
A child's room, dusty, untouched. You close the door and never mention it, and she knows you know.

choices.text: Leave it alone

outcomes.text: She tells you later that she left it on purpose, to see. You passed.
She dies that winter, and the room is cleared before you can ask.

events.title: The Storm Night
events.scene: A storm tears the roof half off in the night. The grown-ups are fighting with ropes and buckets, and someone has to keep the little ones calm.

choices.text: Gather the little ones and tell them a story

outcomes.text: You tell the best story of your life, and none of them cries.
Your voice shakes. They notice, and hold your hand instead.

choices.text: Go out and help with the ropes

outcomes.text: You hold a rope you shouldn't be able to hold, and the roof stays on.
A loose beam catches you. You have the scar still.

events.title: The Gift You Didn't Want
events.scene: A visiting relative gives you a present: something meant for a different kind of child entirely. Everyone watches to see your face.

choices.text: Smile and say thank you

outcomes.text: They are so pleased that you grow to like it, a little.
Years later, the unwanted thing turns out to be exactly what you need.

choices.text: Say what you actually wanted

outcomes.text: The relative laughs, and sends the right thing next winter. You become their favourite.
The room goes cold. Your mother explains manners to you at length.

events.title: Hide and Seek
events.scene: Hiding where nobody will find you, behind a loose board, you find something already hidden there: wrapped in oilcloth, and very old.

choices.text: Keep it, and tell no one

outcomes.text: A knife with strange marks. It's yours now, and you don't know whose it was.
Letters, from someone in your family, to someone who was not. You read them at night for years.

choices.text: Show the grown-ups

outcomes.text: They go pale and take it away, and the house is quiet for a week.
It's a lost family keepsake. You're a hero at supper.

events.title: The Dare at the Bridge
events.scene: The older youths dare each other to walk the bridge rail over the river in spate. It's your turn, and everyone is watching.

choices.text: Walk the rail

outcomes.text: You make it across. Nobody dares you again; they don't need to.
You fall. The river takes you half a mile before letting go.

choices.text: Refuse, and say why

outcomes.text: One of them refuses with you. Then another. The dare dies there.
They call you a coward for a season. Then one of them drowns doing it.

events.title: The Harvest Dance
events.scene: The harvest dance: lanterns in the barn, a fiddler who knows six songs, and every unmarried adult in the valley pretending not to look at anyone in particular. You're old enough to be expected to dance, and young enough to be nervous about it.

choices.text: Ask someone to dance

outcomes.text: They say yes. You step on their feet all night. They don't mind.
They say no, kindly. You survive it, which surprises you.

choices.text: Stay by the wall and watch

outcomes.text: Someone else by the wall starts talking to you. You talk until the lanterns go out.
From the wall you see things others miss: who leaves with whom, who is lying.

events.title: Lost in the Hills
events.scene: Looking for a strayed animal, you go further into the hills than you've ever gone. Fog comes down. Everything looks the same.

choices.text: Find shelter and wait out the fog

outcomes.text: You shelter in a cave with old paintings on the walls. You copy one with charcoal.
Something else shelters with you. You both leave in the morning without a fight.

choices.text: Keep walking downhill

outcomes.text: Downhill means water, water means people. You walk into a village you've never seen and are home in two days.
A ravine in the fog. You climb out with a bad ankle and a better sense of where your feet go.

events.title: The Bad Year at Home
events.scene: Someone at home has started drinking, and the house has started going quiet when they come in. The younger ones look to you.

choices.text: Stand between them and the young ones

outcomes.text: You take what comes. The young ones don't. You grow up fast that year.
One night you say what everyone is thinking. They stop, for a while. Then for good.

choices.text: Spend every hour you can away from the house

outcomes.text: You find somewhere else to belong: a workshop, a gang, a temple.
You're away the night it goes wrong. You never forgive yourself.

events.title: The Merchant's Errand
events.scene: A merchant passing through needs a sharp youngster to carry a sealed letter to the next town. Good pay, no questions.

choices.text: Carry it, unopened

outcomes.text: Delivered and paid. The merchant remembers reliable people, and comes back with more work.
Someone tries to take it on the road. You keep it, barely.

choices.text: Open it on the way

outcomes.text: It's about someone in your town, and it's not good. Now you know.
The seal was a test. You don't get the money, or the next job.

events.title: The First Hunt
events.scene: For the first time you're allowed to go out with the hunters. Before dawn, you're the one closest to the deer.

choices.text: Take the shot

outcomes.text: A clean shot. The hunters show you how to thank the animal. You never skip it after.
You wound it. You follow the blood trail half a day to finish what you started.

choices.text: Lower the bow

outcomes.text: The hunters laugh. The old one doesn't, and later teaches you herbs instead.
Someone else takes it. You feel relief, then shame at the relief.

events.title: What You Overheard
events.scene: Behind the stable, you overhear two respected people of the town planning something that would ruin a family you know.

choices.text: Warn the family

outcomes.text: They're saved, and never know how. You do.
They're saved, and the plotters find out who talked.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself; knowledge is worth something

outcomes.text: You sell what you know, carefully, and learn a dangerous trade.
The family is ruined. You watch them leave town, and it stays with you.

events.title: The One You Couldn't Have
events.scene: You've fallen for {love.name}, which is the worst idea in the world: wrong family, wrong faith, or promised to someone else.

choices.text: Meet in secret

outcomes.text: One summer of secret meetings. When it ends, it ends quietly, and you keep it forever.
You're caught. Both families make sure it never happens again. It doesn't. You don't forget.

choices.text: Let it go before it starts

outcomes.text: You become friends instead. It's not the same. It's something.
You let it go, and wonder about it on long nights for the rest of your life.

events.title: The Healer's Garden
events.scene: The herb-woman needs someone to weed her garden in exchange for lessons. She is sharp-tongued and never wrong.

choices.text: Weed, and listen

outcomes.text: A season of dirt under your nails and names in your head: which plant heals, which kills, which does both.
She teaches you the poisons first, so you'll respect the rest.

choices.text: Say you've better things to do

outcomes.text: The next winter, a fever, and nobody who knows the herbs but her. You go back, cap in hand.
You find other things to do, and never quite learn to look after yourself.

events.title: Night Fishing
events.scene: Out on the water at night with friends and a lantern, the fish biting. Then the lantern shows something big moving under the boat.

choices.text: Put out the lantern and keep still

outcomes.text: It passes. You row home in silence and never fish there again.
It brushes the boat and tips you in. You get everyone to shore, somehow.

choices.text: Lean over with the lantern to see

outcomes.text: An eye as big as your head looks back. Nobody believes you.
Not a creature: a sunken roof, a street, a whole drowned village from before the Cataclysm.

events.title: The Town That Grew Old
events.scene: You go back to a human town you knew when you were young. Everyone you knew there is dead, and their grandchildren have a story about you that is mostly wrong.

choices.text: Stay a while and set the story straight

outcomes.text: You make new friends, knowing how it will end. You do it anyway.
They prefer the story. You let them have it.

choices.text: Leave before it hurts

outcomes.text: You leave, and stay away from short-lived people for a long time.
On the way out you visit a grave and speak to it longer than you meant to.

events.title: A Hundred Years of One Thing
events.scene: You have done one thing for longer than most humans live. One morning you realise you might finally be good at it.

choices.text: Make the thing you've always meant to make

outcomes.text: It takes twenty years. It's the best thing you'll ever make, and you know it.
You stop halfway, because it would mean you were done.

choices.text: Take students instead

outcomes.text: A whole generation learns your way. Some of them surpass you.
Nobody has the patience to learn it your way. Your way may die with you.

events.title: The Feud Older Than Its Reason
events.scene: Your house has been at odds with another for three generations of humans. Nobody alive remembers why. A wedding could end it, or a duel.

choices.text: Find out why it started, and end it

outcomes.text: It started over a misread letter. You end it with a better one.
It started over something real, and someone still guards it.

choices.text: Keep the feud; it's your family's

outcomes.text: You keep it, coldly and correctly, for another fifty years.
It flares into blood, and you are the one who draws it.

events.title: The Grandchild of a Friend
events.scene: A young human knocks at your door with a letter in their grandfather's hand: your old friend asked you to look after them, if ever they came.

choices.text: Take them in

outcomes.text: You raise them half-way, the way your friend would have wanted. They call you by a family name.
They bring their grandfather's enemies with them.

choices.text: Send them on with money and a letter

outcomes.text: They do well. They write every year. You keep every letter.
The letters stop. You've been meaning to look into it for twenty years.

events.title: The Long Way Round
events.scene: You have time, more than humans can imagine. You decide to see what lies past the edge of the maps your people keep.

choices.text: Go as far as the road goes

outcomes.text: Twenty years, a dozen lands, a hundred languages half-learned.
You come home a stranger, and your people treat you as one.

choices.text: Go slowly, and map everything

outcomes.text: Your maps end up in a library, under someone else's name.
You find a place that isn't on any map, and you mark it on none of yours.

events.title: The Dream of Before
events.scene: The oldest of your people still dream of the world before the Cataclysm. One night, you dream it too, though you were never there.

choices.text: Ask the eldest what it means

outcomes.text: They tell you things they've told no one in centuries.
They go silent, and watch you differently after.

choices.text: Try to forget it

outcomes.text: It comes back every winter, a little clearer each time.
It goes. Something in you misses it.

events.title: The Temple on the Hill
events.scene: From anywhere in Neraka you can see the temple: walls twisted like a claw coming up out of the ground, and no two people agree on how many towers it has. The children dare each other to touch its outer wall. Today the dare is yours.

choices.text: Touch the wall

outcomes.text: The stone is cold as winter in high summer. For a week, you dream of a woman's voice you can't quite hear.
A temple guard catches you and drags you home by the ear. Your parents are more frightened than angry.

choices.text: Refuse the dare

outcomes.text: The other children call you a coward for a season. You decide you don't care.
The boy who did touch it is sick for a month. Nobody calls you a coward after that.

era.after.scene: Where the temple stood there is a heap of black stone that nobody will build on. The children dare each other to climb it. Today the dare is yours.

era.mortals.scene: The ruin of the old temple sits on its hill, and the Dark Knights' banners hang from the new hall beside it. The children dare each other to climb the ruin at dusk, when the knights change the watch. Today the dare is yours.

events.title: The Mercenary Camps
events.scene: Outside the walls the mercenary companies camp, recruiting, drilling, gambling and fighting. A grizzled sergeant has been watching you carry water and offers you a place, a sword and a wage.

choices.text: Take the wage

outcomes.text: A year of drill and bad food. You learn to fight in a line, and who to trust in one.
Your first job is a raid on a village that didn't pay. You do what you're told, and remember it.

choices.text: Keep carrying water

outcomes.text: Water, food, gossip: the camps need all three. You do well selling them.
The sergeant doesn't like being refused. You learn which streets to avoid.

events.title: The Market of the Inner City
events.scene: In Neraka's inner market you can buy anything, including people. Today a family is on the block: a woman and two children, taken in a raid on the plains. The auctioneer is looking at you because you've stopped walking.

choices.text: Buy them, and set them free

outcomes.text: It costs everything you have. You walk them to the edge of the city and they don't look back. That's how it should be.
You free them, and the slaver's men notice where the money came from.

choices.text: Keep walking

outcomes.text: You keep walking. You remember the youngest one's face for years.
You keep walking and tell yourself that's how the world is. Part of you believes it.

events.title: The Knights of Takhisis
events.scene: A knight in black armour with a lily and a skull on her shield is choosing squires. Her order takes children young, trains them hard, and gives them a Vision of their place in the Dark Queen's plan. She has chosen you.

choices.text: Accept

outcomes.text: Years of discipline harder than anything you imagined. The order becomes your family, and its Vision your conscience.
You learn everything they teach, and keep one part of yourself they never touch.
After three years you walk away in the night. They don't forgive deserters, ever.

choices.text: Refuse

outcomes.text: She looks at you a long time, and moves on to the next child.
Your family pays for the refusal, quietly, in a dozen small ways.

events.title: The Pilgrims' City
events.scene: Pilgrims still come to Neraka, believing it is the holy city of legend, and the dark temple on the hill grows a little every year, though nobody has seen anyone build it. Its priests have started preaching in the square, about a queen who has not forgotten her people.

choices.text: Listen to the priests

outcomes.text: Their goddess answers prayers. That is more than anyone else's does. It frightens you how much that matters.
You listen, and what they want from the faithful makes you cold.

choices.text: Help the poor pilgrims instead

outcomes.text: Bread and a roof for people who walked a thousand miles for nothing. It feels like the only holy thing in the city.
The temple's priests notice who you've been feeding.

events.title: The Armies Gather
events.scene: Neraka is changing: soldiers in the streets, dragons over the mountains at night, black-robed mages at the temple, and creatures in armour that walk like men but are not. Everyone with a skill is being put to work for the coming war.

choices.text: Take the work

outcomes.text: The pay is good and the questions are few. You try not to look at what you're making.
You see the eggs, the priests, and what comes out of them. You stop sleeping well.

choices.text: Get your family out of Taman Busuk

outcomes.text: You leave at night, west over the passes, and don't stop until the mountains are behind you.
A patrol turns you back at the pass. Your name goes on a list.

events.title: The Night Neraka Burned
events.scene: 352. The armies of the Whitestone close on Neraka, and inside the temple something goes wrong: the building screams and folds in on itself, and the Highlords' armies turn on each other in the streets. By dawn Neraka is burning and its masters are fleeing in every direction.

choices.text: Hide your family until it's over

outcomes.text: Three days in a cellar while the armies fight over the ruins above you.
When you come out, half the street is gone, and some of your people with it.

choices.text: Go into the burning inner city

outcomes.text: You come out with a Highlord's silver, and nightmares about where you found it.
Instead of treasure you find the prison pens, and open them.

events.title: The Ruined City
events.scene: After the war Neraka is a city of ruins, scavengers and leftover soldiers with nowhere to go. Bands of draconians still hide in the mountains. And lately a new order has been seen on the roads: young knights in black, disciplined and silent, who pay for what they take.

choices.text: Scavenge the ruins

outcomes.text: A Highlord's buried strongbox, and in it a map nobody else has seen.
Something in the deep ruins is still alive and still angry. You get out, barely.

choices.text: Watch the new knights

outcomes.text: They are everything the old armies weren't: honest in their way, and terrifying for it.
One of them asks your name, and writes it down.

events.title: The Knights' City
events.scene: After the Chaos War, Neraka is the Dark Knights' city: their halls, their schools, their prisons and their law. From here they reach out across Ansalon. The streets are safe, the taxes are high, and everyone is watched.

choices.text: Work for the order

outcomes.text: You keep their ledgers and learn how an empire is run on paper.
You serve in their auxiliaries and march where they send you.

choices.text: Join the people who smuggle the hunted out

outcomes.text: Mages, mystics, deserters: you get them out through the old tunnels under the ruins.
The knights catch one of your people. You run before she talks.

events.title: The Emperor's Procession
events.scene: Once a year the emperor rides through Gwynned with the senate behind him in their old robes, as emperors have since before Solamnia existed, though the empire is one island now. A senator's horse has thrown a shoe right in front of you.

choices.text: Catch the horse

outcomes.text: The senator asks your name and your father's. The next year your family gets a small post in his household.
The horse kicks you into the gutter. The senator laughs. You don't forget.

choices.text: Watch the old robes go by

outcomes.text: Your grandmother names every senator's house and what its ancestors did. You remember all of it.
You notice the patches on the robes. An empire of patches, you think.

events.title: Over the Sentinel Mountains
events.scene: The kender of Hylo come over the Sentinel Mountains to trade at the border market: maps, oddities, things that once belonged to someone else. One of them has just sold you a compass that points, she swears, to whatever you want most.

choices.text: Follow the compass

outcomes.text: It leads you over a pass you didn't know, to a valley you'll never forget.
It leads you home. You decide that's not the compass's fault.

choices.text: Demand your money back

outcomes.text: She gives it back, and three other things you didn't ask for. You become friends for life.
She's gone, and so is your purse. You laugh about it, eventually.

people.kender.scene: You go over the Sentinel Mountains with your aunt to the border market, where the Ergothians pay strange prices for strange things. A very serious Ergothian boy has bought your best compass and now wants his money back.

events.title: A Senator's Patronage
events.scene: In Ergoth everything moves by patronage: a senator's favour gets you a post, a contract, a marriage. One has offered you his, in exchange for a small service: a document that needs to go missing from the archives.

choices.text: Do it

outcomes.text: The document vanishes, and your career begins. You never learn what it said.
It works, and now he owns you a little.

choices.text: Refuse

outcomes.text: Doors close. A few honest ones open.
The senator makes sure everyone knows you can't be relied on.

events.title: The Imperial Legion
events.scene: The imperial legion is a shadow of what it was when Ergoth ruled half of Ansalon, but it still drills on the field outside Gwynned with the old standards, and still takes recruits. A centurion has seen you and offers you the oath.

choices.text: Swear the oath

outcomes.text: Years of drill, roads and border forts. The legion becomes your family, for better and worse.
They put you with the horse. You ride the border with Sikk'et Hul and learn the goblins' ways.
A senator's son in your century gets you noticed. You rise fast, and make enemies.

choices.text: Decline

outcomes.text: The centurion shrugs. The legion is used to it.
Your family is ashamed. You decide to give them other reasons to be proud.

people.goblin.scene: The imperial legion still takes goblins from Sikk'et Hul as auxiliaries, as it did when the empire gave your people the province. A centurion who speaks a little Goblin offers you the oath.

events.title: The Lost Capital
events.scene: Across the strait, on the other island, old Daltigoth stands in ogre hands, the imperial capital lost when the Cataclysm tore Ergoth in two. Every year the senate debates retaking it, and every year it decides it can't afford to. This year a young senator swears he'll lead an expedition anyway.

choices.text: Sign on to his expedition

outcomes.text: You land on the other island and see the old capital's towers from a hill. The ogres see you too. You run.
The expedition never sails; the money vanishes. You learn about senators.

choices.text: Read about the old capital in the archives

outcomes.text: Maps of streets that are now ogre dens. You copy them, for no reason you can name.
You find a record nobody was supposed to keep, about what the empire did to the elves of the west.

events.title: The Elven Ships
events.scene: Ships full of elves pass down the coast, bound for the southern island: first the Silvanesti, then the Qualinesti, a whole people running from a war on the mainland that the senate still says is no concern of Ergoth's. Some ships put in at Gwynned for water.

choices.text: Help with the water and the sick

outcomes.text: An elf healer works beside you for a day and teaches you three things you still use.
They tell you what's happening on the mainland. The senate is wrong; this war is everyone's.

choices.text: Watch them go from the quay

outcomes.text: Proud, tired, silent. You think about them often.
You sell them water at three times the price. The money feels heavy.

events.title: The Burning Isle
events.scene: 383. Out to sea, the hidden isle where the irda lived, the ogres who turned their backs on evil, is torn apart from inside. Fishermen say the sea boiled and a grey light went up into the sky. A week later the Summer of Chaos has begun everywhere.

choices.text: Sail out to see what's left

outcomes.text: Black rock, steam and nothing alive. A grey stone shard in the shallows hums when you touch it.
A storm drives you back before you get there. You're glad, later.

choices.text: Warn the town

outcomes.text: Nobody believes you until the sky turns. Then everyone remembers you said it.
They laugh. A week later nobody is laughing.

events.title: The Queen of Hylo
events.scene: 396. A kender called Belladonna, who saw the red dragon burn her family in the east, has made herself ruler of Hylo, and she means to raise an army of kender against the dragons. Even the Ergothian senate isn't sure whether to laugh.

choices.text: Go and see her

outcomes.text: She is small, scarred and utterly serious. You leave believing kender might actually do it.
You end up helping drill kender with crossbows. It's the hardest work you've ever done.

choices.text: Laugh with the senate

outcomes.text: You laugh, and later you're sorry, when you hear what her kender did.
You sell her army boots, at a fair price. That's your contribution.

people.kender.scene: 396. Belladonna, a kender who watched the red dragon burn her family, has made herself ruler of Hylo, and she means to raise an army of kender against the dragons. She's in the square today, asking for volunteers, and she doesn't smile once.

events.title: The Cold from the South
events.scene: Since the white dragon froze the southern island, the winters have come harder in the north, and boats keep arriving from the south full of people with nothing: Ergothians and Kagonesti both. The senate argues about where to put them.

choices.text: Take a family in

outcomes.text: A Kagonesti family lives in your barn for two winters. Their daughter teaches you to track.
It's a hard winter for everyone under your roof, and you all get through it.

choices.text: Petition the senate for them

outcomes.text: Against all odds, the senate grants them land. Your name is on the petition.
The senate files your petition. It is still being considered.

events.title: The Senate Debates the War
events.scene: The war on the mainland is over, won without Ergoth, and the senate is debating, thirty years too late, whether Ergoth should have fought. Young people in Gwynned are going to the mainland to see the new Ansalon for themselves.

choices.text: Go to the mainland

outcomes.text: Solamnia, Abanasinia, cities rebuilding everywhere. You come home a stranger.
You stay for years, and send letters home that the family reads aloud.

choices.text: Speak in the debate

outcomes.text: Your speech is quoted for a season. Nothing changes, but people know your name.
The old senators let you talk, and then vote as they always meant to.

events.title: The Veteran's Offer
events.scene: A veteran who drills the militia has been watching you. After a scuffle you didn't start, they find you: there's a place in the ranks, or at their side, if you can take orders and a beating.

choices.text: Take the place

outcomes.text: They take you. Drill starts before sunrise and there's nothing glorious about it.
They take you on as a porter. You train at night with other people's weapons until somebody notices.
The one who agrees to teach you is a foreigner who fights in a way nobody here knows.

choices.text: Say a sword isn't your life

outcomes.text: You walk away. Some nights you still think about how it felt to be chosen.
Word gets round that you turned them down; some call it sense, some call it fear.

choices.text: Ask to be taught without joining

outcomes.text: They agree to an hour at dawn, unpaid, for as long as you keep coming.
They laugh: it's all or nothing. You go home with nothing.

events.title: A Place at the Bench
events.scene: A master of a trade needs an apprentice, with a proper contract: seven years, board and lodging, and the right to call themselves a journeyman at the end. Your name has come up.

choices.text: Sign the contract

outcomes.text: The master is demanding and fair. Within a year your hands know things your head can't explain.
The master hoards secrets and uses you for the heavy work. You learn by looking over their shoulder.
The workshop that takes you is an apothecary's: glass, powders, fumes, and a long list of things never to mix.

choices.text: Refuse seven years under someone else's roof

outcomes.text: You keep your freedom and your empty purse.
Your family is disappointed and says so for a year.

choices.text: Ask for a shorter contract

outcomes.text: Five years, and you'll sleep in the workshop. Agreed.
The master takes someone more grateful.

events.title: The Hunter at the Door
events.scene: An old hunter who sells pelts in town needs someone young to carry, track and keep quiet for a season or two. They've noticed you know the woods better than you should.

choices.text: Go with them

outcomes.text: An old hunter takes you along for a season. Barely speaks, and teaches you everything.
Nobody teaches you. You learn from cold, hunger and your own mistakes.
You begin to understand the woods in a way that isn't just skill: animals stop to look at you.

choices.text: Stay where there are roofs

outcomes.text: You stay. The woods keep calling, more quietly every year.
Someone else goes, and comes back with stories you envy.

choices.text: Ask to bring your own way of doing things

outcomes.text: They let you, and are surprised how often it works.
They say the woods don't bargain. Neither do they.

events.title: Work With No Questions
events.scene: Someone who always has money and never a trade offers you work: carrying, watching, remembering faces. The pay is good. Nobody explains what the work is for.

choices.text: Take the work

outcomes.text: There's a place for you. The rules are few and breaking them costs dear.
You start carrying messages and parcels without asking what's in them. You learn the whole town by its back alleys.
Whoever hires you isn't a thief: they find things and people for whoever pays. They need young eyes.

choices.text: Say no and walk away

outcomes.text: You walk away, and they let you, this time.
You walk away. Later you see who took the job, and what it cost them.

choices.text: Ask what the work is for

outcomes.text: They tell you, and hire you for asking: they need someone who thinks.
They don't like questions. You're marked as someone who asks them.

events.title: The Temple Needs Hands
events.scene: The temple of the true gods is growing faster than its servants can manage. A priest asks whether you'd give your days to it, as a novice, and see what the gods make of you.

choices.text: Become a novice

outcomes.text: The temple takes you. Half the day is prayer; the other half, bucket and mop.
You end up in a house of discipline and silence, where prayer is done with the body: posture, breath, empty hands.
Instead of a temple, a wandering preacher takes you along. Their faith fits in a satchel and a staff.

choices.text: Say the gods can manage without you

outcomes.text: The priest smiles and leaves the door open.
You decline, and feel strangely lighter, and strangely watched.

choices.text: Offer to serve, but not to swear

outcomes.text: They accept a lay helper; you learn the rites without the vows.
Half measures aren't welcome at the altar.

events.title: Someone Who Teaches Magic
events.scene: Word of what happens around you has reached someone who knows what it means. They offer to teach you, quietly, before somebody less kind finds you first.

choices.text: Accept the lessons

outcomes.text: A wizard takes you as an apprentice. The first year is copying, cleaning and touching nothing.
Nobody will. You teach yourself, from the book you have and the mistakes you make.
Your teacher wears no robe and has no tower: a woman of the woods, whose magic came from someone she owes.

choices.text: Refuse, and try to make it stop

outcomes.text: It doesn't stop. It only learns to wait.
For a while it seems to work. Then a candle lights itself in front of your mother.

choices.text: Ask what they want in return

outcomes.text: A service, one day, unnamed. You agree, and the lessons begin.
They say the question is the right one, and leave you a book instead of an answer.

events.title: The Scholar's Assistant
events.scene: A scholar, a scribe, or a keeper of records needs young eyes and a steady hand. The work is copying, sorting and fetching. The reward is everything you'll read.

choices.text: Take the post

outcomes.text: Ink on your fingers, an aching back, and the whole world passing across your desk on paper.
What they need isn't a copyist but someone who can do sums. You discover numbers tell secrets.
Your master's library has a locked shelf. They pretend not to notice you found the key.

choices.text: Say books won't feed anyone

outcomes.text: You stay with work you can see the end of.
You say it, and don't quite believe it.

choices.text: Ask to read before you copy

outcomes.text: The scholar likes the impertinence. You get the run of the shelves.
You're told to copy first and think later. You leave.

events.title: A Place on the Caravan
events.scene: A trader is short of hands for the season: loading, guarding, counting, haggling. The caravan, or the boat, leaves in three days, and doesn't wait.

choices.text: Go with them

outcomes.text: The caravan takes you. In a year you know more road than your parents did in a lifetime.
There's room on a boat working the coast. You learn knots, winds, and how to haggle in three ports.
A childless merchant sees an heir in you and starts teaching you the business from the inside.

choices.text: Stay; the road can wait

outcomes.text: The road waits. It always does, until it doesn't.
You watch the dust of the caravan settle and feel it in your chest.

choices.text: Ask for a share instead of wages

outcomes.text: A small share, and a lot of responsibility. Deal.
They find someone cheaper.

events.title: The Troupe Is Leaving
events.scene: The players who passed through are packing their wagons, and one of them says they could use you: you can sing, or lie, or fall convincingly. They leave at dawn.

choices.text: Climb onto the wagon

outcomes.text: You carry trunks, set up the stage, and slowly earn lines. The road becomes home.
An old singer, who knows the songs from before the war, chooses you so they won't die with them.
What the troupe needs is someone light for the dangerous act. You learn to fall without breaking.

choices.text: Watch them go

outcomes.text: You wave from the road. You know every word of their last song.
You stay, and your family is relieved, and you're not.

choices.text: Ask for a real part, not just the trunks

outcomes.text: They give you a small part and a big costume.
Everybody starts with the trunks. You decide not to start.

events.title: The Healer Needs Help
events.scene: The local healer is getting old, or busy, or both. They ask whether you'd come and learn: herbs, bandages, births, and the times when nothing works.

choices.text: Go and learn

outcomes.text: Herbs, bandages, births in the small hours. You learn that half the craft is knowing what not to do.
Your teacher learned on the battlefields: saw, needle and haste. They teach you the same way.
Your teacher wants to know why people fall ill, and pays for bodies to look inside. You hold the lamp.

choices.text: Say you can't stand blood

outcomes.text: It's true, and nobody holds it against you.
It isn't true, and you know it.

choices.text: Ask to learn surgery, not herbs

outcomes.text: The healer sends you to a field surgeon they owe a favour.
Herbs first, says the healer. You walk out.

events.title: Service in a Great House
events.scene: A household with a name and land needs a page, a messenger, someone presentable who can keep their mouth shut. Someone has recommended you.

choices.text: Enter their service

outcomes.text: You serve, listen, and learn the etiquette of a house where a wrong word ends a career.
The house has an old-fashioned man-at-arms who needs a squire. Honour, horse and sword, in that order.
Your mistress uses you to carry messages that can't be written down. You learn to read faces.

choices.text: Refuse to wear anyone's colours

outcomes.text: Your pride costs you a future. You don't regret it, mostly.
The house remembers the refusal.

choices.text: Ask to serve the lord's old knight instead

outcomes.text: The old knight takes you as a squire.
That isn't how service works, you're told.

events.title: The Family Needs You
events.scene: Someone at home can't carry the work any more: an illness, an injury, or just the years. Without a younger pair of hands, the family's livelihood goes.

choices.text: Take over the work

outcomes.text: You learn the household's work from end to end. There's pride in it, and a window through which you watch the road.
You change how things are done, against the elders' advice, and it works.

choices.text: Leave it to someone else

outcomes.text: A cousin takes it on, and never lets you forget.
Nobody takes it on, and the family sells up.

choices.text: Take it on, but your way

outcomes.text: You change how things are done, against the elders' advice, and it works.
You change too much, too fast. It takes years to win them back.

events.title: The Tower of the Sun
events.scene: Dawn in Qualinost. The sun strikes the Tower of the Sun and the whole city of rose quartz seems to catch fire. Below, the Speaker's household crosses the square, and the grown-ups bow. A child from a great house shoves past you to get a better look.

choices.text: Bow as you were taught, perfectly

outcomes.text: An old courtier notices the bow and nods. Your mother speaks of nothing else for a week.
You bow so perfectly that you miss the whole procession. Something in you decides that was a bad trade.

choices.text: Shove the noble child back

outcomes.text: A scuffle, in front of the Speaker's house. Your family is mortified; the other child's family never forgets your name.
The other child laughs, of all things, and from that day you are friends across a gap neither family approves of.

choices.text: Slip away and climb an arch for a better view

outcomes.text: From the arch you see the whole city at once, and the forest beyond, and the plains beyond that. You want all of it.
You slip, and a guard catches you by the collar. He tells nobody, and teaches you how to climb properly.

events.title: The Servant's Child
events.scene: In the household where you live, the Kagonesti servants keep to the back stairs. One of their children, your age, has painted a stripe of red on one cheek, the way the wild elves do, and the steward has seen it.

choices.text: Say the paint was your idea

outcomes.text: You share the punishment. The two of you share a great deal after that, out of sight of the grown-ups.
Nobody believes you. The other child is punished twice: once for the paint, once for making you lie.

choices.text: Help wash it off before anyone else sees

outcomes.text: It comes off, mostly. The child looks at you as if you'd taken something, and maybe you had.
While you scrub, the child tells you what the stripe means. It is the first thing you ever learn that is not in an elven book.

choices.text: Look away; it isn't your business

outcomes.text: It isn't. That is how the household runs, and you learn to run it the same way.
You hear the steward's voice through two walls. You never quite stop hearing it.

mark.born_in_servitude.scene: You were born on the back stairs of a Qualinesti household, like your mother. Today the master's child finds the red stripe your grandmother painted on your cheek, the way your people did before they served anyone, and runs to tell the steward.

events.title: Shaping the Wood
events.scene: An old shaper of wood lets the children watch while she coaxes a living branch into the curve of a bridge rail. It takes her a season. She hands you a seedling and says it will take you longer.

choices.text: Tend the seedling, every day, for years

outcomes.text: It grows into a small, crooked arch by your door. Elves walking past slow down to look at it.
It dies in a dry summer. The old shaper hands you another without a word. That is the lesson.

choices.text: Ask her how it really works

outcomes.text: She tells you about the old songs that went with the shaping, before the Cataclysm, when some of it was magic.
She looks at you a long time, and asks your parents if she can borrow you for a decade or so.

events.title: The Human at the Border
events.scene: A human has been found inside the forest, three days past the border: a trapper, lost and feverish, with a sack of furs and a broken boot. The Speaker's law says no humans in Qualinesti. The patrol leader looks at you to see what you'll say.

choices.text: The law is the law; walk him to the border

outcomes.text: Two days' walk with a sick man who never stops thanking you. You leave him at the edge of the plains with food you weren't meant to give.
You walk him out and don't look back. You are praised for it, and you find you like being praised.

choices.text: Hide him until the fever breaks

outcomes.text: He lives. He leaves at night, and years later a bundle of the best furs you ever saw turns up at the border post with your name on it.
The patrol finds him. You are not punished, quite, but the senators' families now know your name for the wrong reason.

choices.text: Talk with him first; you've never met a human

outcomes.text: He talks about Haven and Solace and the plains people, in a terrible accent, and you remember every word.
He asks you, quite seriously, whether the elves still have priests. You realise you don't know what to answer.

year>=348.scene: A human has been found inside the forest, three days past the border: a trader running from something in the north, babbling about dragons. The Speaker's law says no humans in Qualinesti. The patrol leader looks at you to see what you'll say.

events.title: The Song of Kith-Kanan
events.scene: In the archives, a keeper of songs teaches the young the founding of Qualinesti: Kith-Kanan, the long war with Ergoth, the kin who broke from Silvanesti. One verse names the elves who died on the wrong side. The keeper skips it.

choices.text: Ask about the verse she skipped

outcomes.text: She tells you, later, alone. Elves killed elves, and both sides called it honour. You start reading history differently.
She says some songs are sung, and some are kept. You find the verse yourself, in a book nobody has opened in a century.

choices.text: Learn the whole song by heart, as it is sung

outcomes.text: You sing it at the midsummer gathering without a single slip. Old elves who fought beside Kith-Kanan's grandchildren weep.
You learn it, and somewhere in the third hundred verses you stop believing a word.

events.title: The Kentommen
events.scene: Your Kentommen: the day the Qualinesti stop calling you a child. Family and friends gather, gifts are given, and you are asked to speak a vow of your own choosing before them all. Everyone has been waiting decades for this, including you.

choices.text: Vow to serve your people

outcomes.text: It is the expected vow, and you mean it. The elders nod. A place is found for you.
A senator of the Thalas-Enthia is among the guests, and asks your family about you afterwards.

choices.text: Vow to see the world beyond the forest

outcomes.text: There is a silence you will remember for a hundred years. Then your grandmother laughs, and it is all right, nearly.
Your father gives you a travelling cloak he has kept since before you were born. He had made the same vow, once.

choices.text: Speak a vow nobody expected, and refuse to explain it

outcomes.text: People talk about it for a decade. You never tell, and the vow quietly runs your life.
Your family is so embarrassed that the gifts are returned. You keep the vow anyway.

people.half_elf.scene: Your Kentommen: half-elves have one too, in Qualinost, when a family insists. Yours insisted. Half the guests came out of duty and the other half to see what you would say. You are asked to speak a vow before them all.

events.title: Before the Thalas-Enthia
events.scene: The Thalas-Enthia, the senate of the guilds and communities, is hearing a petition your family's guild has made: a share of the border trade. Somebody has to stand up and speak it. The Speaker of the Sun is listening from his seat, and can overturn whatever they decide.

choices.text: Speak the petition yourself

outcomes.text: You win it, by two voices. Afterwards a senator takes your arm and says the guild could use you on its council.
You lose it, gracefully. The Speaker himself remarks that it was well argued, which is worth more than the trade.

choices.text: Make a quiet bargain with a senator instead

outcomes.text: The petition passes without a word spoken. You owe the senator something now, and he will remember.
Another senator hears of it. The petition dies, and the bargain becomes a story told about your family.

choices.text: Refuse; let someone older do it

outcomes.text: You watch from the gallery and learn how the senate really works: never in the speeches.
Your family had counted on you. They don't say so, which is worse.

era.mortals.scene: The Thalas-Enthia still meets, under the eyes of a Knight of Neraka who sits at the back and writes down every name. Today it hears a petition your family has brought, and everyone is choosing their words very carefully.

events.title: The Long Watch
events.scene: Decades pass in the forest the way seasons pass for humans. News comes from outside in pieces: towns you have never seen founded and burned, Seekers preaching false gods in Haven, the humans growing more of everything. Someone at supper asks whether the elves will still be here when the humans are done.

choices.text: Say the elves must go out and meet the world

outcomes.text: You end up spending a few years in Solace and Haven, under a hood. You come back changed and unable to explain how.
The argument lasts years. You make friends and enemies by it, and a reputation.

choices.text: Say the forest has outlasted everything before

outcomes.text: You give yourself to the forest's work, and the years go by like water. You get very good at it.
You say it, and lie awake for a month afterwards wondering whether it's true.

era.mortals.scene: Decades pass under the occupation the way seasons pass for humans. Knights in black at the gates, a dragon's tax every spring, and news of the outside world in whispers. The elves endure. Enduring, you begin to suspect, is not the same as living.

year>=345.scene: Decades pass in the forest, and the news from outside grows worse: armies gathering in the east, dragons seen over Nordmaar, refugees on the roads. At supper someone asks whether the Speaker means to fight, or to leave.

events.title: The Speaker's Rangers
events.scene: The rangers who guard the borders of Qualinesti need young eyes. Their captain, one of the Speaker's own kin, watched you in the woods last spring. Now there's an invitation: years of patrols, silence, bowstrings and long nights in the trees.

choices.text: Take the oath of the border

outcomes.text: You learn to move through the forest without a sound and to sleep in a tree. The border becomes your home.
The captain is proud and cold, and the patrols are long. You learn the bow, and you learn to keep your opinions.
An old ranger takes you under her wing and teaches you everything the captain doesn't know he doesn't know.

choices.text: Say your place is in the city

outcomes.text: The captain shrugs and finds someone else. You hear about their patrols for decades.
Your family is relieved. You aren't sure you are.

era.mortals.scene: The rangers of Qualinesti are outlaws in their own forest now, hunting the Knights' patrols and the green dragon's servants. Their captain, one of the few left from the old watch, needs young eyes and steady nerves, and has been watching you.

people.half_elf.scene: The rangers who guard the borders need young eyes, and their captain, against all custom, has asked for you, half-elf or not. Some of the rangers make it clear they would rather he hadn't.

events.title: The Blue Crystal Staff
events.scene: 351. Strangers have come to Qualinost with the Speaker's son: humans, a dwarf, a kender, and a plainswoman who carries a staff of blue crystal. In the Tower of the Sun she heals a wound before the Speaker himself, in the name of Mishakal. The court is in uproar: the gods have come back, and they came back to a human.

choices.text: Push into the crowd to see it with your own eyes

outcomes.text: You see the light. For a moment you are a child again, before everything was certain.
You see it, and you hear an old senator mutter that the gods have forgotten who their eldest children are. Part of you agrees.

choices.text: Say it's a trick of human magic

outcomes.text: Within a season, there are elves praying again in the old temples. You find you have to apologise to several people.
You hold to it, and lose friends over it.

events.title: The Speaker Is Dead
events.scene: Early spring, 356. Solostaran, Speaker of the Sun for as long as anyone can remember, is dead, in exile, far from the tower he built his life around. His eldest son Porthios will hold the Sun: proud, hard, and the one who led the rangers through the war. The mourning songs go on for nine days.

choices.text: Sing with the mourners all nine days

outcomes.text: By the ninth day you have no voice left and no tears either. Something old has ended, and you were there.
You slip away on the third day to grieve alone, the way your family does. Somebody notices.

choices.text: Think about what Porthios will mean for your people

outcomes.text: A hard Speaker for hard times. You decide to be useful to him.
A hard Speaker who listens to nobody. You decide to be careful.

events.title: Home Through the Ashes
events.scene: Ten years and more after the war, the Qualinesti go home. The ships cross back over the strait, and the columns walk inland to find the forest they left: whole valleys burned, the towns empty, Qualinost standing but stripped. There is a great deal to do, and not nearly enough of you.

choices.text: Give yourself to rebuilding Qualinost

outcomes.text: Years of work on the city. When the first bridge you rebuilt carries a festival procession, you have to sit down.
Everyone wants their old house back, and some of the old houses are gone. You learn far too much about the senate.

choices.text: Go out to the burned valleys and replant

outcomes.text: You plant trees you will see grown, being an elf. Your grandchildren's grandchildren will walk under them.
In the ashes of an outpost you find what the last rangers hid before the dragons came.

choices.text: Stay on the island; there's nothing to go back to

outcomes.text: A few hundred stay in Qualimori. You are one of them, and the Kagonesti make it clear what they think of that.
You stay. Some nights you dream of rose quartz, and wake angry.

events.title: The Masters Leave
events.scene: 351. The Speaker has ordered Qualinesti abandoned before the dragonarmies come. Your masters are packing everything they own onto the ships, and that includes you. In the servants' quarters, people are whispering about the forest, and about who might not be missed in the crush at the docks.

choices.text: Go with the household

outcomes.text: Across the strait to Southern Ergoth, where your masters set you to building them a city in a forest full of free Kagonesti.
On the island you meet the free clans for the first time: your own people, painted and proud. They look at you with pity, and with an offer.

choices.text: Slip away into the forest in the crush

outcomes.text: Nobody counts the servants twice. You spend the war free, in a forest full of enemies, and you have never been happier or more afraid.
You get away, and spend the war hunted by the dragonarmies instead of your masters. It is not as much of an improvement as you hoped.

events.title: The Fleet in the Forest
