events.scene: The Speaker has said nothing in public, but the shipwrights have been called in from the coast, whole groves are being felled for keels, and a company of settlers has quietly sailed for Southern Ergoth to build a city. Everyone knows what it means and nobody says it: the Qualinesti are getting ready to leave.

choices.text: Work on the ships

outcomes.text: A year of shipbuilding. Elves are not a seafaring people, and you learn why, and then you learn it anyway.
You fell trees older than your grandmother for keels. You don't sleep well.

choices.text: Say Qualinesti should stand and fight

outcomes.text: The Speaker's son Porthios agrees, quietly. You're sent to the border with the rangers.
The senators listen politely and go on building ships. You've never felt so young.

events.title: The Closed Forest
events.scene: Since the Cataclysm Qualinesti has kept to itself: humans turned back at the border, trade only at the edges, and the Speaker of the Sun ruling as if the outside world were a rumour. Today a half-elf child is brought before the border wardens, alone, asking to come in.

choices.text: Speak for the child

outcomes.text: The child is let in, on sufferance. You become the one person in Qualinost who is kind to them.
The wardens turn the child away. You find out years later what became of them, and wish you hadn't.

choices.text: Keep the law of the forest

outcomes.text: The forest stays closed. It is what you were taught. It is a while before you question it.
You keep the law, and lie awake that night arguing with it.

events.title: The Puppet King
events.scene: 382. The senate sets young Gilthas, Tanis's son, on the throne and outlaws Porthios, the Speaker who freed Silvanesti. A year later the Knights of Takhisis march into Qualinost, and the new Speaker rules at their pleasure. Every elf must choose how to live under them.

choices.text: Go to the woods with Porthios's rangers

outcomes.text: Years of ambushes in the forest. The knights call you bandits. You call yourselves the forest.
The knights burn a village for every patrol you kill. You learn what resistance costs other people.

choices.text: Stay at court and serve the young Speaker

outcomes.text: You learn the court's real art: smile at the Knights, and pass messages to the woods.
You serve the occupiers too well. Some elves never forgive it.

events.title: The Vanishing
events.scene: 405. Elves have started to disappear from Qualinesti: one from a village, two from a road, a whole household overnight. Nobody finds bodies. Then, in 408, the green dragon Beryl takes the realm openly, and everyone understands what she was doing: stealing elven lives to feed her power.

choices.text: Search for the missing

outcomes.text: You find what's left of one, at the edge of the dragon's land. You never describe it.
You find a child before the dragon's servants do, and get her to safety.

choices.text: Hide your family as best you can

outcomes.text: A cellar under the roots, food for a season. Your family survives the worst of it.
Someone you love is taken while you were hiding the others.

events.title: The Fall of Qualinost
events.scene: 421. Beryl comes for Qualinost itself with all her army. The Speaker orders the city evacuated through tunnels under the river; Laurana stays to fight. At the end the dwarves break the river and the city goes under, with the dragon. Where Qualinost stood there is only a lake, and its people are walking east into exile.

choices.text: Stay to fight with Laurana

outcomes.text: You fight in the streets until the water comes, and somehow you're pulled out. You'll never talk about the last hour.
You see the dragon fall into the flood. Then you swim.

choices.text: Lead the families through the tunnels

outcomes.text: Children, grandparents, a harp nobody would leave behind. You get them all out. Behind you, the city drowns.
In the dark tunnels you lose your own family, and find them again on the far side only after three days.

events.title: Your Life Quest
events.scene: Every gnome inherits a Life Quest: the work an ancestor began and could not finish, which must be finished before the family can rest. Today the guild's subcommittee reads you yours, from a scroll that takes most of the morning. It concerns, as far as you can tell, the exact geometry of a nail.

choices.text: Throw yourself into it

outcomes.text: By the end of the year you know more about nails than anyone alive. It is not nearly enough, and that is wonderful.
Thinking about nails gives you an idea about bridges, then one about cranes. The subcommittee is concerned.

choices.text: Ask what happens if a quest can't be finished

outcomes.text: The subcommittee goes very quiet. Nobody has asked that in four generations. A new subcommittee is formed to answer you.
Your grandmother takes you aside and tells you the truth: nobody ever finishes. That isn't the point. You aren't sure what is.

place.mount_nevermind.scene: Every gnome inherits a Life Quest, and in Mount Nevermind the reading of one is an event: relatives, three guilds, a subcommittee and a band. Today it's your turn. The scroll takes most of the morning, and concerns, as far as you can tell, the exact geometry of a nail.

events.title: The Gnomeflinger
events.scene: Mount Nevermind is a hollow volcano, many levels high, and the quickest way between levels is the gnomeflinger: a catapult that throws you up the shaft to be caught in a net, mostly. Today, for the first time, you are old enough to ride it alone.

choices.text: Ride it, eyes open

outcomes.text: Up through the levels, past a hundred workshops, into the net, laughing. You ride it every day for a year.
You miss the net and land in a vat of something the dyers' guild was working on. You are blue for a month.

choices.text: Ask to see how it works first

outcomes.text: You notice a problem with the counterweight and point it out. It's fixed, and your name is added to the flinger's very long plaque.
Your improvement throws the next gnome two levels too high. Nobody is hurt. Everyone is impressed.

events.title: Choosing a Guild
events.scene: Grown at last, you must choose a guild. Each one believes that whatever has been done can be done better with a new invention, and each one has sent a representative with a presentation. The presentations are long. The one from the Music Guild involves a steam organ.

choices.text: Join your family's guild, as is proper

outcomes.text: Your family is delighted. Your Life Quest is filed with the right subcommittee, in triplicate.
You join, and by the second decade you are secretly visiting other guilds' workshops.

choices.text: Join the strangest guild you can find

outcomes.text: The Guild of Things Not Yet Classified takes you at once. It has eleven members and no premises.
You join the medical guild, whose cures are mostly theoretical. Some of yours work.

choices.text: Refuse to choose, and leave the mountain to see the world

outcomes.text: A scandal in four guilds. You walk out of the mountain with a bag of tools and an enormous list of questions.
You get as far as the coast, and come back with notes on boats. The Guild of Navigation is very interested.

events.title: The Prototype
events.scene: Your invention is finished, after years: a device that will do one thing better than it has ever been done. Today you demonstrate it to the subcommittee. Gnomes are wary of inventions that work every time; they suspect the inventor of being unwell. Yours has three safety valves, two of them decorative.

choices.text: Run it at full power

outcomes.text: It works perfectly. There is a shocked silence, and then a motion to investigate you.
It explodes, beautifully. The subcommittee takes notes. It is the most successful failure of the decade.

choices.text: Run it carefully, at half power

outcomes.text: It works, half as well, and nobody is impressed. You go back to the workshop knowing exactly what to fix.
It works, and then someone notices that a rival guild loosened one of your bolts. There is a hearing.

events.title: The Castle on the Hill
events.scene: Since the Cataclysm, when the Knights were hated across Solamnia, Sancrist has been where they could still live in honour. Today the castle's gates are open for the spring tourney, and the children of the island can watch. A young knight's horse has thrown a shoe, and he looks around for someone to help.

choices.text: Run and help with the horse

outcomes.text: He asks your name, and the next spring, a message comes: would you serve in the castle stables?
You fetch the farrier, a gnome who invents a new shoe on the spot. It works. Mostly.

choices.text: Watch the knights at the lists

outcomes.text: You watch every bout. That night you make a sword from a fence post and practise until the moons set.
An old knight beside you explains every rule of the Measure behind every bout. You remember them all.

events.title: Whitestone Glade
events.scene: In the forest of Gunthar there is a glade with a great white stone in it, and nobody is allowed to touch the stone. Knights come here before their vigils. Tonight there's nobody but you, and the stone is faintly warm in the moonlight.

choices.text: Touch it, just once

outcomes.text: Nothing happens. You feel ashamed, and then, strangely, forgiven.
For a moment you see the glade full of people, elves and humans shouting at each other, and a small figure with a hammer. Then it's gone.

choices.text: Keep vigil, as the knights do

outcomes.text: You kneel until dawn. A knight arriving for his own vigil finds you and says nothing, which is the highest praise he knows.
Wolves circle the glade all night, and never come in. You don't understand why, and you don't ask.

era.mortals.scene: In the forest of Gunthar there is a glade with a great white stone in it. Knights still come here before their vigils, though the gods they prayed to are gone. Tonight there's nobody but you, and the stone is faintly warm in the moonlight, under the one strange moon.

events.title: The Steamworks Needs Hands
events.scene: A master of the Guild of Engineering is building the biggest steam engine Mount Nevermind has ever attempted, and needs an apprentice who can hold a wrench, read a diagram and run very fast in an emergency. The master has seen your work and says it is, by gnome standards, alarmingly sensible.

choices.text: Take the apprenticeship

outcomes.text: Years of pipes, pressure, brass and burns. When the engine finally runs, the whole mountain shakes, and you helped.
You turn out to be better at the calculations than the brass. The master hands you the theory and keeps the wrench.
The engine explodes in the second year. You save the master's life, and both of your eyebrows are gone.

choices.text: Say you'd rather work alone

outcomes.text: The master shrugs: there are always more gnomes. You go back to your own bench and your own ideas.
You turn it down, and for years every steam whistle in the mountain sounds like a question.

events.title: The Whitestone Council
events.scene: Early 352. The free nations meet at Whitestone Glade: Knights, elves of both kingdoms, dwarves, gnomes, all arguing over a dragon orb and whose war this is. Then a blacksmith arrives with a new kind of lance, and a kender smashes the orb on the floor, and nobody quite knows what to do next. It's the beginning of the alliance.

choices.text: Be at the edge of the glade, watching

outcomes.text: You see the lances, silver in the sun. People will ask you about this day for the rest of your life.
You see the kender do it, and you see the face of the elf lord who'd been arguing loudest. You will laugh about that for years.

choices.text: Work the council: carrying, serving, guarding

outcomes.text: You stand guard on the road while the great argue. A knight shares his bread with you and tells you why it matters.
You carry wine to the elven tents and hear things nobody meant you to hear.

events.title: Lances for the War
events.scene: 352. After the Council, the island goes to war: knights riding out, ships leaving Thalan Bay full of soldiers, and Mount Nevermind offering, with great enthusiasm, to help. The Knights are polite. The gnomes build things anyway.

choices.text: Sail with the island's soldiers

outcomes.text: You see the end of the war in Solamnia, and come back with a scar and a story.
You spend the war on the supply ships, never seeing the fighting and never sleeping either.

choices.text: Help the gnomes with their war machine

outcomes.text: It works, once, at exactly the right moment. The Knights send a very short letter of thanks.
It doesn't work, spectacularly, on the beach. The gnomes call it a success; it scared off the gulls.

events.title: The Knights Reborn
events.scene: After the war, the Knights of Solamnia are heroes again, and Sancrist is full of young people from every land asking to be squires. The old knights of Castle Uth Wistan don't know whether to be proud or overwhelmed, and are both.

choices.text: Ask to be taken as a squire

outcomes.text: You are taken, after a test you don't understand until years later. The Measure becomes your life.
There are too many, and you are refused. You keep the Oath anyway, privately, and nobody can stop you.

choices.text: Serve the castle without an oath

outcomes.text: Kitchens, stables, ledgers. You learn how an order of knights really runs, which is mostly on bread.
You become friends with a young knight who will someday be famous. You knew him when.

events.title: The Summons from Solamnia
events.scene: 349. Riders and ships bring word to Castle Uth Wistan: armies in the east with dragons in them, Nordmaar fallen, Silvanesti fled. The Knights on Sancrist argue all winter over whether to go, while the gnomes of Mount Nevermind form a committee to study dragons, theoretically.

choices.text: Listen at the Knights' council

outcomes.text: You hear the young knights argue to sail and the old ones argue to wait. You know which side you're on.
You see the Knights' orders fight each other more than they plan to fight anyone else. It worries you.

choices.text: Join the gnomes' dragon committee

outcomes.text: The committee produces a report the size of a door, about dragons nobody has seen. Three pages of it turn out to be true.
The committee builds an anti-dragon device. It's tested on a pig. The pig is fine; the device isn't.

events.title: The Knights' Last Refuge
events.scene: On the mainland they spit at the Knights of Solamnia. Here on Sancrist the old orders still keep their halls and their ceremonies, a little shabbier every generation. Today an ancient knight is buried with full honours, and there are more mourners than knights.

choices.text: Stand vigil with the knights

outcomes.text: All night beside the bier. At dawn an old knight tells you the dead man's story, and it's better than any song.
You make a private promise at the grave. You keep it.

choices.text: Wonder if the knights are worth keeping

outcomes.text: You say so to a squire. He doesn't argue. He looks like he's wondered too.
You say it too loudly. Half the island hears.

events.title: Lord Gunthar's Funeral
events.scene: 392. Lord Gunthar uth Wistan, who held the Knights together through the War of the Lance and the Chaos War, is dead. Knights come from every corner to his funeral, and stay to hear his successor unveil a revised Measure: fewer rules, more judgement.

choices.text: Stand in the honour guard

outcomes.text: You stand all day in the rain. A grizzled knight beside you weeps without wiping his face.
The new Grand Master notices you, and asks your name.

choices.text: Read the new Measure cover to cover

outcomes.text: You understand it better than some knights do, and you can't help telling them.
You find three contradictions in it and write to the Grand Master. Astonishingly, he writes back.

events.title: Between the Rivers of Fire
events.scene: In Sanction the lava runs in channels through the streets, crossed by stone bridges that sweat in the heat. Every child learns which bridges are safe and which ones crack. Today a younger child from your street has gone out onto the wrong one.

choices.text: Run out and pull them back

outcomes.text: You reach them as the stone groans. Your feet blister through your boots. The whole street knows your name by evening.
You both get off as the bridge drops into the fire. You can't stop shaking for an hour.

choices.text: Shout for the channel-keepers

outcomes.text: A channel-keeper reaches the child with a long hook. She tells you that was the right call, and shows you how she knew.
They come in time, just. You learn what waiting costs.

events.title: The Army Camps
events.scene: Whoever holds Sanction, there are always soldiers camped around it, and the camps need everything a city can sell. You've been running errands for a quartermaster, and today she asks you to carry a sealed letter to a captain in another camp.

choices.text: Carry it, unopened

outcomes.text: She gives you more letters after that, and better pay.
Someone else wants the letter. You keep it, and a bruise.

choices.text: Open it first

outcomes.text: It's a plan to sell out the other captain. You reseal it carefully and say nothing, for now.
The seal doesn't close right. The quartermaster never trusts you again.

events.title: The Lava-Wrights
events.scene: The lava-wrights keep Sanction alive: they cut the channels, build the bridges and know which way the fire will turn before it turns. Their master needs an apprentice with steady hands and no fear of heat.

choices.text: Take the apprenticeship

outcomes.text: Years of stone, heat and calculation. You learn to read the volcano like a page.
You turn out to be better at the forges that use the heat than at the channels.
A channel bursts in your second year. You save the master and carry the scars.

choices.text: Decline

outcomes.text: The master shrugs. There are always more apprentices; the fire takes some every year.
You decline, and wonder about it every time you cross a bridge.

events.title: The City of Three Temples
events.scene: Sanction's old temples stand empty since the gods turned away, their doors chained, and people say the volcanoes woke the day the Cataclysm fell. Tonight a light is burning inside the oldest temple, where no light should be.

choices.text: Go and look

outcomes.text: A stranger in dark robes is praying there. He looks at you, and you run, and you never tell anyone.
Nobody is there, only a lamp, and a carving on the altar older than the city.

choices.text: Leave it alone

outcomes.text: Some things in Sanction are better not seen.
A week later the temple doors are unchained, and men in dark armour come and go.

events.title: The Dragonarmies' Stronghold
events.scene: Sanction has become the dark army's base: camps of every colour around the city, dragons sleeping in the warm hollows of the Lords of Doom, and rumours of something hidden deep in the volcanoes that the dragons guard. Every family works for the army now, one way or another.

choices.text: Work in the camps

outcomes.text: Bread, rope, nails: the army pays well. You stop asking what for.
You're sent to carry supplies into the volcano caves, and you see the eggs. Hundreds of them, gold and silver, under guard.

choices.text: Keep out of the army's sight

outcomes.text: You live small, and the army doesn't notice you.
They notice you anyway, and put you to work.

events.title: The Elves in the Volcano
events.scene: 352. The whole city hears it at once: two elves, one of them a silver-haired woman, got into the caves under the Lords of Doom and found the good dragons' stolen eggs. Within weeks gold and silver dragons are in the sky over Ansalon, and the armies in Sanction are packing.

choices.text: Celebrate quietly

outcomes.text: For the first time in years, you let yourself hope the war might end.
Someone sees you smiling at the news and reports it.

choices.text: Help the soldiers who want to desert

outcomes.text: You hide three of them in your cellar and get them on a ship. One writes to you for the rest of his life.
You get them out, and the officers come asking.

events.title: The Free City
events.scene: Sanction is a free city now, governed by a mysterious man named Hogan Bight who seems to control the volcanoes themselves, and besieged on the landward side by the Knights of Neraka, who want its port. The siege has gone on so long the children play at it.

choices.text: Serve on the walls

outcomes.text: You stand watch on the walls for years. The knights never get in while you're there.
A crossbow bolt from the siege lines ends your watch for a season.

choices.text: Find out who the governor really is

outcomes.text: You see him, once, at dawn on the slopes, and something huge and silver beside him. You tell no one.
His people notice you asking. A polite man suggests you stop.

events.title: Mina Takes Sanction
events.scene: 421. After all the years of siege, Sanction falls to Mina's army, and the girl who speaks for the One God rules from the city's temple. Then the elves come, and the last battle of the War of Souls is fought in Sanction's own streets.

choices.text: Fight beside the elves when they come

outcomes.text: You fight in the streets you grew up in. At the end, something in the temple ends, and the sky changes.
You're wounded early and see the end from a doorway, which is enough.

choices.text: Shelter the city's children

outcomes.text: A cellar full of children, and you telling stories through the noise. Every one of them lives.
The dead who follow Mina walk past your door. The children never forget the sound, and neither do you.

events.title: The Armies Leave
events.scene: The dragonarmies are gone, and Sanction is a city with a hole where its masters used to be. Refugees, deserters and fortune-hunters pour in; the council that claims to rule can't agree on who should repair the bridges over the lava.

choices.text: Help rebuild the bridges

outcomes.text: Two years of hot stone and cracked hands. The bridge you built still stands.
You end up arguing the council into paying for it, which is harder than building it.

choices.text: Deal with the deserters who stayed

outcomes.text: They sell what they took from the army, cheap. You resell it, not so cheap.
One of them, a tired old soldier, becomes the nearest thing you have to a teacher.

events.title: The Garden of Astarin
events.scene: Between the Speaker's palace and the Tower of the Stars lies the Garden of Astarin, where nothing has been allowed to grow out of place in a thousand years. You have climbed the wall. In the middle of the garden a single flower is growing where it shouldn't, crooked and very blue.

choices.text: Pick it, for your mother

outcomes.text: A gardener sees you. Your House pays a fine in apologies, and you learn what a thousand years of order weighs.
Your mother presses it in a book and keeps it for three hundred years. She never asks where it came from.

choices.text: Leave it, and come back every day to see if they've noticed

outcomes.text: Nobody notices for a whole season. You learn that even perfect things have gaps, if you look.
An old gardener catches you watching it, and instead of scolding you, shows you how the garden is really kept.

events.title: The Kirath
events.scene: The kirath guard the borders of Silvanesti, unseen. Tonight two of them come to your door with a stranger between them: a human, bound, who crossed the river. They need somewhere to hold him until morning, and they ask your family. You are the one who brings him water.

choices.text: Talk to the human through the night

outcomes.text: He's a trader from Khur who lost his way, and he knows more about the world than all your tutors. You never forget how small Silvanesti seemed after.
The kirath captain listens to you both from the dark, and in the morning asks if you've thought of the border.

choices.text: Give him water and say nothing; that is the custom

outcomes.text: He is put over the border at dawn. You have done exactly what was expected, and you feel nothing about it at all, for years.
He looks at you as he's led away. Years later, you still remember his eyes.

events.title: The Firstborn
events.scene: An envoy has come from Qualinost, cousins who left this land long ago, and the court treats her with perfect, freezing courtesy. At the feast a senior lord of your House tells you, not quietly, that the Silvanesti are the gods' firstborn, and the rest of the world are guests who have forgotten their manners.

choices.text: Raise your cup to that

outcomes.text: The lord remembers you kindly. You learn how the court rewards those who say what it already believes.
The Qualinesti envoy hears. Decades later, when your people need hers, she remembers your face.

choices.text: Find the envoy afterwards and apologise for the room

outcomes.text: She laughs, tired, and you talk until dawn about what the two peoples could have been. You keep writing to each other.
Someone of your House sees you with her. It is not forgotten.

events.title: The Unchanging Years
events.scene: A century passes in Silvanost the way a season passes elsewhere: the same rites, the same Houses, the same light on the Tower of the Stars. Outside, the world burns and rebuilds itself. Someone of your House says that is exactly the point.

choices.text: Give yourself to the slow perfection of your craft

outcomes.text: Your work becomes something the next century will copy. You barely notice the decades go.
One morning you look up from the work and realise you have been doing the same thing for sixty years.

choices.text: Ask the Speaker's leave to travel

outcomes.text: Twenty years of the human world, under a hood. You come back older than you left in a way no elf should be.
Leave is refused, politely. You stay, and the refusal stays with you.

era.mortals.scene: A generation passes under the shield's shimmer. Nothing comes in, nothing goes out, the same rites, the same Houses, the same light on the Tower of the Stars. Someone of your House says that is exactly the point. The grass at the shield's edge is grey.

events.title: The House Mystic's Apprentice
events.scene: A master of House Mystic needs an apprentice: decades of study, then perhaps the long road to the Tower of Wayreth and the Test, which the Speaker himself took once, at Istar, long ago. She asks you a single question, and waits a whole afternoon for the answer.

choices.text: Accept the apprenticeship

outcomes.text: Decades of books, cantrips and silence. The magic of your people becomes yours, slowly, the way everything is in Silvanesti.
She tells you, at the end, that you are ready for the Test. You are not sure you want it. You go anyway.
In her library you find a page about the dragon orbs, and the Speaker's name beside it. She takes it away from you, too late.

choices.text: Say your path lies elsewhere

outcomes.text: She nods as if she had expected it, and gives the place to a cousin of yours.
For a long time you wonder what you would have learned.

events.title: The Envoys of the Dragon Emperor
events.scene: 348. Envoys of the dragon emperor in the east ride into Silvanost, and the Speaker of the Stars receives them in the Tower. The word that comes out of the audience is peace: the armies will pass Silvanesti by, if Silvanesti stays out of the war. Half the court calls it wisdom. The other half doesn't say anything at all.

choices.text: Trust the Speaker's peace

outcomes.text: For a year, it holds. You let yourself believe it.
You trust it, and you also count the envoys' soldiers on the way out. There are more than an envoy needs.

choices.text: Prepare as if it were war

outcomes.text: You lay up stores, sharpen blades, learn the roads to the coast. A year later, it's the only thing that keeps your family alive.
Your House calls it disloyalty. You do it anyway, quietly.

events.title: The Ships Go Back
events.scene: The war is over, and ships are sailing east again: Porthios of the Qualinesti leads them, to take Silvanesti back from the nightmare a piece at a time. Silvanost itself will be the first place cleansed. Every House must decide who goes into the dream, and who waits.

choices.text: Go back with the first ships

outcomes.text: You help cleanse Silvanost street by street. Some of the things you see there you never describe to anyone.
You go on into the forest with Porthios's soldiers, fighting trees that bleed and shadows that remember being elves.

choices.text: Wait in Silvamori until it's done

outcomes.text: You wait, and the waiting turns into decades. The exile city becomes more home than you meant it to.
You wait, and the ones who went back don't let you forget it.

events.title: Sun and Stars
events.scene: 362. Porthios, Speaker of the Sun, marries Alhana Starbreeze of Silvanesti. Two elven nations under one marriage, for the first time since Kith-Kanan walked away. Some of your people weep for joy. Some of them call it the end of everything.

choices.text: Celebrate with the ones who weep for joy

outcomes.text: For a night, the two peoples dance together. You dance with a stranger who turns out to be a cousin, of sorts.
You celebrate, and notice how cold the bride and groom are to each other. It is a political marriage, and everybody knows it.

choices.text: Stand with the ones who call it the end

outcomes.text: You join the quiet circles that want the two peoples kept apart. Some of them want more than that.
You say it, and then you watch the young of both peoples together, and aren't sure any more.

events.title: The Forest Wakes
events.scene: 382. The last of Lorac's nightmare is broken: Porthios and his soldiers have driven the green dragons from their last hold, and Silvanesti is whole again for the first time in thirty-three years. The court that waits to thank him is already whispering about what to do with a Qualinesti who has grown too popular.

choices.text: Go home to your House's lands

outcomes.text: The trees are healing. Your family's house is still standing, mostly. You sit on the step and don't go in for an hour.
You go home and find you no longer belong to it the way you did. The forest healed; you didn't, quite.

choices.text: Warn Porthios's friends about the whispers

outcomes.text: They thank you, and do nothing. You learn that warnings are cheap and listening is dear.
Someone finds out you spoke. From then on, your House is watched.

events.title: The Long Peace
events.scene: Silvanesti waits out the human centuries as it always has. The Speaker Lorac keeps a court of perfect courtesy, and lately he has grown silent, and spends his nights alone at the top of the Tower of the Stars, looking east.

choices.text: Find a reason to be near the Tower at night

outcomes.text: You see the Speaker at his window with something glowing in his hands, and he sees you. Nothing is ever said.
You hear him singing an old song of the Kinslayer War, alone, very softly.

choices.text: Keep to your House's business

outcomes.text: Decades of your House's business. It is very important, and you will not remember any of it.
You find the perfection stifling, and start taking long walks towards the border.

events.title: The Speaker Outlawed
events.scene: 382. Porthios, who drove out the nightmare, and Alhana, who brought him, are cast out: called dark elves, outlaws, forbidden the land they saved. The Heads of Houses say it is the law. Nobody says it is just.

choices.text: Keep the law

outcomes.text: You keep it. Silvanesti is safe and closed and correct, and colder than you remember.
Your House rises in the new order. You don't ask what it cost.

choices.text: Send help to the outlaws in secret

outcomes.text: Food and arrows left at a stone in the forest, every month, for years. You never meet them.
You're found out. Your House shields you, and never lets you forget it.

events.title: The Shield
events.scene: 394. With dragons tearing Ansalon apart, the Silvanesti raise a shield of magic over their whole land. From inside, the sky shimmers. Nothing comes in. Nothing goes out. The Heads of Houses call it safety.

choices.text: Rejoice; the world can burn without us

outcomes.text: Years of peace under the shimmer. You almost forget there is an outside.
Then you remember the cousins who were outside when it closed.

choices.text: Walk to the edge and look at it

outcomes.text: Along the shield's edge the grass is grey and the birds are dead. You report it. The report is filed.
On the far side of the shimmer, a Qualinesti elf is looking in at you. You can't hear each other. You both stay a long time.

events.title: The Wasting
events.scene: 417. The kirath bring word the Heads of Houses don't want: the shield is killing everything near it, and the wasting sickness spreading among the elves comes from the same place. The court says the shield must stay. The sick get sicker.

choices.text: Nurse the sick

outcomes.text: You learn more about dying in three years than in three centuries.
The wasting touches you too. You recover, slowly, but not completely.

choices.text: Speak against the shield at court

outcomes.text: A few listen. More every month. You are dangerous company now.
Your House is fined and your name struck from the court lists.

events.title: The Shield Falls
events.scene: 421. The shield comes down, and the young king who brought it down follows a human girl called Mina out of the forest. Behind her come the Knights of Neraka, and then, by sea, the minotaurs, to take the land the elves can no longer close.

choices.text: Fight the invaders

outcomes.text: You fight from tree to tree, and lose, and keep fighting. Silvanesti will not be given up twice.
A minotaur axe ends your fighting for a season. You heal in a hidden camp in the deep forest.

choices.text: Take your family out of the forest

outcomes.text: You leave with what you can carry. Behind you, the Tower of the Stars has new masters.
You make it as far as the river, then turn back for the ones who couldn't walk.

events.title: The Knight on the Road
events.scene: A knight rides through, alone, armour patched and moustache long in the old style. The grown-ups go quiet. Some of the other children pick up clods of earth; everyone says the Knights brought the Cataclysm down on all of us.

choices.text: Stand straight and salute, the way you saw in a picture once

outcomes.text: The knight sees you and returns the salute, gravely, as if you were someone. You never forget it.
The other children see you too. For a season they call you the little knight, and not kindly.
The knight stops, asks your name, and tells you one rule of the Measure to keep. You keep it.

choices.text: Throw a clod with the others

outcomes.text: It hits the horse. The knight doesn't even turn his head, and somehow that is worse.
Your mother sees it and drags you home. That night she tells you what her grandmother said about the Knights, and it isn't what the others say.
The knight catches your arm, looks at you a long moment, and lets you go. You don't know why your face burns.

choices.text: Hang back and watch the grown-ups instead

outcomes.text: You learn more about your neighbours in that silence than in a year of talk.
One old woman steps out and hands the knight a loaf. Nobody speaks to her for a week. You do.

year>=353.scene: A knight rides through, armour bright, and this time people come out to see. Since the war, the Knights are heroes again, or at least that is what the songs say. Some of the old folk still spit.

events.title: The Great Harvest
events.scene: Harvest on the Solamnic plains: every pair of hands goes into the fields, children too. Then the sky in the west turns the colour of a bruise. Everyone knows what the summer storms do to standing grain.

choices.text: Work until your hands bleed to get it in

outcomes.text: The last sheaf is under a roof when the hail comes. The farmer gives you a coin and a nod, and you value the nod more.
Half the field is flattened anyway. You learn that hard work and enough are not the same thing.
Lightning strikes the oak at the field's edge. You were under it a moment before.

choices.text: Climb the haystack and watch the storm come

outcomes.text: You learn to read the clouds better than the old men do. They start asking you.
You are soaked, scolded and sent to bed without supper. It was worth it.
For one moment the storm seems to look back at you. You never tell anyone.

events.title: The Knight of the Black Rose
events.scene: Around the fire the old ones tell of Lord Soth, the knight who failed and could not die, and of Nightlund to the east, where the sun never quite rises. The older children dare each other to walk to the edge of the twilight.

choices.text: Take the dare

outcomes.text: You walk until the light goes grey and the birds go quiet, touch the dead tree everyone talks about, and walk back. Nobody else went that far.
Something moves in the grey. You run, and the others laugh, but they ran too.
You see a rider on the ridge, black against the dusk, watching. When you blink, there is nothing.

choices.text: Stay by the fire and ask for the whole story

outcomes.text: You learn the story by heart: the pride, the broken vows, the curse. It becomes the story you tell.
What stays with you isn't the ghost. It's that a good knight could go that wrong.

events.title: The Vingaard in Flood
events.scene: The spring melt comes down the Vingaard all at once. Barges break their moorings, the lower fields go under, and a raft with somebody's goats on it spins past in the brown water.

choices.text: Help the bargemen haul the boats in

outcomes.text: You pull ropes all day. The river folk let you ride downstream with them that summer.
The current takes you. A bargeman fishes you out with a pole, laughing, and teaches you to swim the next week.
A merchant pays you for saving a crate. It's the first money you ever earned.

choices.text: Go after the goats

outcomes.text: You bring back three goats and a reputation.
You lose the goats and nearly yourself. You remember the cold of that water for years.

events.title: The Measure, Read Aloud
events.scene: An old man in the village was a squire once, before the Knights fell into disgrace. He still owns a volume of the Measure, one of thirty-seven, and offers to read it to anyone who'll split his firewood.

choices.text: Split the firewood and listen

outcomes.text: Rule after rule, all winter. Some of it is nonsense. Some of it you will live by.
You argue with every page. He loves it; nobody has argued with the Measure in years.
When the reading is done he takes down an old sword and shows you how to hold it.

choices.text: Laugh about it with your friends

outcomes.text: Your friends laugh with you. Old fool, old rules.
He hears you. He doesn't say anything, and the next week he is dead. You carry that.

events.title: The Great Library
events.scene: In Palanthas stands the Great Library, where Astinus records the history of the world as it happens. The robed monks who serve him, the Aesthetics, let a few outsiders read in the outer halls, if they are quiet, clean and patient.

choices.text: Ask to read, and keep coming back

outcomes.text: They let you in. You read about places you will never see, and some you will.
They make you carry ink and sweep floors first. You read in between, and learn the old script on the way.
They turn you away, politely, every time. You learn to read from the books you can steal instead.

choices.text: Wait for a glimpse of Astinus himself

outcomes.text: You see him once, writing, and he does not look up. Somehow you know you are in the book now.
Days of waiting, nothing. A monk takes pity and gives you a book to take away.

events.title: The Guild Fair
events.scene: Once a year the guilds hold their fair: masters show their best work, apprentices are taken on, and the guildmasters, who run the city's money more than any lord does, walk the stalls like kings.

choices.text: Show what you can make and ask for a place

outcomes.text: A master takes you on for seven years. Your hands are hers now.
Nobody takes you, but a guildmaster remembers your face.
Your work is laughed at in front of everyone. You go home and start again.

choices.text: Watch the crowd's purses instead of the stalls

outcomes.text: Fairs are good for some trades. You come home with more than you came with.
A hand closes on your wrist: a fence, not a guard. He offers you work.
The guild's own wardens catch you. Their justice is quick and public.

events.title: Raiders from the Hills
events.scene: The war is over, but not everyone who fought in it went home. A band of ogres and deserters has been taking sheep, then barns, then people, from the outlying farms. The nearest knight is three days away.

choices.text: Join the farmers who mean to fight

outcomes.text: Pitchforks, torches and one good bow. The raiders decide this valley costs too much.
You win, and you carry the mark of an ogre's club for the rest of your life.
Someone you knew doesn't come back from the ambush. You were standing next to them.

choices.text: Ride three days for the knight

outcomes.text: The knight comes, with two squires and no hesitation. You ride back beside them.
The knight is away. His steward offers you a meal and a shrug.
By the time you are back, it is over, one way or the other. You were the one who rode away.

events.title: The Tourney
events.scene: A lord holds a tourney to celebrate a wedding. The lists are for knights, but there is a melee on foot for anyone with a weapon and the entry fee, and a prize purse that would change your year.

choices.text: Pay the fee and enter the melee

outcomes.text: You are the last one standing, bloody and grinning. The crowd shouts a name, and it's yours.
You go down in the end, but late, and a knight in the stands asks who taught you.
Down in the first rush, with a broken nose and an empty purse.

choices.text: Work the tourney instead: horses, food, bets

outcomes.text: You run the wagers on the melee and come away richer than the winner.
You groom a knight's warhorse for three days and learn more about horses than in your whole life before.

events.title: Westgate Pass
events.scene: Every cart between Palanthas and the rest of Solamnia goes through Westgate Pass, under the High Clerist's Tower. You are hired to go with a load whose owner is nervous, and you soon see why: the crates are heavier than wool should be.

choices.text: Ask what's in the crates

outcomes.text: Swords, unmarked, for buyers who don't want to be named. You now know a secret worth money and danger.
He pays you off on the spot and hires someone less curious.
Silver for the temple, sent quietly to keep it from bandits. He trusts you after that.

choices.text: Do the job and don't ask

outcomes.text: Paid well, asked back. You become someone who knows how not to know things.
The guards at the Tower search the carts. You talk your way through, and your heart doesn't slow down for an hour.

events.title: The Temple of Paladine
events.scene: Since the war the true gods are back, and the Temple of Paladine in Palanthas sends its clerics out across Solamnia. One of them sets up in a barn, healing whoever comes, and asks for helpers who don't faint at blood.

choices.text: Help with the sick

outcomes.text: You carry water, hold hands, learn to set a bone. The cleric says you have a gift that isn't only in your hands.
You see a dying child get up. You stop asking whether the gods are real.
You catch the fever yourself, and the cleric sits with you through the worst night.

choices.text: Keep your distance; gods have failed before

outcomes.text: You remember who the people blamed for the Cataclysm. You wait to see what these new priests want.
You stay away, but you keep finding reasons to walk past the barn.

events.title: A Knight Needs a Squire
events.scene: A Knight of the Crown, getting old, needs a squire: someone to keep the armour, the horse and the accounts, and maybe, after years of it, to be put forward for the Knighthood. Someone has told the knight about you.

choices.text: Kneel and take the service

outcomes.text: You swear the squire's oath. Your days now begin before the knight's and end after.
The knight is harsh and the other squires are noble-born. You learn the sword, and you learn to swallow things.
The knight turns out to care more about the Measure's books than its battles. You learn both.

choices.text: Say you aren't made for oaths

outcomes.text: The knight nods as if expecting it. Later, you hear the place went to someone you dislike.
Your family does not forgive you quickly. An honour turned down is still talked about at dinner.

choices.text: Offer to serve for a year, without an oath

outcomes.text: A year without an oath, agreed. It turns into three.
The knight says the Oath is the point. You go home with a story and a bruise to your pride.

events.title: The Free City
events.scene: Solanthus has thrown the Knights out. The guildmasters rule now, and the Knights' Hall is a wool warehouse. People cheer in the square; an old knight is pelted as he leaves through the gate.

choices.text: Cheer with the crowd

outcomes.text: You feel the city become yours for a day. The guilds remember who cheered.
The cheering turns into stones. You see a man knocked down and kicked, and you don't stop cheering in time.

choices.text: Follow the old knight out of the gate

outcomes.text: You carry his bag a mile. He gives you a ring he can no longer wear in the city, and a word of thanks.
Someone sees you. For years, your family is the one that helped the Knights.

events.title: The Blue Army
events.scene: Spring, 351. The dragonarmies come over the plains from the east and the south: Kalaman has fallen, Vingaard Keep has fallen, Solanthus has fallen. Blue dragons in the sky, and on the road, people carrying everything they own towards Palanthas.

choices.text: Take the road to Palanthas with the others

outcomes.text: Weeks on a road full of the hungry. You reach the walls of Palanthas with nothing but your family.
In the crush at a ford, you lose someone's hand. You reach Palanthas without them.
A dragon passes low over the column. The fear takes everyone; you find yourself face down in a ditch, and you never quite stop listening for wings.

choices.text: Stay, and keep your head down

outcomes.text: The Blue army takes the grain and the horses and leaves the people. Mostly.
Soldiers take your neighbours to dig earthworks. You are hidden in the hay and hear everything.
At night, you carry food to the men hiding in the hills. If you'd been caught, they would have hanged you.

events.title: The Winter the Tower Held
events.scene: The Blue army is camped below the High Clerist's Tower, the last thing between it and Palanthas. In the city they are asking for anyone who can carry, cook or bind wounds to go up to the Tower. The Knights are few, hungry and quarrelling.

choices.text: Go up to the Tower

outcomes.text: You carry sacks up the pass in the snow. On the last night you hear the dragons scream inside the Tower, and then the silence. It held.
You bind wounds until your hands stop feeling. A knight dies holding your sleeve.
Someone hands you a spear and puts you on a wall. You don't remember the fight, only the morning after.

choices.text: Stay in the city and help there

outcomes.text: The city is full of refugees from the plains. You find a use, and people remember it.
You watch the city's lords argue about whether the war is their business. You learn what power looks like when it's afraid.

events.title: The Golden General
events.scene: 352. An army comes out of Palanthas behind an elf woman in golden armour, with knights riding dragons that fight for them. The Blue army breaks and runs east. Solamnia is free, and furious with those who did well under the occupation.

choices.text: Run to see the army pass

outcomes.text: You see her ride by, close enough to see she looks tired. You decide that's what heroes look like.
You follow the army for a week, doing whatever they let you. A sergeant sends you home with a pat and a ration.
A silver dragon lands in the square. You touch its scale before anyone can stop you.

choices.text: Watch what the neighbours do to the collaborators

outcomes.text: You point out the miller who fed the Blue army. You were right, and it still feels wrong.
You hide a woman the crowd is hunting. Maybe she deserved it. You don't care.
You go home. Freedom looks a lot like the war from where you stand.

events.title: The Dead Come to Palanthas
events.scene: The Blue Lady comes back. Her army marches on Palanthas, and with it Lord Soth and his dead warriors, who walk through the New City as if the walls were mist. The adults bar the doors and say prayers to gods they only recently learned to trust.

choices.text: Hide, and keep the little ones quiet

outcomes.text: You hold your breath behind a door while something cold walks past. It doesn't stop. You're still not sure why.
You lead three children through the cellars to the temple, and none of them cries. Afterwards, the priests ask your name.

choices.text: Look out at the street

outcomes.text: You see the dead knight himself, and he turns his burning eyes to your window. You stop being afraid of anything else.
You see the city's defenders fight dead men and die. You learn their names afterwards and keep them.

place.solanthus.scene: The Blue Lady comes back and throws her army against Palanthas, with a dead knight and his dead warriors among her troops. Refugees from the north fill the roads past Solanthus with stories nobody wants to believe, and the city closes its gates.

events.title: The Knights Return
events.scene: The Knights of Solamnia are not the outcasts of your parents' stories any more. Lord Gunthar uth Wistan, their Grand Master, has set out to revise the old Oath and Measure, and his knights are rebuilding keeps and looking for new blood.

choices.text: Hire on to help rebuild a keep

outcomes.text: A season of stone and mortar. The knights work beside you, and that surprises you most.
A knight sees you in a brawl and asks if you've ever thought about squiring.

choices.text: Remember what the Knights did before

outcomes.text: Rebuilt keeps mean rebuilt taxes. You've heard the old folk.
You argue about it with a young knight in a tavern and find, to your annoyance, that you like him.

events.title: The Knights Despised
events.scene: Three centuries after the Cataclysm, Solamnia still blames its Knights for it. Today a knight in old, carefully mended armour rides through the market, and the crowd throws mud and worse. He doesn't draw his sword. He doesn't even speed up.

choices.text: Step out and stand beside him

outcomes.text: The crowd loses interest. At the edge of town he thanks you, and tells you a little of the Oath and the Measure.
You get the mud too. Your family is furious. You're not sorry.

choices.text: Stay in the crowd

outcomes.text: You watch him ride on, straight-backed, and something about it stays with you longer than the jeering.
You throw something too. Years later, you'll remember his face when he looked back.

events.title: The Black Knights at the Gates
events.scene: 383. The Knights of Takhisis land in the north and march on Palanthas, and the city's lords open the gates rather than see it burn again. In the south the Knights of Solamnia hold the High Clerist's Tower and lose a battle on the plains that nobody expected them to lose.

choices.text: Go south to the High Clerist's Tower

outcomes.text: You stand on the walls when the black knights come. Then something worse comes for both armies, and the war changes shape overnight.
You're wounded on the plain before you reach the Tower, and carried there on a cart full of dying men.

choices.text: Stay in the city and see what the new masters are like

outcomes.text: They are orderly, disciplined and polite. That is somehow the worst part.
You join the people who keep lists of the collaborators, for later.

events.title: The Blue in the North
events.scene: A great blue dragon has made the lands around Palanthas his own, with the Knights of Neraka as his hands. Lightning walks the plains when he is displeased. The old Knights of Solamnia hold what they can in the south, and argue.

choices.text: Carry goods north, under the dragon's peace

outcomes.text: The roads are safe, as long as everyone pays. You get rich, and you don't feel good about it.
One summer you're on the road when he flies over. The lightning misses you by a field's width.

choices.text: Ride with the Knights in the south

outcomes.text: They are fewer than the songs say, and better. You learn their ways in a hard school.
You learn that the Knights spend as much time fighting each other's opinions as the dragon.

events.title: The Fall of Solanthus
events.scene: 421. Solanthus, the Knights' stronghold, falls in a single night to the girl Mina and her army, with no siege engines at all: she prays, and the walls are hers. The survivors stream south in the rain.

choices.text: Get the wounded out of the city

outcomes.text: You carry people through the gates until morning. You never learn most of their names.
You are taken prisoner, and released a month later with everyone else who wouldn't kneel. You still wouldn't.

choices.text: Guard the refugees on the road south

outcomes.text: A week of mud and fear. Everyone you were guarding reaches safety.
Not everyone. You remember the ones who didn't.

events.title: The Half-Ogre's War
events.scene: 425. A half-ogre warlord named Ankhar comes down out of the mountains with an army of ogres and hobgoblins, and Solamnia, still divided, can barely hold. A man named Jaymes Markham, made Lord Marshal, is gathering anyone who can fight.

choices.text: Join the Lord Marshal's army

outcomes.text: Three years of war. When Ankhar falls, you're there, and the Marshal knows your face.
You win, and then watch the Marshal crown himself Emperor of Solamnia. You're not sure what you fought for.

choices.text: Defend your own village

outcomes.text: The village holds when the raiders come. The ogres go round it the next time.
The village burns. You get the children out, and that's all you get out.

events.title: Your First Colours
events.scene: The clan elder mixes the paints: red earth, white clay, the black of burned bark. Today she will paint your face for the first time, and the pattern she chooses will say something about who the clan thinks you are. She asks you which animal you dreamed of last night.

choices.text: Tell her the truth: a white owl

outcomes.text: She paints the owl's eyes around yours. The clan calls you watchful after that, and it comes true.
She goes very quiet, and paints a pattern nobody has worn in her lifetime. She won't say what it means.

choices.text: Say a bear, because bears are better

outcomes.text: She paints the bear's claws on your cheeks and laughs at you a little. You grow into them anyway.
She looks at you a long time and paints a fox instead. Everyone laughs except her.

events.title: Tusks on the Ice
events.scene: South of the forest the land turns white, and out on the ice live the thanoi: walrus-headed hunters with tusks as long as your arm. Today a hunting band of them has come close enough to see, dragging a seal across the snow, and one of them has seen you.

choices.text: Stay absolutely still, the way the hunters taught you

outcomes.text: It sniffs the wind, grunts, and moves on. You don't move until dark, and you don't stop shaking until morning.
It comes for you. You run, and the forest takes you in. You have dreams about tusks for years.

choices.text: Run to warn the camp

outcomes.text: The hunters are ready when the thanoi come in the night. Nobody dies. The elders mark your name.
You're in time for most of them. Not for the dogs.

events.title: The Long Hunt
events.scene: The great autumn hunt: the whole clan follows the deer herds for a month, sleeping in the trees. This year you carry a bow. On the ninth day you have a stag in your sights, an old one, the herd leader, and the elder beside you says nothing at all.

choices.text: Take the shot

outcomes.text: A clean kill. The clan eats well all winter and sings your name at the fire, once, which is a great deal.
You wound it. You follow its trail for two days, alone, until you can finish what you started. Nobody mentions it after.

choices.text: Lower the bow; the herd needs its leader

outcomes.text: The elder nods. Later she tells you that was the test, and that most fail it.
It's a hungry winter. Some of the clan think you were wise, and some think you were soft.

events.title: The Ogre Toll
events.scene: Ogres from Daltigoth, the old imperial capital, have come for their tribute: grain from the villages, furs from the forest. This year the ogre chief's collector wants a third more, and he wants it from your people today.

choices.text: Pay, and live to plant again

outcomes.text: You pay. The winter is lean, and you hate the ogres in a cold, patient way.
You pay what they can see. What they can't see is in a pit under the barn, and you dug it.

choices.text: Stand with the young ones who won't pay

outcomes.text: The collector goes back empty-handed with a broken arm. The ogres don't come back that year. They will.
It goes badly. The ogres burn a barn and take twice the tribute. Some of the elders never forgive you.

choices.text: Get the collector drunk and confused

outcomes.text: He leaves with half what he came for and a story about being robbed by goblins. You learn ogres can count, but not well.
He can hold his drink better than you can. You wake up owing the ogres personally.

events.title: The Vale of Mist
events.scene: In the mountains there is a vale where hot springs meet the cold air and the mist never lifts. The Kagonesti speak of a tomb there, of a knight from the old stories, and of something silver that guards it. A friend wants to go and see. Nobody who goes talks much about it after.

choices.text: Go into the mist

outcomes.text: You find the tomb, and stand before it for an hour, and come away with a feeling you have no words for.
In the mist you glimpse something huge and silver move, and then it's gone. You never tell anyone.

choices.text: Stay at the edge and wait

outcomes.text: Your friend comes back after a day and won't talk about it. You've always wondered.
Your friend doesn't come back for three days. When they do, they've decided to become a priest of a god nobody worships any more.

events.title: Your House
events.scene: In Silvanost, everyone knows their House, and their House's place. Today you are taken to the Tower of the Stars for the first time, and stand in the place where children of your House stand, behind the ones before you and ahead of the ones behind. A Kagonesti servant child, of House Servitor, stands behind everyone.

choices.text: Stand exactly where you were placed

outcomes.text: Your mother says you did your House credit. You feel the honour of it all the way home.
Standing so still, you see the Tower properly: the light through its crystal, the old songs carved in it. You never forget it.

choices.text: Look back at the servant child

outcomes.text: The child smiles. It is the most interesting thing that happens all day, and the start of something your House would not like.
A steward sees you and corrects you, gently. You learn there is a right way to look at people, and that you don't agree with it.

events.title: The Speaker of the Stars
events.scene: You are chosen to carry a lamp in the procession of the Speaker of the Stars, Lorac Caladon, through Silvanost. Close up he looks tired, and older than an elf should. As he passes, he stops and asks you, quite simply, what you would do if the world ended again.

choices.text: Say you would stay, and keep Silvanesti as it is

outcomes.text: He smiles, as if you had said exactly what he hoped. The courtiers repeat your answer for a decade.
He nods and walks on, and you think, though you can never be sure, that he looked sad.

choices.text: Say you would go and help whoever was left

outcomes.text: He looks at you a long moment. 'Perhaps that is the braver answer.' Your House is mortified.
His daughter, walking behind him, catches your eye and almost laughs. You decide you like her.

events.title: The Speaker's Silence
events.scene: Whispers in Silvanost: the Speaker has stopped receiving his ministers; a delegation from the dark armies in the east was seen leaving the Tower; there is talk of an agreement, that the armies will pass Silvanesti by. House Protector is told to stand down from the eastern border.

choices.text: Trust the Speaker; he sees further than you

outcomes.text: You trust him. For a time, it even seems wise.
You trust him, and sleep badly, and start keeping a pack ready by the door.

choices.text: Ask the wrong person the wrong questions

outcomes.text: An old mage of House Mystic tells you the Speaker has been talking to something in the dark of the Tower. She won't say what.
Nobody answers. But from then on, someone always seems to know where you are.

events.title: Two Courts in Exile
events.scene: Two elven courts on one island: the Qualinesti in Qualimori, the Silvanesti in Silvamori, each certain it is the true heart of the elves. They quarrel over land, over precedence, over who speaks for whom, while the Kagonesti watch them both from the trees.

choices.text: Carry messages between the two courts

outcomes.text: You become the one both courts trust to carry a message without changing it. That is rarer than it sounds.
When a message goes wrong, both courts blame the messenger.

choices.text: Stand firmly with your own people

outcomes.text: Your people remember who stood with them in exile. The other court remembers too.
Standing with your own people means standing over the Kagonesti who build your walls. You start to notice them.

events.title: The Wardens of the Woods
events.scene: The Kagonesti clans keep wardens: hunters who range the whole island, read every trail, and carry word between clans. One of them, grey and scarred, has walked into your camp and asked for you by name. She needs someone who can run all day and keep quiet all night.

choices.text: Go with her

outcomes.text: Years on the trails, from the northern plain to the edge of the ice. You learn the whole island by its smell.
Her work turns out to be mostly killing: ogre raiders, thanoi, goblins. You learn the spear and the bow very well.
She teaches you the old prayers of the hunt, the ones the elders half forgot.

choices.text: Stay with your people

outcomes.text: She shrugs and goes. The trails go on without you.
You stay, and every time a warden passes through you ask about the trails.

events.title: The Ships of Silvanesti
events.scene: 349. The dark armies have broken their word and are marching on Silvanesti. The Speaker of the Stars orders his people to leave: ships, all of them, west across the sea to Southern Ergoth. He alone will stay behind. Silvanost empties in a week.

choices.text: Board with your House

outcomes.text: From the deck you watch the Tower of the Stars until it is gone. In Southern Ergoth your people found Silvamori, and wait.
On the island you watch your House put the Kagonesti to work building the new city. Nobody asks them.

choices.text: Beg to stay with the Speaker's guard

outcomes.text: You are refused, kindly, and put on the last ship. Later you are glad, and ashamed of being glad.
You stay a few days too long, and see the first shadows move wrong in the forest. You barely reach the coast.

events.title: Sails from the East
events.scene: Ships, dozens of them, on the eastern horizon: first the Silvanesti in 349, then, two years later, the Qualinesti, a whole people each, fleeing the dragonarmies. They land, they claim the forest, and before the season turns their stewards are coming into the Kagonesti camps with chains and lists. The cities will need builders.

choices.text: Take your people deeper into the forest

outcomes.text: You stay ahead of the stewards all year. Many others don't.
They find the camp. You spend the next years building the walls of a city for people who call you servant.

choices.text: Go to the newcomers and trade

outcomes.text: Furs for steel, game for cloth. You learn how the city elves think, and keep your people's camps secret.
They trade with you for a month, and then they take you.

culture.foreign.scene: 349. Ships, dozens of them, on the eastern horizon: elves, a whole people, fleeing the dragonarmies, and two years later another people behind them. They land, claim the forest, and send envoys to your village to buy grain, and to warn you that the dragons may follow them. Within the season, their stewards are dragging the wild elves out of the forest to build.

events.title: The Builders
events.scene: On the island, your masters' people are building a city in a hurry, and every Kagonesti they hold is put to it, you among them: felling, hauling, digging, while the free clans watch from the trees. One night a free hunter slips into the camp and whispers that the forest is wide.

choices.text: Run with the hunter

outcomes.text: Three days of running. On the fourth a clan takes you in, paints your face, and gives you a name your masters never knew.
They bring you back. The punishment is public, and you are watched from then on.

choices.text: Stay, for the others who can't run

outcomes.text: You become the one the others come to: who stands between them and the steward, and takes what that costs.
You build their walls well, because they're your walls too, in a way your masters will never understand.

events.title: The Strangers and the Silver Maid
events.scene: Winter, 351. Shipwrecked strangers have washed up on the island: humans, a dwarf, a kender, and the Qualinesti Speaker's own daughter among them. They are held in Qualimori, and argued over. Then one night they are gone, and so is a Kagonesti girl with silver hair who served in the exiles' houses.

choices.text: Help them on their way, and say nothing

outcomes.text: You show them a trail. Months later the songs reach the island: dragon lances, the knights, a war turned. You know you were part of it, a little.
You help them, and someone sees. You keep your head down for a year.

choices.text: Tell the guard which way they went

outcomes.text: The guard never finds them. Later, when the songs come, you keep quiet about your part.
You're thanked. Later, when the songs come, you're less sure you were right.

events.title: White Wings over the Island
events.scene: 352. The dragonarmies come to Southern Ergoth after all: white dragons out of the south, soldiers landing on the coast, the island's camps and villages burning or hiding. For a season, nobody on the island is anyone's master except the dragons'.

choices.text: Hide in the forest with whoever's nearest

outcomes.text: Elf, Kagonesti, human, half-elf: in the forest that winter nobody asks. You share a fire with people who'd never have spoken to you before.
The dragon's breath freezes the camp. You survive. Not everyone does.

choices.text: Fight with the elves and the Knights' outpost

outcomes.text: A long, bitter season of skirmishes in the snow. When the dragonarmies pull out, you're one of the ones still standing.
Frost and steel. You lose the feeling in two fingers forever.

events.title: Word from Silvanesti
events.scene: Word comes back from those who went to look: the war is over, but Silvanesti is not. The Speaker's magic failed and twisted the forest into a waking nightmare. The trees bleed, the dead walk, and he lies dreaming at the heart of it. Your home is still there, and nobody can live in it.

choices.text: Swear to go back and take it back

outcomes.text: You swear it with others who feel the same. It will take longer than you imagine.
You go with the first band that tries. You come back with fewer friends, and dreams you'll never lose.

choices.text: Let it go; build something new

outcomes.text: You put your century into the exile city. Some of your House call it betrayal; you call it living.
You don't let it go. You just stop talking about it.

events.title: House Servitor Goes to Sea
events.scene: 349. The Speaker of the Stars has ordered Silvanesti emptied before the dark armies arrive. The Houses are taking ship for Southern Ergoth, and House Servitor, which is to say you and every Kagonesti in Silvanost, goes with them to carry and to build. Somebody on the docks says the island is full of wild elves who serve nobody.

choices.text: Board with your masters' household

outcomes.text: Across the sea, and straight to work: Silvamori goes up on Kagonesti backs, while the free clans watch from the trees.
On the island, a free hunter speaks to you in a language you only half remember from your grandmother. She tells you where her clan camps.

choices.text: Hide in the city and let the ships go

outcomes.text: You stay in an empty Silvanost, and see what the Speaker's magic does to it. You barely get out alive, and you never speak of it.
You slip away east, into lands at war, free and alone. You never see Silvanost again.

events.title: The First Elves
events.scene: A company of Qualinesti elves has landed on the coast with tools, seed and a great deal of courtesy, and begun to clear a site in the forest for a town. They say they are settlers. They are building far too much for settlers.

choices.text: Watch them from the trees

outcomes.text: You count the houses they lay out: enough for a whole people. You tell the elders, who go very quiet.
One of them spots you and waves, friendly, and offers you a loaf. You take it. It's very good bread.

choices.text: Go and work for them, for pay

outcomes.text: They pay in steel tools. You learn how city elves build, and how they talk about your people when they think you can't hear.
When you want to leave, the steward reminds you of a debt you didn't know you had.

events.title: The Ogres' Tribute
events.scene: The ogres who hold old Daltigoth raid further every year: cattle, grain and sometimes people. The Ergothian villages pay what they're told; the Kagonesti clans melt into the forest and come back with arrows.

choices.text: Set an ambush on the raiders' road

outcomes.text: The ogres lose three of their own and go round your valley next year.
The ambush goes wrong. You carry the wounded home through the snow.

choices.text: Pay the tribute and live

outcomes.text: A thin winter. Everyone lives. The young ones call it cowardice.
The ogres take a neighbour's son as well as the grain. You never see him again.

events.title: The Ice Comes North
events.scene: 395. A white dragon greater than any before, Gellidus, claims Southern Ergoth, and the island freezes. Snow in summer, ice over the forests, rivers stopped in their beds. In one year, a green island becomes a glacier.

choices.text: Stay, and learn to live in the ice

outcomes.text: The Kagonesti teach anyone who listens how to hunt and hide in a white land. You listen.
The first winter takes the old and the very young. You bury them in the snow.

choices.text: Find a boat to the mainland

outcomes.text: You sail for Abanasinia with nothing. Behind you the island goes white to the shore.
The boat nearly founders in the ice. You land half-frozen, and alive.

events.title: The Harbour with No Sea
events.scene: The great harbour of Tarsis: stone quays, bollards, warehouses, and hundreds of ships sitting in the dry dust where the sea used to be, three hundred years after the Cataclysm pushed the shore fifty miles away. The children play pirates on the decks. Today you find a cabin nobody has opened since the water left.

choices.text: Force the door

outcomes.text: Inside: a captain's logbook, the last entry dated the day before the Cataclysm. You read it a hundred times.
Inside: the captain, still at his table. You run. Later, you go back and bury him properly.

choices.text: Tell the old harbourmaster

outcomes.text: He comes with a lantern and tells you the name of every ship in that row, and what it carried, and where it was going.
He claims the cabin for the Lords of Tarsis, and gives you a coin for your honesty. You wonder what was really in there.

events.title: The Library Nobody Opens
events.scene: Somewhere in the old quarter of Tarsis there is a library that nobody has used in two hundred years, its doors chained, its books still on the shelves. You've found a window with a broken shutter.

choices.text: Climb in and read until dark, every day

outcomes.text: Histories, maps, treatises on dragons that everyone says never existed. You start to think everyone is wrong.
In a locked case, a book whose letters move. You take it home under your shirt.

choices.text: Tell the Lords of Tarsis it should be opened

outcomes.text: The Lords say books are for scholars and Tarsis has no use for those. You learn what the city has become.
An old lord, more curious than the rest, gives you the key and the title of keeper, unpaid.

events.title: The Lords of Tarsis
events.scene: The Lords of Tarsis sit in judgement on a stranger: a knight of Solamnia, of all things, in a city that still blames the Knights for the Cataclysm. The crowd wants him thrown out of the gates. You saw what happened in the market, and he didn't start it.

choices.text: Speak for the knight

outcomes.text: The Lords let him go, grudgingly. He thanks you and gives you a book of the Measure.
He's thrown out anyway, and you're known for a year as the one who stood up for a Knight.

choices.text: Stay quiet; it's not your quarrel

outcomes.text: He's put out of the gates. You watch him walk into the dust, and wonder where he'll find water.
You watch how the Lords decide things: never by the facts. It's an education.

events.title: The Clans at the Walls
events.scene: The nomad clans of the Plains of Dust have come to the walls of Tarsis: to trade, they say, though there are a great many of them, and they are all armed. The gates are shut. From the walls you can see their children, staring back at you.

choices.text: Sneak out to the trading ground

outcomes.text: A nomad child swaps you a carved horse for your knife. You meet again every season for years.
The guard catches you coming back. Your family pays a fine, and you get a story.

choices.text: Watch from the walls with the guards

outcomes.text: A guard teaches you to count riders, read banners and tell a trading party from a war party. They were both.
You see a fight break out at the gate, and a man die. You understand why the walls are there.

culture.dust.scene: Your clan has come with the others to the walls of Tarsis, to trade salt and hides for iron and grain. The city's gates are shut, and the people on the walls stare at you as if you were wolves. Your grandmother says they always do, and that their grandparents were the same.

events.title: The Last Well
events.scene: A dry year. The clan has reached the well that was always there, and it's dry too. The next one is four days away, if it holds water, and another clan is said to be heading for it. The speaker of your clan asks the young ones to run ahead.

choices.text: Run ahead to the next well

outcomes.text: You get there first, half dead, and hold it until the clan arrives. They sing about it for a while.
The other clan is already there. You talk, instead of fighting, and both clans drink. The elders don't know what to make of you.

choices.text: Dig the old well deeper

outcomes.text: Two days of digging, and then mud, and then water. The clan stays a month. You are given a new name for it.
Nothing. You lose an animal on the road to the next well, and learn what the dust can do.

events.title: The Centaur Treaty
events.scene: The centaur tribes of the northern plains and the human clans have been feuding over grazing since before anyone's grandmother. This year both sides have agreed to talk, at a dry riverbed halfway between, and both sides want someone they can trust to carry the words.

choices.text: Carry the words between them

outcomes.text: It takes a month and a great deal of patience, but there's a treaty. It holds, mostly, for ten years.
It falls apart on the last day, and both sides blame the messenger.

choices.text: Guard the meeting from the hotheads

outcomes.text: Two young hotheads try to start a fight. You stop them. Nobody thanks you, which is how you know you did it right.
The fight starts anyway. You end it, and it costs you a scar.

events.title: The Salt Caravan
events.scene: A caravan master runs salt, hides and iron between Tarsis, the dust clans and the dwarves of the Kharolis, a route that takes a year and kills someone every trip. She needs someone who can bargain, ride and keep their head. She's heard of you.

choices.text: Join the caravan

outcomes.text: Years on the salt road. You learn three languages, every well, and the price of everything.
You end up as the caravan's guard more than its trader. The road teaches you to fight.
A sandstorm scatters the caravan. You lead the survivors home by the stars.

choices.text: Stay; the road eats people

outcomes.text: The caravan leaves without you. Not all of it comes back.
You stay, and every time the caravan bells come through the gate, you go to look.

events.title: Strangers Looking for Ships
events.scene: Late 351. A band of strangers walks into Tarsis asking for ships to carry refugees away from the dragonarmies: ships, in Tarsis, where the sea left three hundred years ago. The whole city laughs. One of them is a Knight of Solamnia, which doesn't help.

choices.text: Laugh with the city

outcomes.text: You laugh. A few days later, you stop laughing.
You laugh, and then you hear what they're running from. You go home and pack.

choices.text: Point them to someone who can help

outcomes.text: You send them to the old library. They find something in it. You'll never know what.
You show them to an inn that won't throw them out. That night, the dragons come.

events.title: Dragons over Tarsis
events.scene: Winter, 351. The Red Dragonarmy comes to Tarsis without warning: dragons over the dry harbour, fire in the old quarter, soldiers at the gates someone opened from inside. By morning, half the city is ash and the rest belongs to the Highlord.

choices.text: Run for the plains

outcomes.text: You get out through a breach in the wall and walk into the dust with nothing. The clans take you in, for a price.
In the smoke you lose your family's hands. You find them again a month later, in a camp on the plains. Not all of them.

choices.text: Pull people out of the burning streets

outcomes.text: You save four people, and burn your arms doing it. One of them comes to find you years later.
Soldiers catch you in the street. You spend the winter clearing rubble under guard.

culture.dust.scene: Winter, 351. From the plains you see the glow over Tarsis: dragons over the city, the old harbour burning. By dawn, refugees are stumbling out into the dust towards your clan's fires, and dragonarmy riders are behind them.

events.title: Under the Highlord
events.scene: 352. The dragonarmies hold the land around Tarsis: patrols on the salt roads, tribute from the clans, soldiers billeted in the houses that didn't burn. Some people bend, some hide, and some start keeping lists of names for later.

choices.text: Help the people who fight back

outcomes.text: Messages, food and once a knife, for the people in the hills. When the war ends, you're on the right list.
A patrol catches you with a message. You escape, and spend the rest of the war in the dust.
