choices.text: Keep your head down and survive

outcomes.text: You get through it. It takes a long time to stop flinching at dragonarmy colours.
Survival means trading with the occupiers. You do it, and the city remembers.

events.title: Tarsis Rebuilds
events.scene: The years after the war. Tarsis rebuilds its burned quarter, the Lords quarrel over who pays, and for the first time anyone remembers, there's talk of a road to the new coast, fifty miles away, and a real harbour on it.

choices.text: Work on the road to the coast

outcomes.text: Years of digging and arguing. The first cart reaches the sea while you watch, and the whole crew weeps.
The Lords stop paying after six miles. The road ends in the dust. You learn about Tarsis.

choices.text: Rebuild your own street

outcomes.text: Your street is rebuilt in new stone. You know every block of it.
You do well out of the rebuilding. Some say too well.

events.title: Elves Crossing the Dust
events.scene: 349. Columns of elves are crossing the Plains of Dust, westward: Silvanesti, a whole people, walking away from their forest with everything they can carry. They don't stop at Tarsis and they don't explain. Behind them, the nomads say, the sky over Silvanesti has gone the wrong colour.

choices.text: Go out and trade with them

outcomes.text: They pay in silver and jewels for water and bread, and never look you in the eye. One old elf thanks you, and that's all.
A young elf, younger-looking than you, tells you what they're running from. You don't sleep that night.

choices.text: Guide them to the wells on the western road

outcomes.text: A week with the elves. They are cold, proud and quite lost, and they never forget who found them water.
A dust clan comes for their silver. You talk the clan out of it, barely.

events.title: The Hatred of Tarsis
events.scene: When the sea left Tarsis, the city blamed the Knights who had failed to stop it, and drove them out. Three hundred years later, the hatred is still taught in Tarsian schools. Today the children are taken to the ruin of the old Knights' hall, to throw stones at it.

choices.text: Throw your stone with the rest

outcomes.text: You belong. It feels good. Later, you wonder why.
Your stone breaks a window and something inside sighs. Nobody else hears it.

choices.text: Ask what the Knights actually did

outcomes.text: An old teacher tells you the truth, quietly: they did nothing, because nothing could have been done.
You're sent home. Your father isn't angry; he looks proud, then afraid.

events.title: Dragons of the Eastern Plains
events.scene: Two great dragons have carved out realms in the eastern Plains of Dust and now demand tribute from every clan and caravan that crosses them. The dust clans move their herds west, and the salt road changes for the first time in a century.

choices.text: Ride with the caravan that pays

outcomes.text: You pay, and pass, and see a dragon close enough to count its teeth.
The price is more than gold: one of the drivers is kept. Nobody argues.

choices.text: Find a new road round their lands

outcomes.text: Two months of scouting, and a new road through the western wells. The clans use it for a generation.
The new road nearly kills you. You bring back a map of what not to do.

events.title: The Life-Tree
events.scene: Your first trip across the Urkhan Sea on the cable boats, holding the rail. Ahead, hanging from the roof of the world, is the Life-Tree: a stalactite a quarter of a mile wide with a whole city carved inside it, water running down its sides, and four shafts of real sunlight standing around it like pillars.

choices.text: Stare at the sunlight

outcomes.text: Your uncle says it comes from a thing called the sky, far above. You decide you'll see it one day.
You stare too long and see spots for a day. Light, you decide, is not to be trusted.

choices.text: Ask how they carved it

outcomes.text: A Hylar engineer on the boat explains it all the way across, with drawings on the back of a ledger. You understand about half.
An old Daewar tells you it was a gift of Reorx, and the engineer on the boat snorts. You learn that clans argue about everything.

clan.hylar.scene: You were born in the Life-Tree, and today, for the first time, your father takes you down to the waterfront at its foot to look up. Water runs down the stone, the Urkhan Sea laps at the wharves, and four shafts of real sunlight stand around the city like pillars.

events.title: The Cable Boats
events.scene: The cable boats run on great chains across the Urkhan Sea, linking the cities. Today the chain has jammed halfway, the boat is stuck in the dark over deep water, and the passengers are from three different clans. Somebody has already blamed the Theiwar.

choices.text: Climb out along the chain to free it

outcomes.text: You find the jammed link and kick it free. The boat cheers, all three clans at once, which nobody has ever heard before.
You fall into the Urkhan Sea. It's very cold and very black. A Klar boatman fishes you out, laughing.

choices.text: Stop the argument before it becomes a fight

outcomes.text: You get them telling jokes about the ferrymen instead. The boat moves again before anyone throws a punch.
Too late. You end up in the middle of it with a black eye and a Theiwar's ring in your pocket, which you didn't take.

events.title: The Closed Mountain
events.scene: Above the village, Cloudseeker Mountain. Inside it, the mountain dwarves, who shut the gates on your ancestors when the world ended and the Neidar came starving to the door. Your grandfather still spits when he says the word Thorbardin. Today a trader from inside has come down to sell iron.

choices.text: Spit like your grandfather

outcomes.text: Your grandfather is proud. The trader doesn't come back, and the village pays more for iron that year.
The trader looks at you, an old dwarf, tired, and says his grandfather was turned away too, the other way. You don't know what to do with that.

choices.text: Ask the trader what it's like inside

outcomes.text: He tells you about the Life-Tree and the cable boats and the Council of Thanes. You dream about it for years.
You end up helping him sell to your own village, at a fair price. Your grandfather doesn't speak to you for a month.

events.title: Clan Against Clan
events.scene: The great market at the crossroads of the Tenth Road. A Theiwar and a Daewar are shouting over a price, then over a grandfather, then over a war three hundred years old. The Hylar guard is slow to come. Everyone is waiting to see which way the young ones jump.

choices.text: Stand with your own clan, whatever the rights of it

outcomes.text: A proper brawl. The guard breaks it up, the clans each pay a fine, and your clan elders buy you a drink.
Somebody brings a knife. You take it in the arm, and your clan never forgets that you stood.

choices.text: Ask both of them what the price actually was

outcomes.text: It comes down to two copper. You pay the difference yourself, and both of them stop shouting from sheer surprise.
Both of them turn on you instead. You learn that some quarrels are older than the question.

choices.text: Watch, and notice who started it on purpose

outcomes.text: A third dwarf, Theiwar, leaves quietly once the fists start. You follow him, and see who he reports to.
You see it, and say nothing. You'll find out later what it was for.

clan.theiwar.scene: The great market at the crossroads of the Tenth Road. One of your clan is shouting at a Daewar over a price, then over a grandfather, then over a war three hundred years old. Everyone else in the market already thinks the Theiwar started it. The Hylar guard is slow to come.

clan.klar.scene: The great market at the crossroads of the Tenth Road. A Theiwar and a Daewar are at each other's throats, and the Klar around you are grinning. Klar love a fight, and serve the Hylar, and the Hylar guard is slow to come. Everyone is waiting to see which way the young ones jump.

events.title: The Sky
events.scene: Thorbardin has kept its gates shut since the Dwarfgate War, more than three hundred years ago. Most dwarves inside have never seen the sky. But the light shafts have to be cleaned, and the crew that climbs up them to the surface is one hand short.

choices.text: Join the crew and climb

outcomes.text: Hours of climbing, then wind. Then a blue so big you have to hold on to the rock. You don't say anything for the rest of the day.
You come out into a mountain storm and nearly die of it. You see lightning, which nobody below will believe.

choices.text: Stay below; the mountain is enough

outcomes.text: The crew goes without you. You turn your mind to the work in front of you, and get very good at it.
You stay, and ask everyone who went up what it was like, until they tell you to go and see.

year>=353.scene: Since the war, Northgate stands open for trade, and dwarves who have never seen the sky are going out to look at it in twos and threes, holding on to each other. A cousin asks if you'll come.

events.title: The Deep Forges
events.scene: A master smith will take one apprentice this decade. The test is simple: forge a single nail, by hand, in front of her. She has turned away eleven dwarves this year, and she's watching your hands, not the nail.

choices.text: Take all day over it

outcomes.text: The best nail of your life. She looks at it, puts it in her pocket, and tells you to come back tomorrow, early.
A good nail, too slowly made. She sends you away. You make a nail every day for a year and come back.

choices.text: Make it fast and true, the way you were taught

outcomes.text: She nods once. 'You don't think. Good. Thinking can be taught.'
You burn your hand on the stock, finish the nail anyway, and don't make a sound. She takes you, for that.

events.title: The Council of Thanes
events.scene: The Council of Thanes meets in the Life-Tree, one thane for each clan, and nothing gets done without most of them. Your thane needs someone to carry his argument into the side rooms, where the real work happens: should Thorbardin ever open its gates again?

choices.text: Argue for opening the gates

outcomes.text: The Hylar listen. The Theiwar smile and say nothing, and you learn later that smiling Theiwar is a bad sign.
Shouted down by three clans at once. Your thane is pleased; he needed someone to say it first.

choices.text: Argue for keeping them shut

outcomes.text: You're on the winning side, as everyone has been for three hundred years. It feels oddly hollow.
A Theiwar adviser compliments your speech and offers you a drink. And another, and a friendship.

events.title: The Theiwar's Offer
events.scene: A soft-voiced Theiwar has been buying you drinks for a month. Tonight he gets to the point: someone outside the mountain will pay very well to know when the Northgate watch changes, and how many stand it. He calls it trade.

choices.text: Refuse, and tell the Hylar guard

outcomes.text: The guard thanks you and does nothing you can see. The Theiwar stops buying drinks, and starts watching you.
Word goes up to the Hylar thane himself. Months later, you're thanked by someone very senior who doesn't say what for.

choices.text: Take the money; it's only numbers

outcomes.text: It's a lot of money. You spend some of it. You find you can't stop thinking about who the buyer was.
Once you've sold one secret, he explains gently, you'll be selling more. He's right.

choices.text: Play along, and find out who the buyer is

outcomes.text: You follow the coin out of the mountain. The buyer wears the colours of an army nobody in Thorbardin has heard of yet.
He knows, somehow. He laughs, and the next day your workshop burns.

events.title: The Northgate Watch
events.scene: Northgate is the great fortress at the mountain's northern door, and its watch takes young dwarves from every clan and makes them stand together. The captain wants recruits who can hold a line and keep their mouths shut. Your name has come up.

choices.text: Take the watch's oath

outcomes.text: Years at the gate: drill, stone, the long dark, and a shield wall of dwarves from five clans who learn to trust each other. Mostly.
You end up in the gate's engineers, who keep the great doors and the murder holes working. You learn the gate inside out.
Your shield partner is from the clan your family hates most. By the end of the first winter you'd die for each other.

choices.text: Say your work is elsewhere

outcomes.text: The captain shrugs. There are always more dwarves for the gate.
Your clan is disappointed. Your clan is often disappointed.

culture.hill.scene: Since the war, Northgate stands open, and its watch, for the first time in three hundred years, takes a few Neidar. The captain wants recruits who can hold a line. Some of the mountain dwarves at the gate make it clear they'd rather he didn't.

events.title: The Army at Northgate
events.scene: 351. The Red Dragonarmy has come up the valley to Northgate: Highlord Verminaard's soldiers, draconians, a red dragon circling the peak. They batter at the old fortress and call for the dwarves to open. Inside, the clans argue about whether this is their war at all.

choices.text: Go to the gate and fight

outcomes.text: The gate holds. You stand in the shield wall while the stone shakes, and you learn what draconians die like.
A spear through the shield. You're carried back down the Tenth Road, and you hear the gate held while a healer works on you.

choices.text: Keep the supplies moving to the gate

outcomes.text: Weeks of carts, crates and arguing with quartermasters from five clans. The gate never runs short.
You notice a supply wagon going the wrong way, down a disused tunnel, under Theiwar escort.

culture.hill.scene: 351. The Red Dragonarmy comes up the valley past your village to Northgate: soldiers, draconians, a red dragon circling the peak. They burn the Neidar farms on their way. The mountain dwarves stay behind their gate, as they always have.

events.title: The Hammer of Kharas
events.scene: Late 351. Strangers who came with the human refugees have brought back the Hammer of Kharas, lost since the Dwarfgate War. In the Valley of the Thanes, Hornfel of the Hylar holds it up, and the clans kneel to a High King for the first time in three hundred years. Not all of them kneel willingly.

choices.text: Kneel with your whole heart

outcomes.text: For a moment, every clan in the valley is one people. You'll spend the rest of your life trying to get back to that moment.
An old Daewar beside you weeps openly. He was a boy when his father told him the hammer was lost forever.

choices.text: Watch who kneels slowly

outcomes.text: The Theiwar thane's place is empty. Word comes that Realgar is dead, fallen in his treachery, and the clan has a new thane by morning.
Several do, and you remember their faces. Unity is a fine thing for a day.

clan.theiwar.scene: Late 351. The Hammer of Kharas has come back, and Hornfel of the Hylar holds it up as High King in the Valley of the Thanes. Your own thane, Realgar, is dead: he dealt with the dragonarmies, and fell. Every eye in the valley is on the Theiwar as your clan kneels.

events.title: The Gates Stand Open
events.scene: After the war, the High King keeps Northgate open. Caravans of Neidar, humans from Abanasinia and even the odd elf come up the road to trade. Thorbardin's iron goes out into the world, and the world comes in, and not everybody likes what it brings.

choices.text: Get into the trade with the world above

outcomes.text: Iron out, grain and wool and wine in. You learn the price of everything in three currencies.
A smiling human cheats you of a season's work. You learn more from that than from any profit.

choices.text: Meet the Neidar halfway

outcomes.text: A feast at Hillhome, mountain and hill dwarves at one table for the first time since the Dwarfgate War. Somebody starts a fight, and somebody else finishes it with a song.
Three hundred years of grudges don't end at a feast. You learn which families still won't speak.

events.title: Something in the Old Tunnels
events.scene: The old secret tunnels under Thorbardin were sealed centuries ago, or so everyone thought. Now there are tracks in the dust that aren't dwarven, and a patrol that went down didn't come back. The Theiwar thane says it's nothing, quite firmly.

choices.text: Volunteer to go and look

outcomes.text: In the light of your lamp, something with wings and scales turns and runs. Nobody on the Council believes you.
No creatures. Just crates of dwarven steel, marked for nowhere, waiting by a door that should be sealed.

choices.text: Take what you've heard to your thane

outcomes.text: Your thane listens, and doubles the guard, and tells you to say nothing. It's the first time you feel the war coming.
Your thane tells you not to spread Theiwar gossip about the Theiwar. You start keeping your own watch.

events.title: The Gates That Stay Shut
events.scene: Since the Dwarfgate War, more than three centuries ago, Thorbardin's gates have been shut, and the hill dwarves who were left outside to die have never forgiven the mountain. Today a Neidar delegation stands at the old gate and shouts its grievances at the stone, as their grandparents did.

choices.text: Stand with the hill dwarves

outcomes.text: You shout until you're hoarse. The mountain doesn't answer. It never does.
A voice answers from a slit in the rock, quietly: one mountain dwarf who thinks you're right. You never learn his name.

choices.text: Listen from the inside

outcomes.text: Behind the stone you hear them, and the guards laugh. You don't laugh.
You go to the archives to find out what really happened at Dwarfgate. The answer isn't what you were taught.

events.title: Chaos Under the Mountain
events.scene: 383. The war that the rest of the world fights in the sky, Thorbardin fights in its own halls: creatures of Chaos come up through the deep roads, fire runs through the warrens, and the Life-Tree shakes. The kingdom no army ever took is devastated from inside.

choices.text: Go down into the deep roads to fight

outcomes.text: You hold a tunnel for a day and a night with eleven others. Six come back up.
The fire finds you in the dark. You live, and carry its mark.

choices.text: Get the young and old to the high halls

outcomes.text: You get your clan's children up the stairs ahead of the fire. Not all clans are so lucky.
In the smoke you lose your way and find it again by touch, alone. You never quite trust the dark again.

events.title: The Mountain Seals Itself
events.scene: 412. The green dragon Beryl tries to take Thorbardin, and the thanes answer the old way: they seal the gates and let the world go on without them. Not everyone agrees. A dwarf named Severus Stonehand leads those who won't be shut in out into the daylight.

choices.text: Stay inside the sealed mountain

outcomes.text: The gates close behind the last of Stonehand's people. Inside, life goes on, smaller.
You stay, and the sound of the gates closing stays with you.

choices.text: Go out with Stonehand

outcomes.text: Sunlight, for the first time in your life, and it hurts. You follow Stonehand east.
Your own clan calls you a traitor as you leave. You go anyway.

events.title: Thoradin Reborn
events.scene: Word comes of Severus Stonehand: he has retaken Zhakar from the mould-sick dwarves who held it, cured the plague, and named the old kingdom Thoradin again. Dwarves who left the sealed mountain are flocking to him.

choices.text: Go to Thoradin

outcomes.text: A new hall, a new clan, a new name over the door. It feels like being born again, at your age.
You arrive in time for the last of the fighting. Thoradin is built on it.

choices.text: Doubt the stories

outcomes.text: They turn out to be true. You wonder what else you've doubted that was.
The stories grow in the telling. The truth, when you hear it, is smaller and better.

events.title: The First Time for Real
events.scene: It isn't drill. There are armed men on the road, the patrol is small, and you're in it. Someone on the other side runs at you with a raised blade.

choices.text: Plant your feet and do what you trained for

outcomes.text: It ends in three moves. You throw up afterwards, and the veterans pretend not to see.
You bring the man down and take a cut that will ache every winter.
You disarm him and can't finish it. He looks at you, and runs.

choices.text: Cover the comrade who went down

outcomes.text: You hold the line over them until the rest arrive. They live.
You hold the line. For them, it was already too late.

events.title: The Order
events.scene: Your captain orders you to burn the barn of a family who hid a wanted man. It's a direct order, given in front of the troop. The family is watching.

choices.text: Obey

outcomes.text: The barn burns. You discover you can do what you're told, and don't know if that's good.
You stall on purpose, long enough for them to get the animals out. Nobody can prove a thing.

choices.text: Refuse, out loud

outcomes.text: They take your post and your weapon. On your way out, two veterans shake your hand without a word.
Another lowers their torch, then another. The captain swallows the order, and doesn't forget your name.
You take the prescribed punishment standing. The barn burns anyway.

events.title: The Proof Piece
events.scene: To stop being an apprentice you must present a piece to the town's masters. There are three of them; they dislike each other, and newcomers even more.

choices.text: Make the classic piece, without a single flaw

outcomes.text: They look, weigh, rap it with a knuckle, and approve with a grunt.
One of them finds a flaw the other two can't see. Another year as apprentice.

choices.text: Make something no one in town has made before

outcomes.text: The silence lasts too long. Then the eldest asks to see how you did it.
They refuse it: that's not how it's done. A buyer from out of town takes the piece for three times the price.
The piece fails during the test, in front of everyone. The idea was good; the execution, not yet.

events.title: What Mustn't Be Mixed
events.scene: Alone in the workshop at night, you notice that two things your master never allows together are side by side on the bench. You've always wanted to know why.

choices.text: Mix a little of each, carefully

outcomes.text: The reaction is small, beautiful and useful. You write it all down and tell no one.
The bench catches fire. You put it out, and spend a month working off the damage.
The fumes knock you out. You wake with your master beside you, furious and interested.

choices.text: Wait until morning and ask

outcomes.text: Your master shows you, from a safe distance. You understand the reason for half the house rules.
Your master says you're not ready yet, and starts locking the workshop.

events.title: Winter in the Wild
events.scene: The snow closed the pass earlier than expected. You're alone in a hunting hut, with food for three weeks and winter for two months.

choices.text: Hunt every day, whatever the weather

outcomes.text: You come out of winter stronger than you went in, with pelts to sell.
A blizzard catches you far from the hut. You lose two toes and nothing more.
A thin wolf starts following you, and you start leaving scraps. At the thaw it's still around.

choices.text: Ration, save your strength and wait

outcomes.text: You count the days in scratches on the wall and learn how long you can bear your own company.
At the worst of the hunger, someone knocks: another lost soul, of a people not your own. You share what's left.

events.title: Those Who Pay to Be Led
events.scene: A well-dressed group hires you to cross a bad stretch. They pay too much, lie about where they're going, and on the second night you realise they're being followed.

choices.text: Keep the contract and shake off the pursuers

outcomes.text: You lead them where nobody goes. At the end they pay double and ask you to forget their faces.
The pursuers catch up. In the confusion you pick a side without knowing which is right.

choices.text: Demand the truth before taking another step

outcomes.text: They tell you. The truth is bigger than you wanted, and now you're part of it.
They dismiss you on the spot, in the middle of nowhere, with half pay. You walk back alone, thinking.

events.title: Someone Talked
events.scene: The job went wrong because the watch was waiting. Someone in the crew talked. The boss wants a name by dawn, and you know who it was: the person who helped you most when you arrived.

choices.text: Keep quiet and help them vanish

outcomes.text: They're gone before sunrise, leaving a note with an address for the day you need it.
They get away, and suspicion falls on you. You start sleeping with your boots on.

choices.text: Give the name

outcomes.text: The boss nods, and you go up a rung. Nobody in the crew tells you anything any more.
Before they're taken, they say why they talked. The reason was better than the boss's.

choices.text: Use the confusion to leave this life

outcomes.text: You vanish in the night with what you're wearing and start again somewhere else.
Nobody leaves owing nothing. You leave, carrying a debt to people who don't forget.

events.title: The Door Nobody Opens
events.scene: There's a house in town with a famous lock: they say dwarves made it and nobody has ever opened it without the key. Someone bets a fortune you can't.

choices.text: Take the bet

outcomes.text: It takes all night. When the last pin gives, you understand why some people make this their life.
You get further than anyone. You lose the bet and gain a reputation.
The lock had a second secret. The needle leaves your hand numb for months.

choices.text: Refuse the bet and look for whoever made the lock

outcomes.text: The locksmith, an old dwarf, laughs a lot, and ends up teaching you how to think of a lock from the inside.
The locksmith shuts the door in your face. Through the gap you see enough to get ideas.

events.title: The Night Without an Answer
events.scene: They've brought in a wounded child, and the one with the gift of healing is two days away. There's only you. You kneel, ask, and for a time that never ends, nothing happens.

choices.text: Keep praying until the night is over

outcomes.text: Near dawn, your hands grow warm. The child opens their eyes. You never again doubt what you felt.
Nothing comes down from the sky. The child lives, and you never knew whether it was you, the god, or the child's stubbornness.
The child dies before dawn. In the morning you sweep the temple as every day, and that is faith too.

choices.text: Get up and do what ordinary hands can do

outcomes.text: Boiled water, clean cloth, pressure in the right place. The child lives.
You do everything right and it isn't enough. The parents thank you anyway.

events.title: The Other Door
events.scene: A pilgrim of another faith spends the night at the temple. They speak of a god different from yours with a quiet certainty you envy, and before leaving say their door is open too.

choices.text: Spend the night talking

outcomes.text: You argue until sunrise and come away knowing better why you believe what you believe.
Something in what they say fits where nothing fitted before. You change altars.
Their god doesn't live in a temple: it lives in the woods, the rain, the animals. You start praying with your eyes open.

choices.text: Thank them and don't engage

outcomes.text: Your superiors approve. You're left wondering how the conversation would have gone.
You tell your superiors. The pilgrim is put on the road at night, and you didn't like seeing it.

events.title: The Marked Page
events.scene: There's a spell you shouldn't know yet, and it would solve, right now, a serious problem for someone you care about. You have the words. You're not sure you have the strength.

choices.text: Cast it

outcomes.text: It works. You sleep for two days and wake knowing you can do more than they said.
It works, and it charges a price: a white streak in your hair, a tremor in your hand, a dream that keeps coming back.
The magic slips your control and does something else. The problem changes shape, and now it's yours.

choices.text: Close the book and find another way

outcomes.text: The other way is slow and dull, and it works. Your teacher, if you have one, never knew of the temptation.
The other way doesn't arrive in time. You carry the choice, and still think it was right.

events.title: The Three Colours
events.scene: Everyone who meddles with magic in Ansalon hears the same thing one day: present yourself at the Tower and choose a robe colour, or become a renegade, and renegades are hunted. Today someone came to remind you in person.

choices.text: Promise to present yourself when you're ready

outcomes.text: They give you a deadline and a list of what to study. It's the first time anyone has treated your magic as something serious.
Along with the deadline, they leave a travelling tutor who stays a season and teaches with a patience you didn't expect.

choices.text: Say your magic is no tower's business

outcomes.text: The visitor sighs, writes down your name and leaves. You start choosing carefully whom you do things in front of.
The visitor studies you a while and says, puzzled, that what you have isn't what the Tower teaches. They leave without an answer.

events.title: The Paper That Doesn't Add Up
events.scene: Copying old records, you find a mistake that isn't a mistake: long ago, someone altered a land deed, and an important family now owns what was never theirs.

choices.text: Pull the thread in secret

outcomes.text: Three archives and two months later, you have the whole proof stored somewhere safe.
Someone notices which books you keep requesting. One day they simply aren't on the shelf any more.

choices.text: Take it to your master

outcomes.text: They already knew. They explain why they never said anything, and you learn the difference between knowing and being able to say.
They burn the page in front of you and tell you to forget it. You had made a copy.

events.title: The Language Nobody Speaks
events.scene: A text from before the Cataclysm lands on your desk, in a language even your master barely reads. Deciphering it would take months of nights. Nobody asked you to.

choices.text: Decipher it, whatever it costs

outcomes.text: The first whole sentence you read makes your neck prickle. The text speaks of things that should have been forgotten.
You decipher half. The other half becomes the project of your life.
You manage it, and pay with your eyes: after that winter, you need lenses to read.

choices.text: Tip off a buyer of rarities

outcomes.text: The buyer pays well and asks you to let them know whenever something like this turns up.
The text vanishes from your desk before the buyer arrives. Someone else knew what it was worth.

events.title: The Cargo
events.scene: The cargo you were answerable for is lost: a fallen bridge, a storm, it doesn't matter. The owner will want its full value, and you have three days before you arrive with the news.

choices.text: Arrive and tell the truth

outcomes.text: The owner swears for an hour and then hires you again, because people who give bad news straight are rare.
You sign a debt that will take years to pay.

choices.text: Use the three days to replace the cargo, however you can

outcomes.text: Three trades, a loan and a bluff later, you deliver the full cargo. The owner never knew.
You replace the cargo with a moneylender's money. The owner is satisfied; the moneylender, interested in you.
The only cargo you can get in time can't be shown to any customs officer. It arrives all the same.

events.title: The Port on the Far Side
events.scene: The voyage takes you further than anyone from your village has ever been: a port where nobody speaks your language, the coins bear other faces, and there are people of races you thought were history.

choices.text: Head into the city alone

outcomes.text: You get back to the ship at dawn with your head full and twenty new words.
Your purse is gone within ten minutes. A minotaur dockhand finds it funny and buys your supper.
You get into a tavern brawl that wasn't yours and come out with one tooth fewer and one friend more.

choices.text: Stay with your master and learn how deals are done there

outcomes.text: You watch your master lose one negotiation on purpose to win the next. It takes you a while to understand, and you never forget.
A local merchant offers you double to stay. Your master pretends not to hear.

events.title: The Song You Don't Sing
events.scene: Tonight's audience includes the most powerful man in town. The troupe has a song about him, funny and true, that it only sings in faraway villages. Someone drunk shouts for it from the back.

choices.text: Sing it

outcomes.text: He laughs louder than anyone and sends wine to the stage. Only the truly powerful can take a joke.
The troupe is thrown out of town that night. On the road, nobody complains to you.
You spend three days in a cell, and come out with material for ten songs.

choices.text: Improvise another song, flattering and full of double meanings

outcomes.text: Half the audience gets it. He doesn't. Best night of the season.
He understands perfectly, and smiles in a way that promises a conversation later.

events.title: The Act Without a Net
events.scene: The troupe has no money to get through the winter. There's an act that would fill any square: dangerous, old, and only someone your age and weight can do it.

choices.text: Do the act

outcomes.text: The square holds its breath and then explodes. The troupe eats well all winter.
You fall on the last move. The crowd pays anyway; your ankle is never the same.
It goes wrong halfway through and you turn the mistake into comedy. A new act is born.

choices.text: Propose another way to get through winter

outcomes.text: You suggest telling, in instalments, the story of the war as the local people lived it. They come back every night.
The troupe's plan turns out less artistic: a shell game and a quick exit from town.

events.title: Two Lives
events.scene: The birth went wrong in the small hours and your teacher won't arrive in time. The old midwife looks at you and says what you already knew: it may not be possible to save both, and someone has to decide what to try first.

choices.text: Try the risky procedure that might save both

outcomes.text: The baby's cry fills the house, and the mother is alive to hear it. You only shake afterwards.
You save one. The family thanks you, and you carry the other.
It's no use. The midwife puts a hand on your shoulder and says she'd have tried too.

choices.text: Play it safe and save the mother

outcomes.text: The mother lives. You never knew whether the other way would have worked.
The mother lives and, against the odds, so does the baby. Some nights luck works too.

events.title: The Patient Nobody Wants
events.scene: Someone has left at your door, by night, a wounded man the whole village would rather see dead: a known highwayman, or worse. He'll be dead by morning if nobody does anything.

choices.text: Treat him like anyone else

outcomes.text: He lives, and before vanishing says that from today nobody on the road will lay a hand on you.
He lives and the village finds out. For a while, people would rather be ill than knock on your door.
He dies anyway, after telling you where he buried what he stole.

choices.text: Stop the bleeding and call the watch

outcomes.text: He's hanged a month later, with his leg beautifully healed.
His gang finds out who handed him over.

events.title: The Message Never Written
events.scene: You're sent to carry a message by heart to another house. On the way, a pleasant man offers an absurd sum just to hear it. Nobody would ever know.

choices.text: Refuse and deliver the message intact

outcomes.text: It was a test, or it wasn't. Either way, they start trusting you with bigger things.
The pleasant man doesn't take no for an answer. You arrive with the message and a cut on your forehead.

choices.text: Sell it

outcomes.text: You have more money than you've ever had, and the knowledge that you have a price.
The house finds out within a week. There's no public punishment: you simply cease to exist for them.

choices.text: Sell a false message and deliver the real one

outcomes.text: You tell your house everything, hand over the money, and earn a seat at the table where such things are planned.
The buyer sees through the lie. Now someone powerful knows your face and your talent.

events.title: On Your Knees
events.scene: The old man you serve, an exiled Solamnic, wants you to swear his order's oath: honour above life. Half the town thinks knights are fools; the other half remembers who held the wall in the war.

choices.text: Swear

outcomes.text: The words weigh more spoken than read. You rise different.
That same week the oath costs you dear: you must defend in public someone you despise.

choices.text: Say you serve him, not an order

outcomes.text: He's silent a while, then says that loyalty to a person is an oath too, older than the order.
He lets you go, without anger. In parting, he hands you his own dagger.

events.title: Someone Better Than You
events.scene: {peer.name} started after you and is already better, with no visible effort. Everyone noticed. You noticed first.

choices.text: Work twice as hard to catch up

outcomes.text: It takes a year. The day you draw level, it's your peer who comes to ask how you did it.
You improve a great deal, and they're still better. You find out what you're the best at.

choices.text: Swallow your pride and ask them to teach you

outcomes.text: They teach you gladly. You become a pair the others avoid facing.
They laugh. You decide to learn alone, watching from a distance, and you do.

choices.text: Make sure they slip up in front of everyone

outcomes.text: It works. They never knew. You knew every day.
You're found out. They say nothing, and that's worse.

events.title: The Mistake
events.scene: You've made a serious mistake, the kind that costs money or hurts someone. For now nobody knows it was you, and there's an easy way for the blame to land on someone else.

choices.text: Own up

outcomes.text: You pay what you owe, and gain something money can't buy: people believe you when you speak.
It costs dear: months of unpaid work, and a look that takes long to change.

choices.text: Let the blame fall where it falls

outcomes.text: Someone else pays for you, and leaves. Their place at the table stays empty a long time.
They find out months later, and the silence weighs more than the mistake.

choices.text: Fix it in secret before anyone notices

outcomes.text: Three sleepless nights, and nobody ever knew there had been a mistake.
The fix makes things worse. Now there are two mistakes, and you own up to both.

events.title: The Red
events.scene: Someone crosses the line, on purpose, over the thing that hurts you most. The world goes narrow and red, and your body has decided before you have.

choices.text: Let it come

outcomes.text: When the red passes, it takes three people to hold you, and the other one can't get up alone. You didn't know you had that in you.
The one who gets hurt is someone who tried to pull you apart. The anger passes at once; the rest takes longer.
The anger comes, and for the first time you ride it instead of being carried.

choices.text: Hold it with everything you've got

outcomes.text: You shake all over and don't move. Those who saw were more frightened than if you'd struck.
You walk away and look for someone who can teach you to make your body obey.

events.title: Further Than the Map
events.scene: Work takes you, for the first time, out of Abanasinia. On the way, something happens that wasn't in anyone's plans.

choices.text: Take the southern road, through the mountains

outcomes.text: A blizzard forces you to ask the dwarves for shelter. They charge in labour, and you leave knowing how to drink and swear in their tongue.
You see Pax Tharkas up close: the walls, and what's left of the mines where people from your land were slaves.
A landslide closes the road with you on the wrong side. Ten days alone to find a way round.

choices.text: Take the western road, along the edge of the elves' forest

outcomes.text: An elf patrol shadows you for two days without a word. On the third, one of them leaves food on your path.
You're turned back at the border with icy courtesy. You learn what it's like to be the foreigner.
At night, from beyond the trees, comes music you never get out of your head.

choices.text: Go by boat across the New Sea

outcomes.text: The boat calls at Schallsea, where a plains people live whom the other tribes drove out generations ago. They remember.
Ten days becalmed. The water runs out before the wind returns, and you learn what people become when they thirst.
On a day of clear water, someone points down: rooftops. The sea covered whole cities in the Cataclysm, and you saw one.

events.title: Your Mentor's Favour
events.scene: The person who teaches you, to whom you owe almost everything, asks a favour that isn't right: to lie for them before someone who could punish them. If they're found out, they lose everything. So do you.

choices.text: Lie for them

outcomes.text: The lie holds. They never raise their voice at you again, and never look you in the eye the same way.
You're found out. You both fall, and in the fall your mentor takes all the blame to spare you.

choices.text: Refuse

outcomes.text: They're furious for a week. Then they say it was the best thing they ever taught you.
They throw you out. What you learned goes with you; the rest, you finish learning alone.

choices.text: Persuade them to tell the truth, and stand by them

outcomes.text: The truth, told before it's torn out, earns mercy. They lose a great deal, but not everything.
They tell the truth and fall. You're left with an empty workshop and their gratitude, which is worth more than it seems.

events.title: The Proposal
events.scene: There's an offer of marriage on the table. It's a good offer, from a good person, and it would settle your family's life. Accepting means staying, for ever, more or less where you are.

choices.text: Accept

outcomes.text: Contrary to what you feared, it works. You have someone to come back to, and that changes how you leave.
It's a proper, lukewarm marriage. The road keeps calling, and you keep not going.
It's good, and it's short: an illness takes them in the second winter. Nothing holds you there any more.

choices.text: Refuse

outcomes.text: The family swallows it. The other person wishes you luck with a dignity you admire.
The refusal is taken as an insult by both families. Staying close becomes hard.

choices.text: Say your heart already belongs to someone else

outcomes.text: Once said aloud, the truth clears the way. You end up together, with less money and more will.
The one you meant had already moved on. You turned down a life for a love that didn't wait.

events.title: What They Left
events.scene: The person who taught you most has died, or left for good. They left three things: a worn tool, unfinished business, and a sentence you only now understand.

choices.text: Take on the unfinished business

outcomes.text: The business is bigger than it looked and leads beyond the region. Suddenly, you have a reason.
The business had a name and a face: someone who wronged your mentor and never paid.

choices.text: Keep the tool and carry on their work

outcomes.text: You pick up where they left off. Their customers become yours.
In the tool's handle there's a compartment, and in it something that explains why they never spoke of their past.

choices.text: Follow the sentence wherever it leads

outcomes.text: The sentence gives no destination, only a direction. That's more than most people have.
You discover they said the same sentence to someone else, years ago. That person is alive, and knows the rest.

events.title: The Deep Seam
events.scene: The mine is hiring: hard pay for hard hands, and no questions about your age. The foreman looks at your shoulders and says the deep seam needs someone who doesn't mind the dark.

choices.text: Take the lamp and go down

outcomes.text: You learn to read the rock by the sound it makes under the pick. The others start following your lamp.
A gallery comes down behind you. {miner.name} digs you out with bleeding hands, and you owe them everything after that.
You find a pocket of silver nobody else saw. You keep a little of it. Nobody knows.

choices.text: Say the dark isn't for you

outcomes.text: You haul ore at the pithead instead. It's honest work, and it builds your back.
You find other work in town, and you never stop wondering what's down there.

events.title: The Missing Purse
events.scene: A merchant's purse has gone from a locked room, and the merchant has already decided the new servant took it. You were in the house that day. Something about the story doesn't fit.

choices.text: Look into it yourself

outcomes.text: Mud on the wrong boots, a window latch scratched from outside. You hand the merchant the real thief, and the servant keeps their place.
You follow the clues to the wrong person, and have to apologise in front of everyone. You learn more from that than from being right.
You find the thief: the merchant's own kin, {thief.name}. {thief.name} gets away with it, and knows who nearly caught {thief.them}.

choices.text: Keep out of it

outcomes.text: The servant is turned out on the road. You think of them on cold nights.
You watch everyone's faces while the merchant shouts, and see the one who's lying. You say nothing, but you remember.

events.title: The Sealed Letter
events.scene: A factor needs a letter carried across the country, sealed, by someone nobody will think to stop. The pay is good. The factor won't say who's waiting for it, or who might want it.

choices.text: Carry it, and don't ask

outcomes.text: Nine days on the road, two nights sleeping in ditches, and the letter is in the right hands. The factor has more work for you.
Riders come after you on the third day. You lose them in a marsh, and the letter arrives damp but sealed.
The seal cracks in the rain. You read it before you can stop yourself, and now you know something you shouldn't.

choices.text: Turn it down

outcomes.text: Someone else carries it. You hear later that they never arrived.
The pay would have fed your family for a season. You take a worse job, and think about it.

events.title: The Card-Reader's Tent
events.scene: A travelling card-reader has pitched a tent at the edge of the fair. She turns over three cards for you, stops, and says she's never seen that spread on someone so young. Then she offers to teach you.

choices.text: Learn the cards

outcomes.text: {reader.name} says you have the gift. Maybe you do. Maybe you just watch faces well. Either way, people pay.
There's no magic in it, she admits: only reading people and telling them what they need. You turn out to be very good at it.
One night the cards say something about the moons that nobody could have known. It comes true. You put the deck away for a month.

choices.text: Laugh and walk away

outcomes.text: You laugh. The three cards stay with you anyway.
You decide your life is yours to read. It's a good decision, mostly.

events.title: The Wandering Master
events.scene: An old traveller with empty hands knocks down three drunks in the square without seeming to move. Afterwards, sharing your water, they say the body is a weapon most people never learn to hold.

choices.text: Ask to be taught

outcomes.text: {master.name} teaches you for two years: breath, balance, the falling and the getting up. Then one morning they are gone.
The training breaks you before it builds you. You keep at it long after the master has moved on.
They watch you for a week and tell you to go home: you fight angry. You spend years proving them wrong.

choices.text: Thank them and let them go

outcomes.text: You copy what you saw, alone, at dawn. You get some of it right.
It stays a story you tell: the day you saw someone fight like water.

events.title: The Riders' Relay
events.scene: The relay station on the high road is short a rider. The horse is fast and mean, the route is long, and the last rider broke a leg. They ask if you can stay on.

choices.text: Take the horse

outcomes.text: You ride the route all season, in rain and dust. You learn every ford and every inn, and the horse learns you.
The horse throws you twice in the first week. The third week, you don't fall.
You carry the news of a raid ahead of the raiders, and a village empties in time. They remember your name there.

choices.text: Look after the horses instead

outcomes.text: You keep the stable for a season. The horses like you better than the riders do.
You move on. The road keeps calling, but you'll go on foot.

events.title: Picking the Ruins
events.scene: The old burned quarter has been left to the rats and the children. There's still copper in the walls, glass that didn't melt, and once in a while something nobody has seen since before the war.

choices.text: Go picking with the others

outcomes.text: You learn which walls will hold and which will drop on you, and you sell copper by the pound.
Under a fallen beam you find a carved box, older than the city. You don't sell it.
You find a sword under the ash, still sharp, with a crest you don't know. Someone, someday, will want it back.

choices.text: Stay out of the ruins

outcomes.text: Two of the others are hurt that season. You were at home.
You draw a map of the ruins from the rooftops instead, and sell it to the pickers.

events.title: The Bridge at Night
events.scene: The occupiers' supply wagons cross the old bridge every third night. Someone in the resistance says the bridge has a weak pin, and someone who knows wood and iron could make it fail at the right moment.

choices.text: Do it yourself

outcomes.text: The pin goes, the bridge sags, and a month of supplies goes into the river. Nobody was on it. You make sure of that.
A patrol comes early. You get away, but they have your description now.
It works, and the occupiers hang three villagers for it. You carry that.

choices.text: Refuse; the reprisals would fall on others

outcomes.text: Someone else does it, badly. You were right about the reprisals.
You help in a quieter way: food and warnings, passed through back doors.

events.title: The Guild Hall
events.scene: The guild has noticed your work. There's a fee, an oath, and a seat at the long table in the hall, and after that a mark you can put on everything you make. Some say the guild protects its own; others, that it owns them.

choices.text: Pay the fee and swear the oath

outcomes.text: You put your mark on your work for the first time, and it sells for twice what it did.
The guild is more politics than craft. You learn to sit through meetings and make the right friends.
The fee is more than you have. You borrow it, and the guild master holds your note.

choices.text: Stay free of them

outcomes.text: You sell outside the walls, for less, to people who don't ask about marks.
The guild doesn't like competition. Your stall is smashed one night, and you learn who your friends are.

events.title: The Town Watch
events.scene: The watch captain is short of hands after a bad winter. A cudgel, a lantern, a coat that fits nobody, and the night streets: that's the offer.

choices.text: Take the coat

outcomes.text: You walk the same streets every night until you know every face and every lie told on them.
Your partner on the night watch, {watchmate.name}, saves your neck in an alley fight. You'd do the same for them.
The watch takes bribes, and so, after a while, do you.

choices.text: The night is someone else's job

outcomes.text: You sleep at night. Mostly.
The captain remembers you said no, and keeps an eye on you after that.

events.title: The Rope Across the Square
events.scene: A troupe of players strings a rope between two rooftops over the market square. When their rope-walker twists an ankle, the troupe leader looks down at the crowd for anyone light enough and foolish enough.

choices.text: Climb up

outcomes.text: You make it across, and back, and the square roars. The troupe takes you on for the summer.
You fall, and land in the awning of a cloth stall, and get up laughing. The crowd likes that even better.
You fall badly. The arm heals crooked, and you never quite trust heights again.

choices.text: Stay in the crowd

outcomes.text: Another child goes up. You study how they hold their arms, and practise on the garden wall.
While everyone looks up, you notice the troupe's cutpurse working the crowd, and how they do it.

events.title: The Herb Garden
events.scene: The old healer's garden has gone wild since her eyes failed. She can still tell every leaf by smell, and she needs young hands to pick, dry and grind.

choices.text: Work the garden with her

outcomes.text: {healer.name} teaches you which root stops bleeding and which one stops a heart. You keep both lists.
Fever comes to the village that autumn, and your dried leaves save more than one child.
Someone comes asking for the second list. You don't give it. They don't forget.

choices.text: You have better things to do

outcomes.text: The garden goes to weeds. When you're sick that winter, there's no one to grind the willow bark.
You never learn the names, but you never forget the smells.

events.title: Old Scores
events.scene: {rival.name} has grown up, and so have you. This time it isn't a children's scrap: your rival has spread something about you that could cost your family dearly, and everyone is waiting to see what you'll do.

choices.text: Challenge them in public, with rules and witnesses

outcomes.text: You win cleanly. At the end they hold out a hand, and you decide whether to take it.
You lose in front of everyone, and get up more times than anyone expected.
Someone with weight separates you and gives you both the same punishment. Sweating side by side, the anger stops making sense.

choices.text: Gather proof that it's a lie and show it to the people who matter

outcomes.text: The lie collapses under one well-chosen witness.
Half believe you, half believe them. That's how it stays.

choices.text: Don't answer; the people who know you know the truth

outcomes.text: With no answer, the rumour starves.
The rumour grows. Your family loses a deal because of it.

events.title: News From Far Away
events.scene: A traveller brings word from {sibling.name}: alive, caught up in something big, and needing someone from the family to carry an object to a place you only know by name.

choices.text: Go yourself, without telling your parents

outcomes.text: You make the journey, hand it over, and for one night you see the life your sibling leads.
Someone else wanted the object. You barely escape with it, and understand that your sibling has enemies.
You arrive too late. Whoever greets you only says your sibling had to leave in a hurry.

choices.text: Show the message to your parents

outcomes.text: A parent goes in your place and comes back silent, with a letter just for you.
They burn the message. You had already memorised the name of the place.

events.title: The Man Who Asked Too Much
events.scene: A well-dressed stranger is asking around for objects from before the Cataclysm, and describes, in too much detail, exactly what you have hidden. He pays well. He doesn't look like someone who takes no for an answer.

choices.text: Sell

outcomes.text: He pays more than your family earns in a year and doesn't haggle. That says something about its real worth.
The coins are good, and the haste with which he leaves tells you that you sold cheap.

choices.text: Say you've never seen anything like it

outcomes.text: He leaves. You move the hiding place once more.
That night someone turns your room over. They don't find it. Now you know that someone knows.
That night someone turns your room over, and finds it.

choices.text: Ask what the object is, before anything else

outcomes.text: He explains more than he should. You keep the object, and the name of whoever is looking for it.
Your question makes him look at you differently. He says he'll be back in a few years, and that you should study until then.

events.title: The Robe on the Road
events.scene: A wizard in robes passes through. Nobody speaks to him more than they must. Out of all the people there, he stops in front of you and says he knows what you are.

choices.text: Hear what he has to say

outcomes.text: He stays three days. He teaches you the first real thing and leaves a thin book, with advice to show it to no one.
He tells you where the Tower stands, and that one day you'll have to present yourself there, willingly or not.
He warns you that some people hunt folk like you, and is gone before saying who.

choices.text: Tell him he's mistaken

outcomes.text: He smiles like someone who's heard that before, and leaves a marked coin for the day you change your mind.
He snaps his fingers and your hand lights up by itself, in front of everyone.

choices.text: Bring him to speak with your family

outcomes.text: The talk lasts all night. In the morning your parents look at you with fear and pride mixed.
A parent throws him out. That night, the other one secretly hands you what he left.

events.title: The Market Road
events.scene: For the first time you've been trusted with the goods and the money. On the emptiest stretch of road, three men step out of the brush. One of them can't be much older than you.

choices.text: Hand everything over without a fight

outcomes.text: They take it all and leave you whole. The walk home is the longest of your life.
They take it all. But you recognised one of their voices.

choices.text: Drop the goods and run with the money

outcomes.text: You run like never before. You get home with the money and without the goods.
They catch you. They take the money and leave a lesson on your face.

choices.text: Fight

outcomes.text: You wound the first one and the others hesitate. It's enough. The story reaches the village before you do.
You're badly beaten and lose everything, and nobody at home can stay angry after seeing you.
The youngest of them puts his knife between you and the others and tells you to run. You never knew why.

events.title: The Name You Keep Repeating
events.scene: You're grown, and you think about {love.name} all the time. There's a problem, of course: your families have old, stubborn reasons not to like each other.

choices.text: Say what you feel

outcomes.text: It's mutual. You spend a whole season thinking nobody has noticed.
The answer is kind, and it's no. It hurts in a new way.
Someone overhears. The scandal is bigger than it deserves, and the families get worse.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself

outcomes.text: It passes, slowly. It leaves a song you can't hear without remembering.
You watch {love.name} choose someone else, and you smile at the wedding.

choices.text: Do something remarkable to impress

outcomes.text: It works better than it should. The whole village talks about it.
It goes spectacularly wrong. {love.name} laughs, and to your surprise, stays to help clean up.

events.title: Drill Day
events.scene: After what this land has been through, nobody thinks it's excessive to teach the young to hold a spear. The instructor is a veteran of few words, and today he picked you for the demonstration.

choices.text: Give it everything

outcomes.text: The veteran raises an eyebrow. After drill, he asks you to stay behind.
You leave aching, able to do something you couldn't do that morning.
You hurt a fellow recruit by accident. They recover; you start measuring your own strength.

choices.text: Watch the others first and use your head

outcomes.text: You bring down someone bigger with a trick of footing. The veteran laughs for the first time that day.
While you're thinking, they put you on the ground. It was a good idea.

choices.text: Make an excuse and skip drill

outcomes.text: You spend the day doing what you like. The others come back with stories you don't have.
The veteran finds you, and your punishment is carrying everyone's weapons for a month. You learn the weight of each one.

culture.plains.scene: The tribe's warriors train the young with bow and spear, and since the war nobody thinks that excessive. Today the quietest of them picked you for the demonstration.

events.title: The Crossing
events.scene: It was meant to be a short crossing of the New Sea, for work. The sky closes in fast, the skipper stops joking, and someone puts a rope in your hand.

choices.text: Do exactly what you're told, as fast as you can

outcomes.text: The boat holds. In port, the skipper says there's a place for you on the next trip.
The boat doesn't hold. You wash up clinging to a plank on a coast you don't know, and it takes weeks to get home.
A wave takes you. A hand grabs your collar and hauls you back.

choices.text: Curl up in the hold and wait for it to pass

outcomes.text: It passes. Nobody mentions it, and nobody invites you on another trip.
In the hold you see what the boat is really carrying under the grain sacks.

events.title: A Seat at the Table
events.scene: Important people are passing through, and they need a presentable youngster to serve at table and carry messages. They picked you. In the kitchen they warn you: don't speak unless spoken to.

choices.text: Serve in silence and listen to everything

outcomes.text: You learn that decisions that change whole villages are made between one course and the next.
Someone at the table notices your manner and asks your name. Says they'll remember it.
You hear what you weren't meant to hear. Someone notices that you heard.

choices.text: Answer frankly when the talk turns to your people

outcomes.text: The table goes quiet, then laughs heartily. They ask you to stay for dessert.
The table goes quiet, and stays quiet. They send you back to the kitchen.

culture.plains.scene: Chiefs from other villages have come to council, and they need a youngster to serve and carry messages between the tents. They picked you. They warn you: don't speak unless spoken to.

events.title: It Wasn't Me
events.scene: Something valuable has gone missing, and fingers point at you. You didn't do it. You know who did, and it's someone you'd rather not give up.

choices.text: Say who did it

outcomes.text: They believe you. You're free, and you lose someone.
They think you're shifting the blame. Now they suspect you both.

choices.text: Take the blame in silence

outcomes.text: You pay for what you didn't do. The one who did it knows, and doesn't forget.
At the last moment the real culprit steps forward. They couldn't watch you pay.

choices.text: Ask for three days to find the missing thing

outcomes.text: You return it without saying where it was. Everyone understands, and nobody asks.
The three days pass. The doubt sticks to you.

events.title: The Big Job
events.scene: The gang is tired of fairground purses. There's a warehouse, a watchman who sleeps, and a buyer waiting. They want you at the window, because you're the smallest one who still fits.

choices.text: Go in through the window

outcomes.text: It all goes to plan. Your share is more money than you've ever seen in one place.
The watchman wakes. Everyone runs; he saw your face.
It goes wrong, and the gang leaves you behind. You get out alone, by a way nobody thought of.

choices.text: Say this is too much for you

outcomes.text: They curse you, and let you go. The door stays shut from then on.
They don't let you go that easily. You spend months looking over your shoulder.

choices.text: Warn the warehouse owner

outcomes.text: The owner sets a trap, catches two, and offers you honest work.
The gang finds out who talked. You need another street, maybe another village.

events.title: The Impossible Order
events.scene: {mentor.name} has fallen ill at the worst moment: there's a big order due in five days, for a client who never forgives a late delivery. The whole workshop looks at you.

choices.text: Do it yourself, the way you were taught

outcomes.text: The client examines it, looks for a flaw, and finds none. Asks who made it.
It isn't a master's work. It's work delivered on time, and the workshop survives.
The client rejects it. From the sickbed, your mentor says you did what they'd have done at your age.

choices.text: Go to the client and negotiate more time

outcomes.text: You come back with ten more days and a client impressed by your nerve.
The client takes the order to a rival. The workshop tightens its belt.

choices.text: Swallow your pride and ask your mentor's rival for help

outcomes.text: The rival helps, charges dearly, and at the end suggests you change workshops.
The rival laughs in your face. You go back and work three nights without sleep.

events.title: What's Killing the Herd
events.scene: Something is killing the animals at night, and it isn't wolves: the marks are too big. The adults are organising a hunt. You're too young to go, and you read tracks better than half of them.

choices.text: Follow the hunt in secret

outcomes.text: You're the one who finds the den. The adults can't decide between scolding and respect.
You lose the group and come face to face with the beast. It looks at you for a time that doesn't end, and leaves.
The beast finds you first. The hunters arrive in time; the claw marks stay.

choices.text: Set your own trap near the pen

outcomes.text: In the morning the beast is in your trap. You decide, alone, what to do with it.
The trap catches something else: a man who'd been letting the beast loose on purpose.
Nothing is caught. The beast disappears with the change of season, and the doubt stays.

events.title: Where Nobody Goes
events.scene: There are old stones in a place the elders say to avoid: walls from before the Cataclysm, half swallowed by the earth. Your friends have dared you to spend the night there.

choices.text: Accept and, since you're there anyway, go inside

outcomes.text: There are inscriptions you copy by candlelight without understanding them. Understanding becomes a project.
Under a loose slab there's something small and heavy that doesn't belong to this century.
You aren't the only one there. Whoever lives in the ruins doesn't want to be found, and lets you go in exchange for silence.

choices.text: Sleep outside and say you went in

outcomes.text: They believe you. You know the truth, and it bothers you more than it should.
In the middle of the night something comes out of the ruins and passes ten paces from you, unseeing.

choices.text: Refuse the dare

outcomes.text: They laugh at you for a week. The next week they're laughing at someone else.
Someone else goes in your place and comes back changed, and won't say why. You spend years wanting to know.

events.title: The Empty Chair
events.scene: {relative.name}, who held the household together, has died. After the funeral the remaining adults do sums in low voices, and you realise you're part of the sums.

choices.text: Take on the work they did

outcomes.text: You age years in one season. The house stays standing.
It's too heavy for your age, and you carry it anyway, worse than they did.

choices.text: Accept being sent to live with distant kin

outcomes.text: The new house is strange and good. You learn there's more than one way to live.
In the new house you're more a pair of hands than a nephew or niece.

choices.text: Promise, at the grave, to finish what they left undone

outcomes.text: Nobody heard the promise but you. That's exactly why it weighs so much.
Someone did hear: an old friend of the dead, who promises to help you keep it.

events.title: The Offer
events.scene: Someone from outside has seen something in you worth investing in: a place, board and schooling in a bigger city, for a few years. It's the chance nobody in your family ever had. It means leaving now.

choices.text: Accept and go

outcomes.text: It's everything promised, and harder than you imagined. You come home for festivals, a little more different each time.
The schooling is real, and so is the bill: your patron expects things in return that weren't in the agreement.
There was no school at all. It takes months to get home, and you come back knowing how to manage anywhere.

choices.text: Refuse; your place is here

outcomes.text: You stay, and you're at peace with it most days.
You stay. The question of what might have been never leaves.

choices.text: Insist they take someone else along, or no deal

outcomes.text: They agree. You leave together, and you carry the responsibility for both.
They withdraw the offer. The person you asked for never knew.

events.title: What Was Left in the Hills
events.scene: They say the war is over, but not every soldier of the defeated army went home. Far from the houses, you stumble on a camp, and the thing crouching by the fire has scales and wings. It hasn't seen you yet.

choices.text: Back away silently and run to warn people

outcomes.text: The militia finds the camp empty and still warm. From then on, people listen when you speak.
Nobody believes you. A week later two sheep go missing, and nobody apologises.

choices.text: Stay hidden and watch

outcomes.text: There are three, wounded and starving, arguing in a harsh tongue. Monsters, you discover, are afraid too.
One of them turns its head. You run as never before, with heavy footsteps behind you for far too long.
The oldest of them sees you, and makes a sign: silence for silence. You never told anyone.

events.title: Alone at the Big Market
events.scene: You've been sent to sell the season's produce at the big market in town, on your own. A friendly fellow offers to buy the lot at once, at a price that seems great, with a paper for you to sign.

choices.text: Close the deal quickly

outcomes.text: The paper said something else. You come home with a third of what you should have, and a lesson.
Against all odds, he was honest. He becomes a regular customer of the family.

choices.text: Ask someone you trust to read the paper first

outcomes.text: Your reader points out the trap in the third line. You decide you need to learn to read properly.
Your reader was in on it. You only realise on the way home.

choices.text: Refuse and sell bit by bit at a stall all day

outcomes.text: You discover you can draw customers. You sell out before evening.
Half is left. You walk home slowly, eating what didn't sell.

events.title: The Missing Part
events.scene: A troupe of travelling players sets up their stage in the square. An hour before the show, one of them turns up too drunk to stand. The troupe leader looks around and points at you.

choices.text: Get up on stage

outcomes.text: You forget half the lines and invent better ones. The square gives you a standing ovation.
You don't embarrass anyone. At the end they share the hat with you.
You freeze. The square laughs kindly; it takes you a while to laugh too.

choices.text: Offer to help behind the curtain

outcomes.text: You see how every trick is done. Stage magic stops fooling you and starts fascinating you.
A whole night listening to the troupe talk about the roads. They know places your neighbours think are legends.

events.title: Sickness in the Village
events.scene: The sickness got into one house and within a week it was in ten. The healers can't cope and ask for help from anyone brave enough to go in.

choices.text: Go in and help

outcomes.text: You carry water, change cloths, and learn to tell who'll get better and who won't.
You fall sick too, and survive. The people you helped don't forget.
Someone dies holding your hand. You go back the next day anyway.

choices.text: Leave the village until it passes

outcomes.text: You come back when it's over. Some people take a while to greet you again.
You carry the news to the next village in time for them to prepare. There you're a hero; at home, someone who left.

choices.text: Seek someone who claims the favour of the gods

outcomes.text: They come, and what they do has no other explanation. The village changes faith that week.
Nobody comes, or whoever comes can do nothing. The village saves itself, more slowly.

events.title: The Price of Silence
events.scene: An outsider has discovered what your family hides and has come to collect: a sum every month, or the whole village finds out. Your parents are ready to pay for ever.

choices.text: Find the blackmailer and learn what they're hiding

outcomes.text: Everybody has a secret. Theirs guarantees silence about yours.
They laugh and double the price. Now they know your face too.

choices.text: Persuade the family to tell the truth before the blackmailer does

outcomes.text: The village listens, grumbles, and next week has something else to talk about. The blackmailer has nothing left to sell.
The village doesn't forgive so easily. The family loses friends and at least gets to sleep.

choices.text: Help pay, working on the side

outcomes.text: You work to pay for a stranger's silence, and the anger becomes fuel.
One day they simply don't come to collect. Nobody knows why, and nobody asks.

events.title: The Row and the Door
events.scene: It was the worst fight you've ever had at home. Things were said on both sides. The door is right there, the night is clear, and you're holding everything you'd need to take.

choices.text: Leave

outcomes.text: You spend weeks on the road, working for food. You come back thinner, with no apology; nobody asks for one.
Someone on the road takes you in for a while and teaches you what they know before sending you home.
You don't come back. A year later you send word, from somewhere else, that you're fine.

choices.text: Drop the bundle and stay

outcomes.text: In the morning someone makes your favourite dish, and the real conversation comes after.
Nobody mentions it again. What was said stays said.

events.title: A Name From the Songs
events.scene: You're in real trouble, the kind that ends badly, when a stranger steps in, settles it with frightening calm and asks if you're in one piece. Only afterwards does someone whisper who it was: one of those who ended the war.

choices.text: Thank them and ask how one learns to be like that

outcomes.text: They think before answering, and the answer has nothing to do with swords. You repeat it to yourself for the rest of your life.
They spend the afternoon showing you two or three things. It's enough to change what you want to be.
They say they wouldn't wish it on anyone, and seem older than the songs make them.

choices.text: Be unable to say a thing

outcomes.text: They understand, nod, and leave. You keep every detail.
Before leaving, they ask your name and repeat it aloud, like someone storing it away.

events.title: Paying What's Owed
events.scene: {debtor.name} is back. Different (cleaner, better armed, or more dangerous), remembers exactly what you did, and has come to pay. Asks what you want.

choices.text: Ask them to teach you what they know

outcomes.text: They stay a season and teach without hurry. When they leave, the debt is paid with interest.
What they know is nothing to teach a youngster. They teach it anyway.

choices.text: Ask for money for your family

outcomes.text: They leave a heavy purse on the table and go without looking back. You'd rather not know where it came from.
They pay with honest money, slowly earned, and make a point of saying where every coin came from.

choices.text: Say it isn't time to collect yet

outcomes.text: They smile, hand you a small token and tell you where to send it when the time comes.
They agree, and warn you they may not be alive when the time comes. They leave a name to look for instead.

events.title: The First Part
events.scene: It happens exactly as the old woman said, down to the detail you thought absurd. Which means the rest of what she said is coming too.

choices.text: Prepare for the rest

outcomes.text: You start training, studying, gathering what you think you'll need. Others find your hurry strange.
You begin to see signs everywhere. Some of them really are signs.

choices.text: Deliberately do the opposite of what she foretold

outcomes.text: The second part doesn't happen. Or doesn't happen yet.
It's precisely by running from it that you fulfil the second part.

choices.text: Find the old woman to learn more

outcomes.text: You find her, very ill. She tells you what she didn't before, and asks a favour in return.
She died last winter. She left something for you with a neighbour.

events.title: Hands for the Temple
events.scene: The new temple is growing and needs young people for everything: sweeping, copying, caring for those who arrive. {cleric.name} asks if you'd like to spend a season there, to see if it suits you.

choices.text: Accept the season at the temple

outcomes.text: During a dawn vigil, you feel that someone is listening back.
You hear no voice. You learn to read, to care for people and to keep silent, which is already a lot.
You see up close that the gods' servants fight for power like everyone else.

choices.text: Thank them and decline

outcomes.text: The invitation stands. The temple door becomes a place you know you can knock.
Someone else at the temple insists too much, with too many promises. You learn to distrust people who need you that badly.

choices.text: First ask why the gods were silent for three hundred years

outcomes.text: The answer is long and honest, and includes an "I don't know". You respect that more than any certainty.
The question goes down badly with those listening. The invitation cools.

events.title: In Front of Everyone
events.scene: The tax collector is taking more from an old man than the law allows, in front of everyone, and everyone is looking at the ground. The old man was once kind to you.

choices.text: Step between them

outcomes.text: Others lift their eyes, one by one. The collector does the arithmetic and backs off.
The collector's guards beat you. The old man loses what he was going to lose, and the village gains shame.
The collector backs off, smiling, and writes down your family's name.

choices.text: Wait, and help the old man later, unseen

outcomes.text: Little by little you replace part of what was taken. He knows it's you and never says.
You return to the old man exactly what the collector took, taken from the collector himself.

choices.text: Go to whoever is above the collector

outcomes.text: To everyone's amazement, it works. The collector is replaced.
They listen politely and do nothing.

culture.plains.scene: The son of an important man of the tribe is taking from an old man what isn't his, in front of everyone, and everyone is looking at the ground. The old man was once kind to you.

events.title: The Man in the Ditch
events.scene: By the side of the road lies a dead traveller, with no sign of violence. He has a full purse, a sealed letter addressed somewhere far away, and nobody else is around.

choices.text: Keep the purse and walk on

outcomes.text: Nobody ever knew. The money solves one problem and creates a memory.
Months later, someone turns up asking about a man who vanished on that road.

choices.text: Bury the man and see the letter delivered

outcomes.text: The letter arrives. Weeks later an answer comes back, with gratitude and an invitation.
On the way, curiosity wins and you read it. What it says was not meant for your eyes.

choices.text: Touch nothing and call the authorities

outcomes.text: They take care of everything. You never learned who he was.
They spend two days asking what you were doing there. The purse, you notice, disappears along the way.

events.title: The Rite
events.scene: You've reached the age when your people stop treating someone as a child, and there's a customary way to mark it. It isn't really dangerous. It isn't easy either, and everyone will know how you did.

choices.text: Do it the way it's always been done

outcomes.text: You pass, without glory and without shame. You're one of the adults now.
You do it better than anyone has in a generation. The elders talk.
You fail. You can try again next year, and it's a long year.

choices.text: Do it your own way, which nobody has tried before

outcomes.text: The elders argue all night and decide it counts. In a few years, others will copy you.
They say it doesn't count. You know what you did, and that it was harder.

events.title: The Outsiders
events.scene: A caravan of people from far away camps for a week at the edge of the village: another language, other clothes, other smells of cooking. The adults trade by day and bar the doors at night. One of them, your age, waves at you.

choices.text: Spend the week at the camp

outcomes.text: In a week you can curse, thank and haggle in their tongue.
You swap knives when you part, as they do. That, you learn later, is a serious thing.
The caravan master says there's room for another pair of hands, if you want it, when they pass back this way.

choices.text: Take the chance to sell them something of yours

outcomes.text: You sell dear something worth nothing here, and understand trade all at once.
You end up with a shiny trinket instead of something good. The trinket is pretty, at least.

choices.text: Keep away, as the adults told you

outcomes.text: The caravan leaves and takes the most interesting week of the year without you.
When the caravan leaves, something is missing from your house. The adults say they warned you.
